1yyeu0i: How do I note the illnesses and known causes of death in the family (🩺 Family health)?

It is hidden at first, because it is private: Settings → Data → “🩺 Family health” → “Show”. On the record, the “🩺 Health” block (arranged like the other blocks): “＋ Add” an illness, a disability, a cause of death or an epidemic lived through, with its date (as in a record), its source, a note and “To check”. The cause written on the death record appears there by itself, and the epidemics during the person’s lifetime (“🌍 The world around”) are noted in one click. The whole family: Lists → “🩺 Family health”. This is family memory: the app gives no advice and calculates no risk.
0fl5150: How do I see an illness across the branches of the family?

Lists → “🩺 Family health” → “🌳 By branches” tab (or the “🌳 By branches” button of the 🩺 block on the record): choose the person at the centre and the illness with the picker. The fan of ancestors colours those in whom it is noted; “The four sides” sorts these people by grandparent. Only numbers of people, never a percentage.
1e20s0u: Does family health go into my exports?

No. It is never in the website, family sharing, packages, books, simple mode, games, or when printing the record; when hidden, it does not appear in search either, and nothing shows in view-only mode 🔒. Only GEDCOM can carry it, if you tick “🩺 Include family health” when exporting. The causes written on death records remain events, exported as before.
03m4mco: How do I see the guided tour (first steps) again?

Settings → “FAQ / guide” → “▶ Restart the guided tour” (or type “tour” in the quick search). In 6 steps, the app circles the real buttons: create a record, add a parent, add a photo, add an event and its place, make a backup, find Settings and the FAQ. Click the circled button to do it for real (the tour waits until you have finished), or “Next” to just look; “Previous”, “Skip the tour”, and on the keyboard → ← Esc. A step whose button is hidden (locked record, hidden block) is skipped. The tour is offered once at first launch; it never opens in simple mode or view-only mode.
1146a46: What is the first-launch screen for (“I want to do something else”, sample database)?

The very first time an empty database is opened, under “Create and open the database”, the link “I want to do something else ▾” offers 9 uses (🌳 genealogy, 🐾 animal lineage, 🔭 counting animals, 🏠 house or village, 🎨 artist, 📚 archives, 🔤 surname, 🏭 company, ✨ memories): the app then only shows the useful tabs, without deleting anything. You can also import (Hérédis, MacFamilyTree, GEDCOM), “Start with an empty database” or “🧪 Try with a sample database”: an imaginary family (5 generations, nobody born after 1950, nobody living) kept separately in “My genealogies”, with a “🧪 Sample database” banner to go back to your genealogy. To change later: Settings → Appearance → Menus → “🧭 How you use the app” (several uses at once, “First screen on opening”, “🧭 See the first launch again”).
1b31n1l: What was the weather on the day of a birth, a marriage or a death (weather of the past)?

On the record, under the place of each event, a small “🌦” badge gives the icon and the temperature (at the hour of the record if known, otherwise in the afternoon). On hover: a sentence (“It was very cold: −6 °C in the morning…”) and the reliability; on click: the day in 4 moments (since 1940), the comparison with the 30-year normal, the station, the days around, the source. The date must be known to the day and the place must be placed on the map. Everything works without the Internet: the data is in the app (the base set) or in a pack imported once. Old weather remains an estimate: it helps you imagine the day, it does not replace the record.
1szcbip: What do “Measured”, “Station 31 km away”, “Estimated” and “Rough reconstruction” mean?

“Measured”: a station less than 15 km away (and less than 150 m difference in altitude) took readings that day. “Station … km away”: the nearest is between 15 and 40 km away, so it is indicative; rain becomes “it rained in the area”, because it changes quickly from one village to the next. “Estimated (grid cell ≈ 30 km)”: no station close enough, the value comes from the ERA5 reanalysis (1940 → today). “Rough reconstruction”: from 1836 to 1939, the 20CR reanalysis (≈ 100 km), hidden until you ask for it in the settings. Before that, or with nothing: “No known reading near here before 1863 (first station: Toulouse)”.
19fyywj: How do I compare two old maps of the same area (two periods)?

Map → “⇆ Compare” button (top bar): on the left the background you usually choose, on the right a second background (“Right”: Cassini, État-Major, IGN 1950…). “▏ Line”: drag the white line (or the ← → arrows on the keyboard); “◫ Side by side”: the two backgrounds next to each other, centred on the same spot (the points are hidden); “◐ Transparency”: the second background on top, with adjustable transparency. × closes the comparison; the choice is remembered.
00fkgkz: How do I see the provinces before 1789, the departments of 1790 or vanished communes on the map?

Map → “🏛 Borders ▾”: tick “Provinces of the Ancien Régime”, “Departments of 1790”, “Vanished or merged communes” (and, if you like, renamed communes). A click on an area or a circle gives its name, its date and, for a vanished commune, its present-day commune. The provinces and departments of 1790 are APPROXIMATE outlines drawn from today’s departments (there is no free official source of their real outlines). Vanished communes come from the official INSEE history (since 1943), to download once.
0orlwlw: Where are the old borders (vanished communes)?

They come with the app: two official INSEE files (Code officiel géographique 2026, Licence Ouverte 2.0, 5.5 MB), installed by themselves and checked by their fingerprint, without the Internet, for all your genealogies. Settings → “🏛 Old borders” shows their size, their fingerprint and their licence; “⤓ Install the old borders” puts them back if you removed them. The old names of communes also help the place picker (“formerly “…””). “🗑 Remove” takes them away, with “↶ Undo”.
0bpxe99: How do I see where a surname is concentrated, century by century?

Charts → New → Maps → “🔤 Surname map” → “From the app” tab: choose the name in the list (the most frequent first) or a person (their name is used), then “Use this data”. Coloured departments or circles per place; the ▶ slider under the drawing goes through the centuries one by one. Never a living person or a confidential record.
1u75lze: How do I see on a map the places of the ancestors I share with my DNA cousins?

Charts → New → Maps → “🧬 DNA cousins map” → “From the app”: choose the DNA test. Each match linked to a record in the tree (DNA tab) gives the calculated common ancestor and their places; colour by group or by shared cM. The names of the matches (often living) are only written if you tick the box.
0a60wws: How do I see on a map what I have already searched and what is missing?

Charts → New → Maps → “🔎 Map of your research” → “From the app”: your record indexes (registers consulted), the communes of your search sweeps and the records your ancestors are missing (“What’s missing?”). Green = all seen, orange = partly, red = gaps to cover; choose the kind of record and the period in the settings. A click on a commune: what has been seen and what is missing, with “↗ Open”.
1quklwc: How do I see a heat map decade by decade?

Charts → New → Maps → “🔥 Heat map over time” → “From the app”. The ▶ slider under the drawing (the same as for all diagrams) goes through the decades; in the settings: the decade alone or everything up to it, the same scale for all or one for each.
01s8hkw: How do I hide the weather (everywhere, for one person or for one event)?

Everywhere: Settings → Data → “🌦 Weather of the past” → “Weather on records”: Always, On hover or Never; below, the kinds of events (birth, baptism, marriage, death, burial, census…). For one person or a single event: right-click on the badge (or ⋯ in the details, or ⋯ of the “🌦 Weather of their life” block) → “🙈 Hide the weather for this event” or “… for this person”, with “↶ Undo”. Everything hidden is found in the settings, under “Hidden weather”, and shows again with a click on ×. The “Weather of their life” block can also be moved or hidden like the other blocks of the record.
0vvxuqz: Why does the altitude of a place matter for the weather?

In the mountains, a nearby station in the plain does not tell the weather higher up: the app adds 1 km of distance per 10 m of difference in altitude and never says “Measured” when the difference exceeds 150 m. Each place automatically gets the altitude from the relief map (a grid of about 1 km taken from the Copernicus DEM, supplied with the weather, for France, Belgium, Switzerland, Luxembourg, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, Germany, Portugal, the United Kingdom, Poland, Denmark, Czechia and Slovakia, islands included; outside France, Belgium, Switzerland and Luxembourg, only the altitude, no weather without the Europe pack), shown as “≈ 312 m (relief map)” in grey. To correct it: Charts → Places → the commune, “Altitude” box (in metres), or “⛰ Altitude of the place” in the details of a day; “↺ Put back the map altitude” returns to the automatic value. The day’s details give the altitude of the station and yours (“Station: Chamonix, 1,042 m — your place ≈ 1,035 m”).
1e3owj5: How do I give the time of the record for the weather?

In the event window, “Time of the event” box: write it as in the record (“at 3 o’clock in the morning”, “14:30”). Below, the app says how it understood it and converts it to world time: local solar time before 1891, Paris time until 1911, German time in the occupied zone (1940–1944), then summer time (and the rules of Belgium, Switzerland and Luxembourg). It takes the nearest value (since 1940); before 1940, only the day. The time as written does not change.
1k6e1b1: How do I install the full weather pack or the Europe pack?

The pack is built (or downloaded) once, on any computer with the Internet: step-by-step instructions in docs/METEO.md (program scripts/meteo/build-meteo.py). Then, Settings → “🌦 Weather of the past” → “⤒ Import the file…”: the “Import” window checks the .lcmeteo file, shows what will come in (stations, years, hours, size), then imports it, with “↶ Undo”. The base set stays: the pack is added on top. “🗑 Delete the pack” removes it (with “↶ Undo”). “↗ About the data” gives each source and its licence. The Europe pack adds stations in Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark, the United Kingdom, Spain, Poland and Czechia (and a few long series from Italy, Portugal and Slovakia), and, for all of Europe, the 20CR reconstruction (1836–1939) and ERA5: every place in Europe then has at least a “Rough reconstruction” before 1940. To build it, you sometimes need a free key (AEMET for Spain, CEDA for the United Kingdom): docs/METEO.md explains everything; a source without a key is simply skipped.
0kbqbfz: Where can I see the weather other than on the record?

The “🌦 Weather of their life” block on the record (to switch on in the weather settings: each big day of the life, and curious sentences such as “Born during the coldest week of the winter of 1900–1901 in Agen”); the “🌦 Weather of the past” widget on the dashboard (“100 years ago, on the day Jean and Marie married, it was raining in Auch”) and the ancestors’ badges in “🎂 Dates to celebrate”; Timeline → “🌦 Weather” in the column; the page layout → Object menu → “🌦 Weather box for an event…” (a dynamic object, with its source). Never a living person or a confidential record in the widget.
19s2die: How do I track animals (rings, microchips, GPS collars, sightings)?

Switch on the “🐾 Animal tracking” tab: Settings → Appearance → Top tabs (it is hidden at first), or “↗ Show the tab” in the list of animals. Its page is made of blocks like the dashboard: map of sightings, latest sightings, tracked animals, today’s GPS track, figures, counts at a site, animals to find, search by ring or chip, GPS import, weather, veterinary follow-up, groups. You can also put the usual dashboard widgets there (left column, “Other widgets of the app” section).
18j5a8x: How do I have a tracking page per species?

In Tracking, “＋ New page”: its name, its icon, the species and the site. The page starts from blocks suggested for this species and only shows its animals (a block can keep its own choice with ✎). The page’s ⋯ (or a right-click on its button): rename, change the icon, duplicate, page shown on opening, delete (↶ Undo).
18sb4dd: How do I put a tracking block on the dashboard?

The block’s ⋯ → “📌 Also put it on the dashboard”: it is copied with its settings to the “Overview” page. The tracking blocks are also in the dashboard column, in the “🐾 Animal tracking” section, and work even if the tab is hidden.
1v3jgta: How do I note a bird’s colour rings?

The animal’s record → “🔖 Rings and marks” block (section of the same name) → “🎨 Colour rings” → ✎: click one of the 4 positions (left or right leg, top or bottom), then one of the basic ring colours (white, black, red, orange, yellow, light green, dark green, light blue, dark blue, purple, pink, grey, brown, metal) or “Other colour” (the shared colour window: eyedropper, # code, recent colours), and the engraved code. A change keeps the old combination in the history.
0t7iknb: Which marks are offered depending on the species?

Bird: metal ring, colour rings, wing tag, GPS tag. Cat, dog: microchip, tattoo, collar, tag, GPS collar. Horse: microchip, UELN, description. Cow, sheep: ear tag, tattoo. Fish, turtle, bat: PIT, scute mark, forearm ring, transmitter. Marine animal: photo-identification (fin, fluke, scars), Argos tag, fin tag, PIT. Wild mammal: GPS or VHF collar, ear tag, ear notch, tattoo, microchip, photo-identification. Primate: photo-identification, microchip, tattoo. Everywhere: “Other mark”.
0rco2b1: I misread a ring code: how do I say so?

In “New sighting”, write “?” for a character you could not read (“7?”) and [K|X] when you are unsure (“7[K|X]”, “3[3|8]”). Or click a character: sure → not read → “I’m unsure between…”. The app looks for the matching animals, with a lower score for doubtful characters, and the sighting keeps the reading: “reading: 7[K|X] (doubt)” with the “Partial reading” badge.
1jw88r8: How do I find an animal seen outdoors?

“＋ New sighting”: for a bird, click the colours seen on the legs (“?” = colour not sure, “∅” = no ring) and the code read; for a cat, a dog, a cow, a marine animal… the number read, even partly (“250 26 9…”). The app suggests the most likely animals (colours, code, seen near here) with a percentage. Otherwise: “＋ Create the record of a new animal” or “✎ Keep without a record”. A sighting can have several photos, sounds or videos (“Photos, sounds or videos” box): you see them as small thumbnails (3, then “+N”) in lists, blocks and the map; a click shows them large, one after the other.
156ixe3: How do I import the track of a GPS tag or collar?

“⤒ Import a track…” (Tracking, the animal’s record, or the “Quick GPS import” block): GPX, KML, GeoJSON, CSV (Movebank export, Tractive, Weenect, Invoxia, Kippy collars…). Step 2: the number of points, “one every N min”, “split into nights”, the animal (suggested automatically if the tag is on its record). Afterwards “↶ Undo” removes the points.
11jmgfn: Where can I see the health of an animal in care?

The “🩺 Health” tab of its record: the timeline of states (healthy, injured, ill, in care, released, dead), the weight curve and each event (what it has, why, where, who treated it, care, medicines, weight, photos, outcome). The “🩺 Veterinary follow-up and state” block shows all the animals at a glance, with the most frequent causes of injury.
00xowra: How do I note that an animal belongs to a pack, a troop or a pod?

The “👥 Group” tab of its record: “＋ Joined a group” (the group, its role: alpha, matriarch, young, satellite… or a free word, the date). Then “Change role” or “Left the group…” (gone, excluded, dead, moved to another group). The timeline shows its whole social history; the group page shows its current and past members.
0uspuv4: Where can I see all the animals and all the sightings?

Lists → “🐾 Census” (also in the Tracking ⋯): Sightings, Tracked animals, Sites, Groups tabs; the shared bar (search, filter by species, site, year, ring reading…), List or Cards, sort. “⤓ Export ▾”: CSV, Movebank, GPX, KML or “🧾 Open in the spreadsheet”.
1lk1dp1: How do I share my animal tracking with someone?

In Tracking (⋯), the Census or an animal’s record: “📤 Share”: one record, chosen animals, a species, a site or all the tracking, with or without the GPS points and the photos. The observers’ names only go if you tick the box. The other person opens it with “⤒ Receive shared tracking…”: they see what will come in, then compare and choose for each difference (mine, theirs, both) before merging; “↶ Undo” puts everything back as before.
1dnbygq: How do I check that there are no mistakes in my database?

Settings → Data quality → “✅ Database check”: a single list of what seems impossible or very rare (born after the father’s death, married after their own death, a 57-year-old mother, 31 February, duplicates, misplaced places, impossible journeys, baptism far from the place of birth, burial before death, sex that does not match the Sosa number, “between 1900 and 1800” written backwards, a date that is too long (a note pasted into it), “-5” read as the year 5, a person married to their grandson or to their ancestor, an animal recorded as a person’s parent or spouse…). The “Merge duplicates” list shows the same duplicates, with the same number. Badges 📅 Dates, 🎂 Ages, 👪 Parents, 👥 Duplicates, 📍 Places and 🔴 🟠 🟡 with the number found; “Filter ▾” for a branch, your ancestors (Sosa) or someone’s descendants; “⤓ CSV” to work at the archives. On each line: “↗ Record” (the child and the parent), “✎ Fix” (opens the event concerned) and “This is not a mistake”. Nothing is changed without you.
13xq6bv: A check alert is wrong: how do I stop seeing it?

“This is not a mistake”: choose a reason (“I checked in the record”, “These are two different people”, “The place is right”…), add a note if you like, then “Stop reporting” (“↶ Undo” right after). It goes into the “🙈 Exceptions” badge, from where “↺ Report again” brings it back. If one of the dates concerned changes later, the alert comes back by itself, marked “Dates changed” (box ticked automatically). Two different people are no longer suggested in “Merge duplicates” either.
0fcd1j3: I am merging two records that each have their own parents: what happens?

The record you keep receives both families of parents (nothing is deleted). Before merging, “⚖️ Compare” (Settings → Merge duplicates) says so in a yellow ⚠️ box, and so does the question before the merge. Afterwards, the “✅ Database check” points out the record with two families of parents: open it and remove (“Remove”) the wrong family.
0ci1e0s: How do I go through the check alerts one by one?

In “✅ Database check”, “▶ One by one”: the alert in large, a small timeline of the dates, the family alongside. Dates are corrected on the spot (write them as in the record, Enter to save) and the alert is recalculated straight away. On the keyboard: C fix, N not a mistake, L later, ← → previous / next, Esc to go back to the list.
0xj8gfv: Can I change the age from which a mother is flagged as “too old”?

Yes: Settings → “⚙️ Check thresholds”: age of the mother and of the father (to check 🟠 / impossible 🔴), young marriage, longevity, delay after the father’s death, gap between two births, distant baptism, likeness of duplicates… Each slider is saved straight away (“↶ Undo” in the message), double-click = starting value, “↺ Reset to default” at the top. You also choose the record banner there: always, only 🔴 or never.
0olqduk: What does “⚠️ 2 things to check” at the top of a record mean?

It is the database check banner: what seems impossible for this person (“Married on 17 April 1863, after his death”, “His daughter Louise is born 4 years after his death”). It is folded: “See ▾” unfolds it, with “✎ Fix” and “Not a mistake”. An alert set aside does not come back there. The “✅ Database check” widget on the dashboard gives the number by kind and the % of records without an alert.
1fy6bw9: Why are shortcuts not written the same on a Mac and on a PC?

Shortcuts are written for your computer: the Command key on a Mac, Ctrl on Windows and Linux, as small grey keys, the same everywhere (tooltips, menus, texts and Settings → Keyboard shortcuts). Leave the mouse on a button for a moment: a black tooltip says what it is for, with its key.
0s179ce: What is in the “⋯” menu and under the right-click?

The same small action menu everywhere: Open, Edit, Rename, Duplicate, Export… and Delete in red at the very bottom. A right-click on a list row, a thumbnail or an object in an editor (Cut, Copy, Paste, Bring to front…, with their keys) opens this same menu, where the mouse is. Shift + right-click: the browser’s usual menu.
0balzpt: How do I print a record, a booklet or a list?

“🖨 Print” (or ⌘P) always opens the same window: the preview of the page, the size (A4, A5), Portrait or Landscape, what is printed (photos…), then “🖨 Print”. “⤓ PDF” makes a PDF file: in the print window, choose “Save as PDF”. Only the content of the screen is printed, without the menus.
10otw27: How do I print a presentation, a folded booklet, a slideshow or a single page?

Everywhere, “🖨 Print” (or ⌘P in an editor, or “⤓ Export ▾ → 🖨 Print”) opens the same window, without a new tab. At the top: A4, A5 or ✎ Other, Portrait or Landscape. In the blue “What gets printed” area, the tool’s choices: slides with or without notes and how many per page, entries or table of the catalogue, one photo per page or a contact sheet, image and text of a transcription, bleed and crop marks of a page layout… Then “Pages”: All, The one shown, or Choose (“1-3, 7, 10-12”) and the number of copies. The preview on the right changes with each choice; ‹ › to see the other pages. The size and your choices are remembered for next time, tool by tool.
1buz65b: How do I import my tree from Gramps?

In Gramps: Family Trees → Export, choose “Gramps XML Package (family tree and media)”: you get a .gpkg file that contains the tree and its photos (a plain .gramps file works too, but without the photos). Then Settings → Import → “⤒ Import a tree…”: the window shows what will come in (people, families, places, sources, media, witnesses), then “⤒ Import”. Everything is taken over: multiple names (married name, nicknames), events with their witnesses, godfathers and godmothers, places with their hierarchy and coordinates, sources, citations and repositories, notes, labels (with their colour), attributes. Only the photos stored in the package are copied: a path that would point outside the package is refused. Right after, “↶ Undo” removes everything.
1yze8zk: How do I import a tree from Ancestry or MyHeritage?

Export the tree as GEDCOM on the site (Ancestry: Trees → Tree Settings → Export Tree; MyHeritage: Family Tree → Export to GEDCOM), then Settings → Import → “⤒ Import a tree…”. The app recognises the site: married names, main photo, labels, links to the site’s records and documents (kept in the citations), dates written in English (“Abt. 1850”, “Bet. 1850 and 1855”). Photos that stayed on the site are never downloaded: their addresses are kept in an “🔗 Online media” note on the record. To add this tree to a database that is already filled without duplicates, use Settings → “Merge a tree” instead.
19wgpo5: How do I import my tree from RootsMagic, Family Tree Maker or Généatique?

RootsMagic: Settings → Import → “⤒ Import a tree…” and choose your .rmtree (or .rmgc) file directly: it is read without being changed (people, names, families, adoptions, events, places and localities with coordinates, sources, citations, media, notes, witnesses). Family Tree Maker encrypts its .ftm files: no other software can open them; in FTM do “File → Export → GEDCOM”, then import the .ged (military service, adoptions _FREL / _MREL, main photo are understood). Généatique: its own file format is not documented; export a GEDCOM (File → Export): ANSI, ANSEL or UTF-8, places with locality and INSEE code, godfathers, godmothers and witnesses are taken over. For a cousin’s tree, “Merge a tree” also accepts the .rmtree.
071izf6: How do I import a GeneWeb file (.gw)?

In GeneWeb, export the database as a .gw text file (the “gwu” command, or Geneanet’s .gw export). Then Settings → Import → “⤒ Import a tree…” and choose the .gw file: the window shows what will come in (people, families, events). Taken over: families and children, births, baptisms, deaths (also “killed”, “died young”), burials, events from the pevt and fevt blocks, witnesses, godparents, adoptions, notes, sources, titles, GeneWeb dates (about, before, after, between, Julian and Republican calendars). An unreadable block is skipped and reported. Right after, “↶ Undo” removes everything. A .gwb database (GeneWeb’s folder) cannot be read: you need the .gw.
0j11i9z: How do I import a GEDCOM-X file (FamilySearch)?

Settings → Import → “⤒ Import a tree…” and choose the GEDCOM-X file, in JSON (.json) or XML (.xml). People, other names, couples, parent-child links (with adoption), dated and placed facts, places with coordinates, sources and pages, notes, FamilySearch and Wikidata identifiers are taken over. The GEDCOM-X exported by the app reads back without any notable loss.
0ox7v5d: How do I import from Legacy, Family Historian, Ancestral Quest, Reunion, Ancestris, webtrees, Brother’s Keeper, PAF, WikiTree, Geni or GenoPro?

Export a GEDCOM from that software or site, then Settings → Import → “⤒ Import a tree…”. The app recognises the software and keeps its special features: private records (_PRIV) → confidential, Legacy tags (_TAG) and Family Historian flags (_FLGS) → labels, webtrees “to do” → note, Wikidata identifier → record, adoptions (_FREL, _MREL), accents of old Mac or DOS files; other data specific to the software goes into a “Data specific to …” note. GenoPro’s .gno file is not read (no reliable public description): go through its GEDCOM export.
1mxksxg: How do I export my tree WITH the photos (GedZip, Gramps package)?

Settings → Export → “⤓ To other software and sites” → “📦 GedZip with the photos” (GEDCOM 7 + media folder in a .gdz) or “🌳 Gramps package with the photos” (.gpkg). The window first gives the size and the number of files. With “For sharing”, living people and confidential records are hidden, and a photo showing one of these people is not put in the package. Both packages can be reopened here with “⤒ Import a tree”.
0yv79sa: What is a record’s Wikidata identifier for?

For a well-known person (artist, mayor, scientist…), the Wikidata “Q…” number is noted in the “External references” block (✎). It gives a ↗ link to their page, and the “🌐 Complete from Wikidata” button: only when you click, the app reads the Wikidata entry on the Internet and shows you what is missing in your database (birth, death with the place, sex, occupation, a note with the description and the Wikipedia links). Nothing is replaced; you tick what you keep, and “↶ Undo” removes everything right after. The identifier also goes into GEDCOM and GEDCOM-X exports.
0kt2a9n: How do I put my tree on Geneanet?

Settings → Export → “⤓ To other software and sites” → “🌐 For Geneanet”: a GEDCOM ready for Geneanet (UTF-8, places in the format “[Locality] - Commune, INSEE code, department, region, country”). Living people and confidential records are always hidden: anonymous (“Living person”, to keep the links between branches) or removed, as you choose. Geneanet does not receive the photos: only those with an online address go, as a link. Then on Geneanet: My tree → Import a GEDCOM file.
075hs4w: How do I move my tree into Gramps, or send it as GEDCOM-X (FamilySearch)?

Settings → Export → “⤓ To other software and sites”: “🌳 To Gramps” makes a .gramps file (in Gramps: Family Trees → Import) with places arranged by country, region, department, commune; “🔗 GEDCOM-X” makes FamilySearch’s JSON. Tick “For sharing” to hide living people and confidential records. The photos are not in these files, only their names.
1x2x8g1: How do I put the family’s birthdays and name days in my calendar?

Settings → Export → “📅 Birthday calendar” (or Family calendar → ⤓ Export the birthdays): choose your ancestors (Sosa), the whole database or a branch, only the living or everyone, and births, marriages, deaths and 🎉 name days. The .ics file opens in Apple, Google or Outlook; each date comes back every year (a 29 February: the last day of February). Approximate dates (about, before…) are left aside and counted. Confidential records are never in it.
0q4ta3c: How do I put my cousins and the archive services in my phone’s contacts?

Settings → Export → “📇 Contacts” (or Lists → Directory of the living → ⤓ Export ▾): a vCard file (.vcf) with the addresses, e-mails and phone numbers you noted: directory of the living, archive services, DNA cousins, correspondents in the letter register. Open it on your phone or your computer.
0fotih2: How do I see my family’s places in Google Earth?

Settings → Export → “🗺 Places (KML)” (or Lists → Places → ⤓ Export ▾): a .kml file with one folder per kind of event (Birth, Marriage, Death…) and one marker per place. “🗺 Places (GeoJSON)” does the same for QGIS, uMap… Places without coordinates are left aside; the events of hidden living people are not included.
1ukn0is: How do I import my genealogy society’s transcriptions (Nimègue)?

Settings → Import → “📜 A society’s transcriptions (Nimègue…)”, or Lists → Record indexes → “⤒ Import transcriptions”. A Nimègue file (v2 or v3, with or without a header line, even in an old Windows encoding) or a society’s CSV, Excel or LibreOffice table: the columns are recognised automatically (date, surname, first name, father, mother, godfather, witnesses, shelfmark, image…) and you can correct them in the preview. Each record becomes a line in the record index of its commune, with its people and their role (child, spouse, deceased, father, godmother…). Tick “Create or link the records”: for each person who looks like a record in your database, the app asks “is this the same person?” — nothing is linked or created without your choice, a person mentioned in several records gives only one record, and an existing record is never changed. A record already imported is pointed out. Right after, “↶ Undo” removes everything.
098xijp: How do I import my family from an Excel or LibreOffice spreadsheet?

Settings → Import → “👥 Table of people”. One row per person: first name, surname, sex, dates (written as in a record: “7 May 1925”, “about 1784”, “08/12/1960”), places, occupation, note, and the father, mother and spouse links by row number, by name (“Pierre MARTIN”) or by Sosa number (2 and 3 are the parents of 1…). The preview shows the records, couples and children that will come in, and the links that could not be made (a name used by two rows, unknown number). If a person may already be in your database, you choose: the same record, or create one. “↶ Undo” removes everything right after. Cells that contain a spreadsheet formula are never taken over.
0x2e3zj: How do I exchange my sources with Zotero, EndNote or JabRef (RIS, BibTeX)?

To bring references in: Settings → Import → “📚 References (RIS, BibTeX)” — each one becomes a source in your database, ready to cite (title, authors, publisher or archive service, date, address, shelfmark, notes; accents understood, even written the LaTeX way). A source already there is not taken again. To send them out: Settings → Export → “⤓ Sources (RIS, BibTeX)”. The exported file reads back without loss. The Research workshop has its own .bib and .ris buttons, which also keep the archive collection, the shelfmark and the notes.
1y95vgb: How do I fill in the coordinates of my places from Google Earth or a GeoJSON file?

Lists → Places → “⤒ Import coordinates (KML, GeoJSON)”, or Settings → Import → “📍 Place coordinates”. Each point in the file (KML, KMZ or GeoJSON) is matched with a place in your database by its name, and the department settles namesakes. Line by line, you tick: add the coordinates to a place that has none, replace those of a place (unticked at first), choose between several places with the same name, or create the place. The KML and GeoJSON files exported by the app read back without loss. “↶ Undo” puts everything back as before.
0f589r1: How do I open my genealogy in Obsidian (linked Markdown notes)?

Settings → Export → “⤓ To other software and sites” → “🗒 For Obsidian”: a .zip file to unzip, then “Open folder as vault” in Obsidian. One note per person (identity, events, sources, notes) and one per place, linked by [[…]] links to the parents, children, spouses and places; the “Genealogy” note lists them all. You choose the whole database, your Sosa ancestors or a branch. Living people and confidential records stay hidden (“Living person”) or removed.
1n42vpi: How do I see my family network in Gephi, yEd or Graphviz?

Settings → Export → “🕸 Network (GraphML)” for Gephi and yEd, or “🕸 Network (Graphviz)” for a .dot file (dot -Tsvg reseau.dot -o reseau.svg turns it into a drawing). Each person is a point with their name, sex, years, generation and Sosa number; each parent-child link and each couple is a line. Tick “one point per family” to put the couple between the parents and the children. Same privacy rules as the other exports.
14u2pg5: How do I send my DNA segments to DNA Painter, or import DNA Painter, Genetic Affairs and LivingDNA?

“🧬 DNA” tab → 🧩 Chromosomes → “⤓ Export for DNA Painter”: a CSV file (the format of FamilyTreeDNA’s chromosome browser, which DNA Painter reads in “Paint a new match”). To import: “⤒ Import (CSV)” also recognises the export of a DNA Painter profile (segments, side, group, colour), Genetic Affairs’ AutoCluster and AutoTree files (each cluster becomes a group, the grid gives the shared matches, AutoTree gives the common ancestor) and LivingDNA’s list of matches. A raw DNA file is never imported.
07r8w8l: How do I import my photos from Google Photos or Apple Photos with their date and place?

Lists → Media and documents → “⤒ Import photos”. Google Photos: the .zip archive from Google Takeout (1 GB at most; beyond that, unzip it and choose the photos with their .json files). Apple Photos: File → Export, with “Title, Keywords, and Caption” and “Location Information” (or with the .xmp files). The app takes over the date the photo was taken, the description, keywords and albums (as labels) and the GPS position. Places and named people are only suggested: tick “Link” for each one after checking. Everything is read on your computer, nothing is sent to the Internet. HEIC photos are left aside (export them as JPEG). “↶ Undo” removes everything that has just come in.
12o913j: Which DNA files can I import?

“🧬 DNA” tab → Matches (or Chromosomes) → “⤒ Import (CSV)”: the lists of matches and segments exported by Ancestry (with DNAGedcom), MyHeritage, 23andMe, FamilyTreeDNA and GEDmatch. The company and the columns (cM, segments, longest segment, relationship, side, common ancestors, link to the profile or tree…) are recognised automatically; you can correct them in “Recognised columns”. “↶ Undo” right after puts everything back as before. A raw DNA file (your SNPs, the “raw data” file) is always refused: out of caution for your privacy and your family’s, and because in France a genetic test outside a medical or research setting is forbidden.
0rl05j6: How do I import a file (GEDCOM, CSV table, setting, list…)?

All the “⤒ Import…” buttons open the same 3-step window: 1. drag the file (or paste it, or choose it); 2. you see what will come in (“12 people”, “34 rows”, the name of the setting…); 3. “⤒ Import”. When possible, the message that follows offers “↶ Undo”.
1rwctq2: Can the tab menu go at the bottom, or the column on the right?
Yes: Settings → Appearance → “Tab menu” (top or bottom) and “Side column” (left or right), then Save.
05oogmk: What do the colours of the badges (In progress, Done, Sosa…) mean?

Everywhere in the app, the same colour means the same thing: blue = in progress, green = done or certain, yellow = to check, red = problem, grey = closed or archived, black = death. The Sosa number is always solid blue, on the record as in the picker. The record’s colours can still be set in Settings → Appearance → “Badge colours”.
0peodyk: Why does the date show “today at 10:22” or “Tuesday”?

The dates when something was created or edited are all written the same way: “today at…”, “yesterday at…”, the day of the week if it was less than 7 days ago, then “17 Oct 2026”. Hover over it to see the full date. The dates of your genealogy (births, records…) do not change.
0xchhim: Something is missing in a window: where is the error?

Just under the field to correct: it has a red frame, with the sentence that says what to do (“Give the widget a title.”), and the cursor is already there. If there are several things to correct, the window says so at the top (“2 things to fix before saving”). The window stays open: nothing you wrote is lost, and the red goes away as soon as you correct it. The message at the bottom left is now only used when saving itself fails.
1d4fzce: Why do all the windows have the same size and the same bottom?

There are only 4 sizes: small for a question or a choice, medium for a form, large when there are two columns or a preview, very large for galleries of images and templates; editors (drawing, page layout, editing…) take the whole screen. The bottom of the window always stays visible when you scroll: “Delete” on the left, “Cancel” then the main button on the right; a window that only shows something has “Close”.
0lw7zp6: Why do the buttons say “Create the book”, “Link” or “↺ Reset to default”?

Everywhere, the same action has the same word and the same symbol. “Create the …” makes something new, “Save” keeps something that exists, “Add” puts one thing into another, “🔗 Link” attaches two records, “↺ Reset to default” returns to the starting settings, and a window that only shows something has “Close” alone. The symbols: ⤒ import, ⤓ export or download, 💾 save, 🖨 print, ✎ edit, 🗑 delete, ↗ open, ⚙️ settings, 🔍 search, ＋ add or new, 📋 copy, ⧉ duplicate, ⭐ favourite, 📁 file, × close.
1ipml9u: A block or a list is empty: how do I start?

When there is nothing, the app always says so the same way: a large box for an empty page or list, a small line in a block (“📚 No sources”). Next to it, the button to start (“＋ Add…”) does the same thing as the usual button.
1l9bxne: How do I add a child, a parent or a spouse?
Open the record, then in the Parents, Spouses or Children blocks click “＋”. You can choose a person who already exists or create a new one.
14jig6r: How do I show a block (Departures, WWI soldier, Resistance member…) on a record?
Record → Identity (pencil) → “Blocks to show on the record”: tick the block. To have it on all records: Settings → Appearance → “Blocks shown on request”.
0hsu91h: How do I create my own dashboard widget?

Settings → Widget editor (or “＋ Create a widget” at the bottom of the dashboard column) → “＋ New widget”. Start from scratch (figures, list, chart, statistic, app screen, text, shortcuts), from any element of the app (a list, a diagram, a statistic, a record, the map, a tool), from an app widget (an editable copy, or the same widget dressed with your title, icon and colour), from one of your widgets or from an example. The preview updates while you adjust it. It then appears in the left column of the dashboard; “Share” turns it into a file for someone close to you.
19yn2ku: How do I arrange the dashboard into pages and groups?

Dashboard → “Reorder the widgets”. “＋ New page” adds a page (List, Cards, Search…): its buttons appear at the top, under the title; tick the one that opens by default, and “Arrange its widgets” to organise it (widgets added from the left column go onto the page shown). “＋ Group” creates a frame with a title that gathers the widgets that follow it; ▶ makes it a sub-group, with as many levels as you like. The ▾ button to the left of the frame folds or opens the group.
0f64upo: How do I move a row with the mouse?
Wherever there are ↑ ↓ arrows, the ⠿ (or ↕) handle in front of the row can be dragged to the place you want.
0lz1uey: How do I create my own block?

Settings → Block editor → “＋ New block”. Start from a template, an app block (Departures, WWI soldier, Resistance member, Grave…) or one of your blocks, add or remove fields by clicking the buttons, then save. It then appears in Identity → “Blocks to show on the record”. The “📊 Chart” field places a chart fully set up in the Chart editor (“New chart…”, then back to the block); with the criterion “Relative to the person on the record”, it counts their ancestors, descendants, family… The “🧱 Widget” field places one of your widgets (figures, list, chart…) or an app screen (the person’s record, a list, a diagram…).
183h8hi: How do I add a label?
In almost every form, the “🏷️ Labels” line: click “＋”, type the beginning of the name or create a new label. The list of all labels is in Lists → Labels.
1j3fspr: How do I spot a generation mistake (a father confused with his son of the same name)?

Settings → ✅ Database check (🎂 Ages badge): besides ages at marriage and parents who are too young or too old, a set of siblings spread over two generations, a Sosa ancestor too young or too old for their place in the line, a death before birth or a marriage after death.
0dlyj4c: How do I protect a record against changes?
The padlock at the top of the record locks it: nothing can be changed there any more, not even by working together.
1rvo3kd: Who is the root person (de cujus), and why do they have Sosa number 1?

The root person (de cujus) is the starting person of the tree: they are Sosa number 1, their father 2, their mother 3, and so on. Go menu → “Root person” (⌘⇧H or Ctrl+Shift+H) opens their record. To change: Settings → Appearance → Sosa numbering, look for the person then “Recalculate”; the choice is saved in the database, so it follows the backup and another computer.
0tnentb: How do I make a widget of shortcuts to anything?

Settings → Widget editor → “＋ New widget” → 🔗 Shortcuts, then “＋ Add shortcuts…”. Three tabs: 🔎 In your database (a person, a place, a Note, an investigation, a search sweep, a Workshop project, a table, a book, a media item, a diagram, a chart, a house, a map, a transcription, a work, a magazine, an employer, a source, a label… with the filters “All (n)”, “👤 People (n)”), 🧭 Screens and tools (screens, your own tabs, lists, tools such as photo retouching or video editing, actions such as “＋ New person” or the backup, tool projects) and 🌐 Website. You can put as many as you like in the same widget, rename them, give them an icon, a colour, show the person’s photo or the media image, add subheadings, arrange them (⠿ or ↑ ↓) and choose tiles, list or small buttons, the size and the number of columns. The widget goes on the dashboard, in your tabs and in a Note; make several if you like.
1l35nmx: How do I change my shortcuts directly on the dashboard?

Click the ✎ pencil of the shortcuts widget (on the dashboard, in one of your tabs or in a Note), then “✎ Edit the shortcuts”: “＋ Add shortcuts…” to put in what you want, ⠿ or ↑ ↓ to put them in the order you want, rename them, change their icon, remove them (↶ Undo), choose the layout, then “Save”: the widget redraws straight away. No need to go through Settings.
17i80aa: How do I quickly add a record or a list to my shortcuts?

The ⭐ button (Add to shortcuts), at the far top right of a person’s record, a list, a Note, an investigation or Charts: choose which shortcuts widget to put it in (or create a new one, placed on the dashboard). For a list, the current search, filters and sorting are kept: the shortcut reopens the list just as it was. If the target has been deleted, its tile turns grey “not found” with a “Remove” button (↶ Undo possible).
01sq966: How do I make a shortcut that creates a new house, a new video edit, a new book…?

Click the ✎ pencil of the shortcuts widget (or Settings → Widget editor) → “＋ Add shortcuts” → “＋ Create…” tab (the same section is also at the top of “🧭 Screens and tools”): one shortcut per editing tool (🏠 New house, 🎬 New video edit, 📐 New book, 🎚️ New photo retouch, ✒️ New drawing, 📰 New announcement, 🎞️ New presentation or slideshow, 📜 New transcription, 🎧 New sound project…). A click on the shortcut opens the tool directly on a new item (an empty document, or the tool’s assistant).
0dy0320: How do I change the order of the search types, or hide some?

Research → “Reorder” (at the bottom of the left column): drag a row or use ↑ ↓, and click the eye to hide or show a type. It is saved straight away (“↶ Undo” in the message at the bottom left); “↺ Reset to default” puts back the starting order. A hidden type that another tool opens (a record index, the log…) stays in the menu, marked “(hidden)”.
1viq0w0: Is the order of the map backgrounds the same everywhere?

Yes. The order chosen in Settings → Maps and map backgrounds → “Map backgrounds” (categories and backgrounds) is followed by all the background menus: the Map, photo maps, the slideshow, drawn maps, a village’s page (“Map backgrounds as buttons”) and the address plan. An unticked background no longer appears there (unless it is the current one).
105hfod: How do I create my own tab in the top bar?

Settings → Tab editor → “＋ New tab”. Start from an empty composed page, an app screen, a copy of the dashboard, one of your tabs or a template (My research desk, My village, Tree and map…). In the page, place whatever you want: any app screen (a list, a diagram, a statistic, a person’s record, the map, one of your lists, a Settings tool), with its height and its menus if you like, widgets, your charts, free texts. “↗ Full size” opens the screen. A tab can also be a simple shortcut to a screen. Choose its name and icon; arrange or hide it in Settings → Appearance → “Order of the main menu”, with the other tabs; “Share” turns it into a file.
1g7p5y4: How do I see who is hidden behind a bar in a statistic?
Click the bar, the column, the slice or the legend line: a window shows the people counted, with a search, sorting by name or by birth and a CSV export. “others” also shows the grouped values.
0bfe2h0: “others” gathers all the small values: it no longer sets the chart’s scale (otherwise the real values would have almost no colour left). Its stripes say that it goes beyond the scale.
1u8l81p: How do I save a chart (or a statistic) as an image?
Charts → My charts → the chart: “PNG image” (sharp, for a forum) or “JPG image” (lighter, for an e-mail), “CSV” for a spreadsheet, “Print / PDF”.
0r7jjgw: Where do I keep my DNA results?

The “🧬 DNA” tab, hidden at first: Settings → Appearance → menu order, tick “DNA”. Be careful: in France, taking a genealogical DNA test is forbidden outside a medical or research setting (Civil Code art. 16-10, Penal Code art. 226-28-1: a €3,750 fine); the warning and the links to the official texts are in “⚖️ Law and warnings”. The tab stores tests, haplogroups, matches (CSV import), groups (Leeds method), segments (chromosome browser), offers a cM calculator and shows the Y, mt and X lines of the tree. Everything can be set in “⚙️ Settings”.
1xx8sf9: How do I draw a coat of arms, a logo, or redo an image as vectors?

Lists → Editing tools → “✒️ Vector drawing” (or “🛡️ New coat of arms”), the ✒️ button of a record’s coat of arms, or Settings → Boards → Shapes (✒️ on a shape). Illustrator-style tools: pen, pencil, shapes, text, direct selection of points, layers, groups, masks, Pathfinder, gradients. “Coat of arms” tab: shield, partition, charge, tinctures, charges and automatic blazon. Coat of arms → “Vectorise an image” turns a scanned coat of arms into paths. SVG, PNG, JPG, WEBP, GIF, BMP import; SVG, PNG, JPG, WEBP, PDF export; save to “My shapes”, to a record’s media or as a coat-of-arms image.
098nijt: How do I draw the plan of a family house, in 2D and 3D?

Lists → “🏠 Family houses” (or Editing tools → House plan). ⬚ Drag a room: its walls are made automatically and its area is shown; ▬ draws walls by clicking (snapped to the grid, the corners, right angles); 🚪 and 🪟 one click on a wall. Furniture: more than 450 objects (box bed, kneading trough, spinning wheel, stove, longcase clock…), or your own: ⤒ Import an image seen from above, or a 3D file (OBJ with MTL, STL, glTF, GLB). Materials for walls (stone, brick, half-timbering, panelling, wallpaper…) and floors (terracotta tiles, parquet, flagstones…), floors, roof, a scanned plan to trace (scaled in two clicks), and the “3D view” where you turn around and visit. The house is linked to a place, its inhabitants and its censuses, can have several periods (1850, 1900…); each room keeps its memories.
17wob2e: How do I place a chart in a Note, an investigation, the Workshop or a person’s record?

Wherever you place a diagram (📊 block of a Note, “＋ Diagram” of an investigation, of a Workshop project, Diagrams block of a person, dashboard), the window offers: ＋ New diagram, 📊 From a chart (one of yours, an example or an app statistic, drawn with the type of your choice and kept up to date), 📈 One of my charts (a chart from the Chart editor, placed as it is and kept up to date; you choose it in the usual search menu, with its thumbnail, its drawing, where its figures come from and the number of places where it is already placed) and ⤒ Import (a diagram or chart shared as a file, a CSV, a pasted table, a Wikipedia page, an image of a chart). “＋ Create a new chart” leads to the Chart editor.
0zxla12: Where do I create my own chart or diagram?

Everything is done in Settings → Chart editor (formerly called “Statistics editor”): “＋ New chart” (with your own figures or the app’s) and “＋ New diagram” (hemicycle, timeline of a group, organisation chart…). All your charts and diagrams are gathered in Lists → “Charts and diagrams”, as a list or as cards with their thumbnail, where you can search, filter, sort and create others. Charts → “My diagrams” and “My charts” also show them in large. Your charts are stored in your genealogy: they follow the backup and another computer, and can be found in the quick search (⌘K).
1282ch0: How do I sort My diagrams and My charts into folders?

In Charts, left column: “＋ 📁 Folder” to the right of “My diagrams” or “My charts”. A click on a folder opens or closes it (▸ / ▾), and the app remembers; the number on the right says how many items are inside, sub-folders included. On hover: ✎ to rename it, 🗑 to delete it (nothing is lost: what it contains moves up one level). To file a diagram, drag it onto a folder (it lights up in blue) or out of the folders to take it out; drag a folder onto another to make it a sub-folder, or between two folders to change the order (three levels at most). You would rather not drag, or it is one of My charts? Open it and click “📁 File”. After each filing, “↶ Undo” undoes it. The numbers D1, D2… and M1, M2… do not change.
0rpfmam: Where are my charts stored, and how do I find one again?

Your charts (made in Settings → Chart editor, formerly “Statistics editor”) are stored in your genealogy, like your records: they follow the full backup, restoration and another computer. Those that were kept in your browser moved there by themselves, once only, without losing anything. To find one: type a few letters of its name in the search menu (“📈 One of my charts”), in the quick search (⌘K or Ctrl+K) or in Lists → “Charts and diagrams”. Each row shows its thumbnail, its drawing (bars, pie…), where its figures come from and in how many places it is placed.
17a5liy: How do I make a chart with my own figures (not those of the tree)?

Settings → Chart editor → “＋ New chart” → “✍️ My own figures” (or, in “2. Chart”, Data → “✍️ My own figures”). A table appears: one row per value (the name, then the figures), “＋ Row”, “＋ Series” for several columns of figures (e.g. 1900 and 1950). You can paste cells from a spreadsheet into a box, “📋 Paste a table” (the first row of headings gives the names of the series), “⤒ Import a CSV”, or “📊 Start from a chart” to copy figures (from one of your charts or an app statistic) and adjust them. With several series, choose a drawing from “My diagrams” (columns, line, stacked, radar…) to see them all.
01yuu6d: How do I place one of my charts everywhere (record, investigation, page layout…) and keep it up to date?

A chart saved in the Chart editor has a name and can be placed everywhere: as a widget on its own or with other parts on the dashboard, and wherever there is “＋ Diagram” (block of a Note, investigation, Workshop project, page layout, table) → “📈 One of my charts” (the usual search menu: type a few letters of the name). For a person’s page or an investigation, you can also do it from the chart editor: “📌 Also place it on…”. When you change the chart (figures, drawing, colours, name), it changes everywhere it is placed; “✎ Edit” on the placed chart reopens the Chart editor.
0w51up5: Can my charts use the timelines, slices and links of the diagrams?

Yes. In the Chart editor, “Drawing” offers the simple drawings, then all the types of My diagrams: slices (pie, ring, mosaic, gauges, pictograms…), figures (columns, line, radar, pyramid, heat map…), assemblies (hemicycle…), links (word cloud) and, with a list of people, the lives timeline, the chronological timeline and the migration flow (place of birth → place of death). The types are the same on both sides: ⚙️ in the diagram gallery (Charts → My diagrams → ＋ New) (or ⚙️ Arrange the types in the gallery) for their order, to hide those you do not use and to make your own groups.
0xsdry8: Which diagrams for my genealogy (fan, sunburst, network, arcs, Venn)?

In “＋ New diagram”, the “Genealogy” group offers: 🪭 the ancestry fan (half circle, three quarters or full circle, from 3 to 10 generations) where each box is coloured according to a figure or a category — research rate, region, department, occupation, century, name…; 🌞 the lineage sunburst (rings from the centre outwards, each slice sized by its figure, for example the number of descendants); 🕸 the network of relationships (witnesses, godfathers, godmothers, neighbours…: the points spread out by themselves, you can drag them, zoom with ＋ − or Ctrl + wheel, ↺ to reset to default, double-click to free a point); 🌈 the link arcs (people on a line, joined by arcs: pedigree collapse, marriages between families); ⭕ the Venn diagram of 2 to 4 sets. Each one is filled in by hand, by pasting a table, with a CSV, or through the “From the app” tab (your Sosa ancestors, a line of descendants, the witnesses of records, your labels, profiles and name groups), then adjusted, exported and placed everywhere like the others.
07s71c0: How do I see the seasons and the long timespan of my family (calendar, month rose, spiral)?

In “＋ New diagram”, “Timelines” group: 🗓 the coloured calendar (each day is a box that is darker or lighter depending on the number of events; all years together to see the season, or one row per year), 🌸 the month rose (12 slices, one per month, with several series: births, marriages, deaths…) and 🌀 the time spiral (one turn per century or per decade; a date = a point, a start and an end = a line, like a life). Dates are written as in a record: “7 May 1925”, “08/12/1960”, “12 Thermidor Year II”. The “From the app” tab takes the births, baptisms, marriages, deaths and burials of your whole database or of a person’s ancestors.
03hy5ov: Which diagrams can tell my family’s story (who knew whom, survival, occupations, marriages, pedigree collapse, births, places lived)?

In “＋ New diagram”: 🤝 Who knew whom (Timelines) — the lives of several generations one under another; the app tells who knew whom, for example “your great-grandmother knew her great-grandson for 6 years”, and colours in yellow the years when the most generations were alive together; 📉 Survival curve (Figures) — the share still alive at each age, one curve per century, per sex or per branch, with the age at which half are still alive (living people count up to their age today); 🔀 Occupations from father to son (Genealogy) — bands that follow occupations over 3 to 5 generations, in green if the occupation is kept; 💍 Marriage radius (Genealogy) — one point per couple, at the distance between the two spouses’ places of birth, with one circle per century and a small table; 🧮 Pedigree collapse (Genealogy) — per generation, the possible ancestors (2, 4, 8…), the places found and the different people; 📅 Months of marriages and conceptions (Timelines) — Lent and Advent marked, conceptions = birth minus 9 months; 👶 Birth spacing (Timelines) — one row per mother, her children at the age she was, the gap in months and the children who died young; 🏘️ Timeline of places lived (Timelines) — one band per person, coloured by commune, department or country. The “From the app” tab fills them with your database (the starting person is chosen in the usual search menu); a click on a bar, a point or a month opens the record or the list of the people concerned. The occupation comes from the record or the first “Occupation” event; the marriage radius needs the coordinates of the places.
05714l3: How do I colour a map according to my figures (departments, regions, countries)?

In “＋ New diagram”, “Maps” group: 🗺️ the map coloured by area. In Settings, choose the map (France, Belgium, Switzerland, Luxembourg, Europe, World) and its level of detail (departments, regions or communes; provinces; cantons; countries or NUTS 1 and 2 regions; countries or continents). In Data, one row per area: its name or its code (35, 2A, FRH03, VD, BE…) and its figure; you can paste a table or import a CSV, and rows that are not found are flagged under the map. “From the app” counts your births, marriages or deaths (or only those of your ancestors, over a period): each place in your database is attached to its area according to its coordinates. Gradient or class colours, labels, legend; the value shows on hover. The overseas territories are in insets.
0nd1mqf: How do I choose the part of the world a map shows?

In the preview of a map: the wheel zooms, dragging moves, Shift + drag (or “▭ Draw a frame”) frames an area, “↺ Reset to default” goes back to the starting frame. This framing is saved with the diagram. In Settings, “Part of the map” also offers ready-made frames (Western Europe, Mediterranean, North America, North Africa, Indian Ocean, Caribbean, Quebec and Acadia… or, for France, Brittany-Normandy, South-West, Corsica…) and “Projection” the drawing of the globe (Equal Earth or Robinson for the world, Lambert for Europe).
0cigboh: How do I draw my family’s migrations on a map?

In “＋ New diagram”, “Maps” group: 🧭 the migration map. Each row is a flow “departure → arrival → how many”; the arrow is thicker when there are more people. “From the app” takes from your database the place of birth → place of death, birth → marriage, or from one generation to the next (parent’s birth → child’s birth), possibly for your ancestors only. “Add a flow” lets you choose the two places with the place search menu; a place without a position is chosen in “The places in the table”, found automatically (🔎) or typed with its coordinates (“Brest 48.39, -4.49”). Same backgrounds and same framing as the coloured map.
10b3zw3: How do I colour the communes (towns) on a map, or see Paris in large?

In the map coloured by area, Settings → “Level of detail” → “Communes (towns)”, for France (overseas included), Belgium, Switzerland and Luxembourg. One row per commune: its INSEE (35238) or official code, or its name; if there are several communes with the same name (Saint-Martin…), add the department: “Saint-Martin (Gers)”, “Saint-Martin 32”; otherwise the row is flagged “namesakes” under the map. The arrondissements of Paris, Lyon and Marseille and the former merged communes are recognised. “From the app” attaches each place by its INSEE code, then its name and department. To see the communes of a single department, choose “Part of the map” → “Zoom on a department…” and type its name or number. On maps of France, “Zoomed inset on Île-de-France” shows Paris and the inner suburbs (or the whole region) in large in a free corner (under the map on a phone), with the same colours, labels and tooltips.
1p3d1gd: How do I see on a map where my ancestors were born (or married, died), one point per event?

In “＋ New diagram”, “Maps” group: 📍 the point map (one point per event, coloured by kind or by century; the points of the same place spread out in a spiral) or ⬢ the hexagon map (the map cut into equal cells, darker where there are more events; cell size in Settings). “From the app” tab: births, deaths, marriages, residences or one kind of event, only your ancestors, between two years; places without coordinates are found among the communes of France, and “🔎 Find places without a position” looks for the others. A click on a point or a cell opens the record, or the list of people.
0w8qkfe: How do I make a distorted map, where departments grow according to the number of ancestors?

In “＋ New diagram”, “Maps” group: 🫧 the distorted map (cartogram). Each department, region or country becomes a circle (or a square) whose size follows its figure, placed near its real position, with the real map faintly underneath. “From the app” → “Different people” + “Only my ancestors” gives the number of ancestors per area. Settings: shape, size, colours, labels.
0f1jngn: How do I tell an ancestor’s life on a map, step by step?

In “＋ New diagram”, “Maps” group: 📖 the storytelling map. “From the app”: choose the person, their events become the steps. Under the drawing: ◀ ▶, ▶︎ play and the slider move the life forward; the map follows the step (or shows the whole life, Settings → “The map”), the path already travelled is in red, the timeline at the bottom shows the years; a click on a step of the timeline goes there.
1q6oij9: What other drawings are there for descendants, godparents and causes of death?

In “＋ New diagram”, “Genealogy” group: 🧱 descendants as rectangles (each child under their parent, width = number of descendants; click = the record); 🎀 names passed on (godfather or godmother → godchild who bears their first name, one row per name, colour according to the relationship: grandfather, uncle, sister…; “From the app” reads the “godfather” and “godmother” witnesses of births and baptisms); 🎗 causes of death as rings (the large groups in the centre, guessed from the words of the record, the details around; click = the list of people). The cause is noted in the “Cause” field of a death.
1bku3hg: Which figure diagrams for my family (ranking, streams, histogram, box, dumbbells, figure cards…)?

In “＋ New diagram”, “Figures” group: 🏁 the changing ranking (the most given first names, decade by decade: the app calculates the ranks from the numbers); 🌊 stacked streams (the family’s occupations over 200 years); 📶 the histogram (type or paste raw values, for example ages at death: the app sorts them into bins whose width you choose); 📦 the box plot (median, quartiles and outliers calculated for each group, for example age at marriage by century); 🏋️ dumbbells (two values per row: the husband’s and the wife’s age); ↗️ the before / after slope; 🪜 the waterfall (a total that goes up and down, with subtotals); 🍭 🍡 horizontal or vertical lollipops; 🐝 the beeswarm (one person = one point, their name on hover); 🔲 small line charts in a grid (same scale or not). “Key figures” group: 🔢 figure cards (a big number, the arrow and the change from the previous value, a mini line, a colour according to your thresholds) and 🎯 the target bar (value, target and zones, for example “64% of ancestors found in the 8th generation”). The “From the app” tab → “🌳 Data from my tree” fills them with your database: ages at death and at marriage, first names, occupations, births by name or by commune, database counters, ancestors found per generation.
1t2onmp: How do I see my DNA as a diagram (painted chromosomes, cM ruler)?

In “＋ New diagram”, “DNA” group: 🧬 chromosome painting (the 22 pairs and the X, one bar for the copy received from the father and one for the mother’s; each segment shared with a cousin is painted, coloured by branch, by cousin or by side; at the top, the share of the genome already painted) and 📏 the cM ruler (each match is a point on a cM scale, under which the ranges of relationships from the Shared cM Project are lined up; write a name in “Show the possible relationships of…” to see the most likely ones in %). “From the app” tab: choose the tested person then their test, the app takes the segments or matches from the DNA tab. A click on a segment or a point opens the cousin’s record if they are in your tree. Without a test in the app, fill in or paste the table (chromosome, start, end, cM, cousin, side, branch).
1iv46af: What other figure diagrams are there (ridgelines, mosaic, dot plot, Nightingale rose, occupational mobility)?

In “＋ New diagram”: 🏔️ ridgelines (Figures group: one curve per century or per sex, overlapping like mountains, for example age at death; click on a ridge: the list of people); ⚫ the dot plot (one point per series on the same line, for example the average age at death of women and men by commune); 🔁 the mobility table (the father’s occupation in rows, the son’s or daughter’s in columns, each cell darker when it is frequent, framed when it is the same occupation; occupations can be grouped into families; click on a cell: the people); Slices group: 🧱 the variable-width mosaic (each column is wider the bigger its total, for example occupations century by century) and 🌹 the Nightingale rose (one slice per month, its area follows the figure, series stacked or overlaid: births, marriages, deaths or conceptions). “From the app” → “🌳 Data from my tree” fills them with your database.
0yzueuz: Diagrams: what do the options in “From the app → Chart” mean?

In a diagram’s editor, “From the app” tab: choose “🧮 Count in my database” in “Chart” (a ready-made starting point, or “Custom”), then set, always in the same order: what is counted (people, births, marriages, deaths, events, families, places, media; “each person only once” for events), the group of people (your whole database, your ancestors, your descendants, the paternal or maternal branch, a label, one of your lists, a search in the names or the people you choose), the period (from … to …, written as in a record), the grouping (surname, first name, sex, occupation, generation, commune, department, region, country, century, decade, year, month, age, number of children…), the series (by sex or by century, for stacked columns, the pyramid, the heat map), the sorting, the top N and “Others”, “Unknown” shown or hidden, the unit (number, %, average or median of age at death, age at marriage or number of children) and “🔄 Keep up to date” (the diagram is recalculated when your database changes). The sentence above the preview sums up the setting (“People born between 1800 and 1900, my ancestors, by department, top 10”). Each option has its “?” tooltip. The other types (maps, timelines, calendar, survival, occupations, marriages, tree figures…) keep their panel and gain the same group of people and the same period. An example, an app statistic or one of your charts can also be sorted, cut to the top N and switched to %. Your diagrams already made do not change.
0usezmw: Which diagrams about life and death, couples, places and my research (child mortality, widowhood, signatures, proof…)?

In “＋ New diagram”. “Life and death” group: 👶 Child mortality (by decade, the share of children who died before 1 year and before 5 years), 👨‍👩‍👧 Surviving siblings (for each couple: children born, reaching adulthood, dying young), 🗓 Seasons of births and deaths (month × period). “Couples and families” group: 💔 Widowhood and remarriage (the time before remarrying, men and women), ⏳ Length of marriages, 👴 Age of the parents at each birth (scatter plot), 🤰 Conceptions before marriage (first child born before the marriage or less than 8 months after), 💑 Age gap between spouses. “Places” group: 🧭 Far from the cradle (how far away the ancestors were born, generation by generation). “My research” group: ✍️ Able to sign, ✅ What you have proved (ancestors’ births, marriages and deaths with a source, without a source, not found), 📚 Registers consulted (the years seen and the gaps, according to the record index tracking and your sourced records). The “From the app” tab fills them with your database (without living people or confidential records), with the group of people and the period; a click on a bar or a point opens the list of people. The dark years, the incoming names, marriages between villages and the witnesses and godparents already existed: 📉 Births, deaths and crises, 🌳 Surname tree, 🎼 Chord diagram (marriages between villages) and 🕸️ Network of relationships (witnesses, godparents…).
18tve8u: Which diagrams for a relationship, completeness, the ahnentafel, DNA (Leeds), the wheel of the year and two-axis figures?

In “＋ New diagram”. “Genealogy” group: 🔗 the relationship path (choose two people: the shortest path step by step and the sentence “… is the second cousin of …”; in-laws and pedigree collapse are taken into account), 🧩 tree completeness (share of ancestors known in each generation, as bars or as a fan), 📜 the ancestry table (one row per Sosa number; “🖨 Print the table…” in “From the app”). “Maps” group: 🎯 the family’s centre of gravity (the average point of the places of birth of each generation and its path) and 🌈 the generations map. “DNA” group: 🧬 the Leeds matrix (your matches from 90 to 400 cM sorted by grandparent colour, from the DNA tab). “Timelines” group: 🎡 the wheel of the year (birthdays, marriages, deaths, name days). “Figures” group: 📊 bars + line (second axis on the right), ↔️ diverging bars, 🏔 stacked hills, 🧵 parallel coordinates, 📶 step line (how many in the family were alive, year by year). “🔒 For sharing” removes the names of living people; a confidential record is never named. A click on a box opens the record (or the list of people).
0cmmz2h: How do I annotate a diagram (arrow, text, area, “WWI”)?

In the diagram editor, “⚙️ Customise” tab → “✏️ Annotations”: ＋ Arrow, ＋ Text, ＋ Area, ＋ Vertical or horizontal band, ＋ Date marker (a date, or “from… to…” for a period). Drag them on the preview (and their small circles to enlarge them); double-click to change the text; Delete or × to remove them (“↶ Undo” right after). They are kept with the diagram, wherever it is placed, on export (PNG, SVG, PDF) and when printing.
0lkmkdi: How do I give the same style to all my diagrams?

“⚙️ Customise” tab → “🎨 Style”: a ready-made style (Plain, Archive, Bright colours, Printable black and white, Colour-blind) or your own (palette, font, background, line thickness, corners, text size, grid). “💾 My saved styles” keeps it under a name (and exports or imports it). “Apply to all diagrams” puts it on all of them (“↶ Undo” puts each one back as before); “⭐ Default style” gives it to new diagrams. “As before” removes the style.
1ex48jx: How do I compare side by side (small multiples), by sex, century, branch, place or generation?

“⚙️ Customise” tab → “▦ Small multiples” → “Repeat the diagram by”: a small drawing per group, side by side, with the same scale. “The series in the table” works as soon as there are several columns of figures; for sex, century, branch, department, country or generation, first get your figures with “🧮 Count in my database” (“From the app” tab), ticking “Keep up to date”. For columns, bars, lines, areas, stacked and radar.
04ezebg: How do I make a diagram scroll through time (▶ the years)?

As soon as the data has dates (years as categories, timelines, members of a group, schedule…), a ▶ slider appears under the preview: play, speed (slow, normal, fast), loop, “⤢ All” to go back to the full drawing, and “🎬 Video” (WebM or MP4, depending on the browser). The scale does not move during playback. With “Reduce animations” (Settings → Accessibility), playback moves one step per second, without sliding. To show it also where the diagram is placed: “⚙️ Customise” → “▶ Playback over time”.
146lk65: How do I add an average, a median or a target to a chart?

“⚙️ Customise” tab → “📏 Reference lines and axes” (columns, bars, stacked, lines, areas): ＋ Average, ＋ Median (calculated automatically, over all the series or just one), ＋ Target, ＋ Value. In the same place: “Logarithmic scale” for very large differences, and “Second axis (on the right)” to draw a series with its own scale.
1tz0rgo: Does every diagram have a “Chart” menu in “From the app”?

Yes. In a diagram’s editor, “From the app” tab, each type starts with “Chart”: ready-made starting points. For columns, bars, pies…: “🧮 Count in my database” and the app’s statistics. For the types that have their own panel (maps, timelines, fan, calendar, survival, occupations, marriages, DNA, child mortality, widowhood…): for example “Birth regions of my ancestors (6 generations)”, “Departures (born here, died elsewhere)”, “Who was alive in 1789”, “My ancestors, by century”; the choice sets the fields of the panel (and the group of people or the period), then click the panel’s “Use…” button. “✏️ Custom” leaves everything to you. The scatter plot, the flow (Sankey), the organisation chart, the two timelines, the figure cards and the target bar also take their data from your database (age at marriage and at death, father’s → son’s occupation, department of birth → of death, your ancestors as an organisation chart, the life of the starting person, the quality of your database…).
07891ei: How do I note that a person signed a record (or “cannot sign”)?

In “Edit an event”: under the witnesses, “✍️ The person (or the husband) signed” and, for a marriage, “✍️ The wife signed”: Not known, Yes, or No (cannot sign). Each witness also has their own “✍️ Signed the record” box. The “✍️ Able to sign” diagram shows, period by period, the share of husbands, wives and witnesses who could sign.
1fjlj7r: How do I make a diagram of the woodcutters who had 3 children born in Pernay (combined criteria)?

In a diagram’s editor, “From the app” tab, “Chart” → “✏️ Custom”. Under “Only the people…”, “＋ Criterion” adds as many criteria as you want, the same as in My lists: occupation, number of children (“3 and 3” = exactly 3, “3” then an empty box = at least 3), place of birth, place of death, period of birth or death, sex, living or not, age at death, Sosa generation, label, without a source… “not” reverses a criterion. With two or more criteria, choose “all these criteria (AND)” or “at least one (OR)”. Then “What is counted” and “Group by” (decade of birth, commune, occupation, age at marriage, age at first child, number of unions, branch, with or without a source…). The sentence above the preview reads the setting back and says how many people are found (“People, occupation “woodcutter”, having 3 children, born in “Pernay”, by decade — 2 people found”). A click on a bar or a slice opens the list of these people. The ready-made starting points are arranged by section (People, Couples, Children, Places, Occupations, Dates, My research, Media); those that make no sense for the chosen drawing are greyed out “not for this diagram” (for example decades in a pie chart).
0yghktd: How do I create my own chart from external data (Wikipedia, spreadsheet, image)?

Wherever you place a diagram, “⤒ Import”: 📄 File (CSV, or an LCNDA diagram or chart), 📋 Paste a table (first column = the names, following columns = the figures, a row of headings becomes the names of the series), 🌐 Wikipedia page (paste the address: the tables and chart images of the page appear, choose one; you need the Internet), 🖼️ Image of a chart (pie, bars, columns, line or hemicycle: the app spots the colours and suggests the slices, lengths or seats; you name them, correct them, give the real top value). Then you choose the drawing and set everything in the editor. The step-by-step guide is also in the ⚙️ of the diagram gallery.
1etf3xk: How do I say that a person was an athlete, an elected official, a soldier, a farmer… (profiles)?

On their record, the “🧩 This person was…” block → “🧩 Choose their profiles…” (or Edit the record → “Blocks to show” → “🧩 Profiles…”). Tick one or more profiles (Artist, Athlete, Politician, Local elected official, Soldier, Farmer, Teacher…), then “Apply”. Each profile adds its sections to the person’s page. A person can have several; unticking a profile hides its sections without erasing what you wrote in them. The “Artist” box on the record and the “Artist” profile are the same thing.
03je6f6: How do I create my own profile (brass band musician, beekeeper…)?

In the profiles window: “＋ Create my own profile…”. In 3 steps: 1 · the name, the icon and the colour; 2 · the sections, taken from other profiles (the artist’s concerts, the athlete’s statistics…) or your own (a table, linked records, images, a text); 3 · the order of the page. Your profile goes into “✎ My profiles” and is ticked like the others.
1whh87z: How do I see the page of a person who has several profiles (artist, athlete, mayor…)?

“🧩 This person was…” block → “Open their page”. At the top: “All together” (a single page with the sections of all their profiles, and the life timeline coloured by profile) or one profile at a time. “⚙️ Organise the page”: arrange the profiles and sections (⠿ or ↑ ↓), hide some (👁), choose the width (full line, ½, ⅓), “Setting specific to this person”, “Hide empty sections”. The coloured edge says which profile a section comes from.
0ng31lf: How do I record a politician’s career (terms of office, elections, votes)?

Tick the “🗳 Politician” profile (or “🏛 Local elected official”), then open their page: 🏛 Terms and positions (level, place, dates, predecessor, successor), 🗳 Elections (ballot, round, registered voters, votes, %, result, opponents, poster, election manifesto, results by commune), 👥 Parties, groups and committees, 📜 Texts, votes and proposals, 🏢 Government, 🗣 Speeches, ⚠️ Controversies, 🗺 Map of terms, and the career timeline. “⚙️ Organise” offers templates: Local elected official, Member of parliament, Minister, Activist, Diplomat, Senior civil servant.
11la1y8: How do I record an athlete’s career (clubs, medals, records, statistics)?

Tick the “🏅 Athlete · sportsperson” profile, choose their sport or sports (more than 120, each with its own fields: position and shirt for rugby or football, time and wind for athletics, horse for riding, grades for judo, Elo for chess…). Their page: 🏟 Clubs and teams, 🥇 Medals and titles, ⏱ Records, 📊 Statistics by season (columns depending on the sport, “＋ Add a column”, “🧮 Calculated column”), 🏁 Results (wins, losses, by competition), coaches, injuries and career change, and the timeline of clubs and selections.
1je0dm2: How do I keep an artist’s bibliography, works, discography or filmography?

On their record, tick “Artist” (Edit → Blocks to show) and choose their discipline.
