The blocks 📚 Bibliography, 🖼️ Works and inventory, 💿 Discography (musician, singer, composer, conductor, band) and 🎬 Filmography (filmmaker, actor, videographer) then appear; a block already filled in always stays visible. “See all, edit” opens the catalogue full screen: 🎨 the artist’s page, then one tab per kind (Books, Works, Records, Tracks, Films, Exhibitions; “＋” for the others). Each list has the same bar (🔍 Search, Filter ▾, List | Cards, Sort: by year, by title, catalogue number, value or “My order” with ⠿ ↑ ↓); ＋ New, ⤒ Import, ⤓ Export (PDF, printing, CSV spreadsheet, 💾 re-importable file). If the record is not ticked “Artist” yet, the app offers to tick it when you first save.
0ecxeky: How do I make an inventory of an artist’s works?

Artist’s catalogue → 🖼️ Works and inventory: inventory number (suggested after the last one), catalogue raisonné number, technique, support, dimensions, signature, where the work is (in the family, museum, private collection, sold, lent, lost…), exact place, owner, condition, estimated value, provenance, exhibitions, photos. The “Inventory” view gives the table with the total of the values; “🖨 Print the illustrated inventory” puts it on paper with the photos. ⤒ Import: a table from your spreadsheet pasted as it is (columns No., Title, Date, Technique, Dimensions, Place, Owner, Condition, Value… recognised automatically), or the known works from Wikidata (those in museums, with their image).
0xshuqo: How do I make a complete discography, track by track, as on Discogs?

Artist’s catalogue → 💿 Discography: each record has its type (album, EP, single, compilation, live, soundtrack…), label, catalogue number, format, country, date, genre and styles, barcode, production, studio, its photos (front, back, disc, booklet, inside), its credits, its tracks (no., title, duration — the total duration is calculated; 📝 for the lyrics, notes and annotations, the track’s credits and the version) and its editions and pressings (format, label, catalogue number, country, year, barcode). 📋 “Paste a track list” fills everything in at once. Click on a record: its page as on Discogs, with lyrics that unfold.
0b05v4s: How do I import a discography from Discogs (or MusicBrainz, Apple Music)?

Catalogue → 💿 Discography → ⤒ Import → Discogs: paste the address of the artist’s page (…discogs.com/artist/…), of an album (…/master/…) or of a record (…/release/…). For an artist, their releases appear to be ticked (appearances unticked); each album comes with its tracks, durations, credits, label, format, covers and the list of its editions. Discogs limits the pace: a little more than one second per record. To search by name, you need a free Discogs token (discogs.com → Settings → Developers) to put in 🔑 Keys. Without a key: MusicBrainz (albums, tracks, editions, covers from the Cover Art Archive), Apple Music (tracks and durations) or Wikidata. The covers are brought into the record’s media (tick box). You need the Internet.
16brdf6: How do I import a filmography (IMDb, TMDb)?

Catalogue → 🎬 Filmography → ⤒ Import: “Wikidata” with the person’s name, or “An IMDb address” (…imdb.com/name/nm…): IMDb has no free access, but Wikidata links each IMDb entry and gives films, jobs (actor, directing, screenplay, music, cinematography, editing, production), roles, director, length and the film’s IMDb identifier. With a free TMDb key (🔑 Keys), “TMDb” adds posters, summaries, cast, countries and companies. Everything can then be corrected by hand (role, awards, festivals, notes).
0q0c9ok: How do I add a sculpture, a poster, a play, a concerto… (all the types of works)?

In the person’s catalogue: “＋ New work” (on their page) or “＋” at the end of the tabs. The “What kind of work?” window arranges 131 types into 12 families (visual arts, music, stage, writing, moving image and sound, design and crafts, space and landscape, digital and games, model-making and hobbies, tastes and scents, linking records, my types). Type in the box (“bronze”, “opera”, “podcast”, “coppersmith”…), filter by family, then click a type: its record opens with its own fields. “☰ See the list” opens the list of that type instead of a new record. ⚙️ Manage the types: hide those you never use.
1lwpt79: How do I record the casts of a bronze sculpture?

The sculpture’s record → “🔥 Casts and editions” → “＋ Add a cast”. Each cast is a small record: engraved number (1/8, EA I…), founder, date, process (lost wax, sand), patina, patinator, foundry mark, weight, posthumous cast, “ours”, where it is and who owns it, provenance and sales, photos. The table of casts can be filtered (all, during the artist’s lifetime, posthumous); the planned edition (“8 + 4 EA”) recalls the legal limit. Enlargements, reductions and versions are linked at the bottom of the record.
194hcfy: How do I follow a play, its productions and its tours?

Create the play (author, genre, acts, characters, publication), then “＋ Add a production”: company, director, team, music, cast (character, performer, understudy). In each production: “＋ Add a performance” (date, town, venue, audience, première…) and “＋ Add a tour”. The play’s record shows everything as a Tree, a Table, a Calendar or on the Map.
1m6qhop: How do I create my own type of work (carnival float, carved clog…)?

“＋ New work” → “＋ Create my own type…”. In 5 steps: 1 · name, plural, icon, family, start from scratch or from an existing type, “part” records (a float has editions); 2 · the fields, arranged in groups: 24 kinds (text, date, duration, dimensions, list of choices, person + role, place, linked record, image, table, calculation…), or taken from other types in the library; each field has its help, its starting value, “required”, “shown by default” and “in the search”; 3 · the possible links to other types, named in both directions; 4 · the columns of the list and the lines of the thumbnails; 5 · the preview. Your type has the same tools as the others; ⚙️ Manage the types → ⤓ to export it and give it away.
0j66pa1: Where is the list of craft trades, and how do I record a piece of ironwork?

“＋ New work” → “Design and crafts” family → “⚒️ The 16 fields of the craft trades…”: the official French list (order of 24 December 2015), with search by trade or speciality. Choosing a trade opens the right type of work with the trade noted. A piece of ironwork: kind (gate, banister…), patron and decision, where it is installed, designer, metal, techniques (forged, riveted, repoussé…), dimensions, decoration, hallmark, workshop and journeymen, preparatory drawings, commission (quote, paid, deadlines), protection (Historic Monuments, Mérimée database), states and restorations.
1okz09b: How do I note that a person was a craftsperson (apprenticeship, compagnonnage, MOF)?

Tick the “🔨 Craftsperson” profile (or, in the craft trades window, “🔨 “Craftsperson” profile”). Their page gains its sections: 🧑‍🏭 Training and apprenticeship (master, contract, CAP diploma, schools), 🛠 Compagnonnage (guild, journeyman name, Tour de France, masterpiece), 🎖 Titles (Meilleur Ouvrier de France, Maître d’art, Entreprise du patrimoine vivant), 🏭 Workshop · business, 🔏 Hallmarks and marks, ⚒️ their pieces. “…” on a section to write it.
1dwyun8: How do I import a bibliography?

Catalogue → 📚 Bibliography → ⤒ Import: Open Library by ISBN (on the back of the book), all the books by an author, or the books on a subject (they arrive under “About him / about her”), or Wikidata. Cover, publisher, year, pages, ISBN and language are filled in. Each book gives its link with the artist (by them, about them, illustrations, translation, preface, exhibition catalogue) and where to find it (library, shelfmark, at home).
00dhs9l: How do I show, hide or arrange the fields of an artist’s record (record, track, painting…)?

On the record, “⚙️ Shown fields”: by groups (Release, Tracks and credits, My copy, Identifiers…), 👁 shows or hides a field, ⠿ (drag) or ↑ ↓ arranges it, and the form follows the same order. A hidden field keeps what is written in it; when reading, an empty field is never shown (“Hide empty fields” switch). Tabs: The record, The list (the columns), The thumbnails, The export (what goes into an entry and into the book). The setting applies to all artists, or only to this one (“Setting specific to…”). “💾 Saved settings”: save under a name, ⤓ export, ⤒ import; ↺ Reset to default.
0baawev: How do I add my own fields to a record, a work, a book?

“⚙️ Shown fields” → “＋ Add a field” (or at the bottom of the form): a name (“Bought by”, “Listened to on”…) and its kind: text, long text, number, date, period, duration, dimensions, measure + unit, amount, list of choices, labels, yes/no, rating out of 5, web link, code, person, place, linked record, image · sound · video, document, colour, note. Tick “For all records…” to have it everywhere. Your fields go into “✎ My fields” (or the chosen group), can be renamed (✎) and removed (🗑, with “↶ Undo”; “Put back a removed field” brings them back).
1td8qe4: How do I create my own kind of record (sculpture, poster, carnival float…)?

In the catalogue, “＋” at the end of the tabs → “＋ Create a kind of record…”: a name, the plural, an icon, a family, and “Start from…” nothing or an existing kind (its fields are taken over). Then “⚙️ Shown fields” to add, arrange and hide its fields. It has its list, its filters, its export, and its records link to others like the app’s kinds.
0p70fqz: How do I change or remove the emoji in front of a menu tab (🧬 DNA, 📒 Notes…)?

Settings → Appearance → “Order and names of the main menu”: to the right of each tab, the small box contains its emoji. Type or paste another one ({mac:⌃⌘Space|pc:⊞ + .}), or empty the box to have none, then “Save”. “↺ Reset the names to default” also puts back the original emojis.
0u3kfxt: I have the same record or the same book twice, three times: how do I note it?

On its record, in “📦 My copy (collection)”: the first copy is described as usual (condition, storage, price, dedication); below, “Other copies (duplicate, triplicate…)” → “＋ One more copy” adds a line per copy, each with its condition, its edition or pressing, its place, its price, its value and its dedication. ⚙️ Shown fields lets you show or hide this line.
1haw5mv: How do I link a track to its takes, its mixes and the records it appears on?

The track (🎵 the written work: lyrics, music, publisher, SACEM…) has its recordings: “＋ Add a recording” (take, mix, remaster, version, live), each with its date, studio, duration, sound file (▶), credits, “made from” (the mix of a take…) and “chosen take”. On a record, each track can point to a recording (purple badge): the track’s record then shows the tree of takes and mixes and, for each, the releases (record, track, format, year, duration). “Tree | Table” changes the view.
03qnlb8: How do I record the provenance, exhibitions and bibliography of a painting?

On the work’s record: “Provenance” (one line per step: date, how — the artist, given, sold, bought back, inheritance… —, who, detail, price) reads like a timeline; “Exhibitions”: each exhibition is a record (🏛), with the catalogue number and the lender; “Bibliography of the work”: the book or article (📚 record) and the page. Also: catalogue raisonné and inventory numbers, where it is and who owns it, states and restorations, value and insurance, related works (study, sketch, replica, engraving after, pendant), editions and casts.
1wwca8s: How do I make the book of the catalogue raisonné or the discography?

In the list of works (or records), “📖 Create the book…” — or Page layout → “🖼 Catalogue raisonné” / “💿 Discography”. Choose the artist, the design, the format, the works (those of the filtered list, or all), the order, the parts of the book (to tick and arrange: cover, introduction, chronology, entries, exhibitions, bibliography, index, concordances…), the fields of each entry and the layout (a double page per work, one, two or four per page). The book opens in the page layout; each entry follows the work’s record: File → “↻ Update the dynamic objects” picks up a corrected provenance.
1pis8xp: How do I organise an artist’s page?

Catalogue → 🎨 Page → “⚙️ Organise the page”: each section (biography, artistic identity, awards, discography, works, exhibitions, bibliography, filmography, concerts…) can be arranged (⠿ or ↑ ↓), hidden (👁) and take the whole line, half or a third. “Template” starts from the discipline (Musician, Painter, Writer, Filmmaker, Photographer, Sculptor, Architect); “＋ Add a section” for your own (“Their instruments”…). A section’s “…” button edits the artist’s profile (stage names, bands and their members, labels, galleries, training, awards, official links, press).
0q5jkoe: Why “Mentioned in artists’ catalogues” on a person’s record?

A person chosen in a catalogue (credit on a record, owner of a painting, dedication, band member…) sees this block on their record: “Paris canaille (1958) — accordion”. The links read both ways: the record’s page also shows the person in “🔗 Linked to”. A name without a record (grey “?” badge) can become a record later.
1g07huj: How do I record a concert or a show with its setlist (setlist.fm-style)?

Artist’s catalogue → 🎤 Stage tab (or “＋” → 🎤 Stage and shows → Concerts and performances) → “＋ New concert or performance”. Choose the kind of evening (concert, comedy, theatre, dance, circus, orchestra, storytelling): the setlist adapts (songs, sketches, scenes, acts, works). Each line points to the record of the track, sketch or scene (“＋ Create” if it does not exist yet); 📝 on a line for the cover, the 👤 guests with their role, the dedication, the 1st or last time, a version, “unfinished”, the duration. “＋ An encore”, “📋 Paste a list” (one title per line), “📋 Copy another evening’s setlist”. The title fills itself in (“Joseph MARTIN in Tulle, 14 July 1958”). On the record, a title without a record has “＋ record” to create it in one click.
15ifgn9: How do I see the most played tracks, the first and last time, the map of concerts?

🎤 Stage tab: the top bar offers List, Cards, Map, Timeline and 📊 Statistics. The statistics (most played titles with the first and last time, evenings per year, country, town and venue, average length, titles per evening, typical setlist of a tour, never played live, compare two evenings, roles and understudies in the theatre, conductors and soloists, who goes on stage most often) are calculated on the filtered list: filter a tour, a town, years or a title played to see them change. On the map, the size of the marker = the number of evenings; a click shows the list for that place.
0ch3t44: How do I group the dates of a tour?

On an evening’s record, “Tour” field → “＋ Create the record “…””. The tour’s record shows its dates (each evening shows “date 12/31”), the route on the map and the typical setlist (the title most often played in each position, encores included). “＋ Add a date” creates the next evening, already linked to the tour.
16kko8q: How do I record the performances of a play, the evening’s roles and the understudies?

An evening of the “🎭 Theatre” kind: the “Production” field makes it one of its performances (the production’s record lists them all, with “＋ Add a performance”); “Evening’s roles”: the role, played by 👤, regular, standing in, understudy, created the role; also incidents, curtain calls and box office takings. The actor’s filmography counts their performances and stand-ins.
1f1m80y: How do I turn a concert recording into “live” recordings?

On the evening’s record, 🎙 Recordings box: choose the sound or video, then “→ Turn into “live” recordings”. Each track in the setlist that has a record gets a “Live” recording (date, place, recording, timing noted on the line); “↶ Undo” right after if needed.
0in0vt6: How do I make the filmography and stage credits of an actor or actress?

Catalogue → 🎭 Roles tab. Each detailed role is a record: the work (film, series, episode, production…), the character, the kind of role (lead, supporting, extra, voice, dubbing…), the director 👤, the credits, the shoot (period, locations), the co-stars, the fee, the contract, performances and stand-ins, the original voice, the anecdote. The list also gathers the films in the catalogue, the series (episodes ticked), the evening roles of performances and records from other catalogues that mention the person. Tabs Cinema, Television, Theatre, Voice, Advertising…, search, filters (kind of role, years, director, co-star), sorting, List | Cards | Timeline; a click on a line shows its card; “＋ Make it a detailed role record” for a line coming from elsewhere.
07csaee: Where can I see all the people who have profiles (artist, athlete, elected official…)?

Lists → “This person was… (profiles)”: one row (or one card, “Cards”) per person with the coloured badges of their profiles. Filter ▾ by profile, group, number of profiles, occupation, customised page or locked record; Sort ▾ (A → Z, most profiles, most records…). A click opens their page. The “Occupations” list stays separate: it sorts the occupations (a text), this one the people.
1infa19: How do I make a section of a person’s page ¾ or ⅔ wide, or change the colour of its edge?

On their page: “⚙️ Organise the page”. Each section has its width (full line, ½, ⅓, ¼, ⅔, ¾) and a colour badge for the top edge (app colours, recent colours, eyedropper, # code, “None” = no edge; ↺ = the profile’s colour). In “All together”, a profile’s badge changes its colour (badges, edges, timeline). The same goes for the artist’s page.
1kxrbos: How do I set the pages of all the people who have profiles in one go?

Settings → Appearance → Person and animal records → “This person was… (profiles)”. On the left the standard setting (order, visibility, width and colour of the sections; order, colour and visibility of the profiles; templates), on the right an exception for one person (chosen in the picker). At the bottom, the customised pages: “↗ Open” or “↺ Reset to default” (the page goes back to the standard setting, with ↶ Undo). “💾 Saved settings” keeps everything under a name.
0dv8i9i: Why can I no longer edit a person’s catalogue or page?

Their record is locked (or the app is in view-only mode): the catalogue, its work records and their profile page open read-only (“🔒 Locked record” at the top); the buttons to edit, add a profile or a record are hidden. Unlock the person’s record to edit.
1jjkppc: Why “Tick Craftsperson?” when I add a piece of ironwork or ceramics?

A craft piece (ironwork, ceramics, glass, goldsmithing, cabinet-making, instrument-making…) goes into the “Craftsperson” profile (or “Artist” if it is already ticked). A work of art (sculpture, painting…) asks for “Artist”; a tour or a series, “Artist” or “Actor”.
13ydvt9: How do I show the “Actor” profile on a person’s page?

Tick the “Actor, actress, performer” profile (🎭 Roles tab → “🎬 Tick the profile”, or the record’s profiles). Their page gains its sections: roles (with Cinema, Television, Theatre…), filmography, television, stage credits, voice, advertising, music videos, statistics (roles per decade, most frequent directors and co-stars, lead / supporting), training, agents and companies, castings, awards, skills and voice, stage evenings. “⚙️ Organise the page” arranges them, hides them, chooses their width; “…” on a section writes the profile.
14uwxns: How do I record a series, its seasons and its episodes (IMDb-style)?

Catalogue → “＋” → 🎬 Films and shows → Series and programmes → “＋ New series, programme”. On its record: “＋ Add a season”, then “＋ Several…” creates all the numbered episodes at once (you then write their title, date, director, screenplay, guests, filming locations, music, video). Click a season to see its episodes, an episode for its card. Same model for a television or radio programme, a podcast, a radio serial, a manga in volumes or a book saga (cycle → volumes).
053u3df: How do I record the episodes in which a person acted or worked?

On the series’ record, the “👤 … in this series” panel: 🎭 Role (character, kind of role) or 🛠 Job (screenwriter, director, composer…). Tick the episodes in the list (Shift+click for a whole range), or write “episodes 2 to 7” → Tick, or “the whole season”, “the whole series”; add the credited name and the fee, then 💾 Save. Their filmography then shows “recurring · S3 ep. 2-7 (6 episodes)”. “＋ A person…” for another crew member; “Remove” offers “↶ Undo”.
1wyzdxx: I deleted a record or a work by mistake: how do I get it back?

Right after, “↶ Undo” in the message at the bottom left: the record comes back, with the same number and all its links. To keep a catalogue elsewhere: ⤓ Export → 💾 File, then ⤒ Import → “A file exported from here” (the old “JSON backup” can be re-imported too).
0qt2f62: How do I record an invention and its patents?

On the inventor’s record: open their page (catalogue) → 💡 Inventions → “＋ New invention”. Field, problem, principle, first idea, workshop; “📜 Patents”: one line per country (country, no., filing, grant, applicant, status) and, with 📝, the title, the claims, the class, the patent attorney; then prototypes, licences, manufactured objects, prior art and lawsuits, awards (Lépine competition…).
0y3koyp: How do I record a discovery (species, comet, gene, site…)?

The person’s page → 🔬 Discoveries → “＋ New discovery”: choose the “Kind” (species, comet, gene, fossil, archaeological site, wreck…) and the matching fields appear. Then the place (on the map), the discoverers 👤, the naming (name, in honour of, status), the publications and “recognised or disputed”.
0fdb6pt: How do I make a scientist’s profile (thesis, positions, students, publications)?

Tick “🔬 Scientist” on their record, then open their page: each section (thesis, laboratories and positions, publications, academic genealogy, missions, academies, things named after them, notebooks…) has its “…” button to write in. Institutions are Employer records. ⚙️ Organise the page → “Template: Scientist” for the starting order.
05k7urq: How do I import a researcher’s publications (DOI, ORCID, HAL)?

The scientist’s page → 📚 Publications → “⤒ Import (DOI, ORCID, HAL)”: paste DOIs, their ORCID identifier or their name in HAL, tick what to take. Those already there are recognised (same DOI or same title); their name among the authors is linked to their record.
13i4j1n: How do I see the academic genealogy (supervisor, students)?

The “🌳 Academic genealogy” section of the scientist’s page: their thesis supervisor and their mentors above, their students below. If a student has their own record with this thesis supervisor, they are added automatically.
001s638: How do I record an expedition and draw its route on the map?

Tick “🧭 Explorer” on their record, then page → 🧭 Expeditions → “＋ New expedition”: “🗺 Route”, one line per stage (place, dates, means, ▲ summit): the map draws itself. Then members 👤 and their roles, firsts, notebooks and films, collections and where they are today, accounts, place names.
1kv1ggu: How do I note that a person appeared in the newspaper, on the radio or on TV?

On their record, the “📰 In the media” block → “＋ Add”: the kind of media (press, radio, TV, podcast, web, newsreels, book, poster), the type of appearance (interview, portrait, report, obituary, birth or marriage notice, review, published photo, small ad…), the date, the outlet (chosen in “Lists → Magazines and periodicals”, or written as it is), the title or programme, the page or duration, the journalist, the other people with their role (★ main, ☆ secondary), the subject, the tone, an extract, and the scan, sound or video (the images, sounds and videos window). The block shows a timeline by year and “📰 Press · 📻 Radio · 📺 TV” badges to sort what you see.
1g52xzt: Where can I see all the family’s articles and programmes?

Lists → “Press review”: all the appearances of all the people, with the usual bar (🔍 Search, Filter ▾ by person, kind of media, type, tone, List | Cards, Sort). From a record, “See all” opens the same list already filtered on the person (“Joseph MARTIN ×” badge: one click removes it to see everyone). ⚙️ chooses the columns, “⤓ Export” gives a spreadsheet, a PDF or a file.
1cd07ji: How do I record a prize, a medal, a decoration or a competition (even an unusual one)?

On the record, the “🏆 Competitions and awards” block → “＋ Add”: the category (sport, game, food, unusual, agricultural, artistic, school, professional, decoration… or your own word), the award, the competition (a 🏅 record that gathers its whole list of winners: “＋ Create” directly from the field), the edition, the level (local → world), the event, the date, the place, the performance, the rank, the medal, the title won, the prize, the organiser, the jury or teammates, the trophy or the cutting. For a decoration (Légion d’honneur, Mérite agricole, medals…) the grade, the promotion, the decree, the file (Léonore database) and the sponsor also appear. Lists → “Honours list” gathers the whole family, with its timeline.
1thklii: How do I record school, diplomas and classmates?

On the record, the “🎓 Diplomas and education” block: “＋ A stage” for each school or training (primary school, secondary school, high school, university, apprenticeship, compagnonnage, military training…) with the establishment (a record that gathers everyone who went there), the years, the class, boarder or day pupil, the teachers and classmates (picker with a role), the subjects, the results, the end-of-year prizes, the class photos and the school reports; “＋ Add” in “Diplomas” for a diploma (ready-made list: certificat d’études, brevet, CAP, baccalauréat, degree, driving licence, military certificates… or free text). The block shows the timeline of the path, the table of diplomas, the latest class photo with the classmates, and the school record books and reports.
0gt0zcx: Where can I find all the family’s tracks, albums, plays, films, inventions, terms of office…?

Lists → “🎨 Creations and careers” group: “Everything that was created or lived”, then one list per family (🎵 Music, 🎭 Stage, 🎬 Films and series, 📚 Writings, 🖼 Visual arts, ⚒️ Crafts, 💡 Inventions and discoveries, 🧭 Expeditions, 🏛 Political careers, 🏅 Sport, 🎓 Education, ✎ My types…), for all the people. The same bar as the other lists: 🔍 Search (title, person, place, year), Filter ▾ (kind with the number, person, period, place, with image, with sound or video), List | Cards, Sort. “Group by kind” puts a subheading per kind (“🎵 Tracks (34)”); untick it to mix everything. A click opens the record in the person’s catalogue, “↗” opens the person’s record, “＋ New…” asks for the person then the kind. Press review and Honours list are in the same group.
1wojb8j: A person is mentioned as a classmate, jury member or guest in someone else’s record: where can I see it?

On their own record, in the same block: the appearances, awards and stages stored with another person where they appear are shown too, with “in the record of …” and their role. A click opens the record concerned.
07deohi: Which shapes are there for the decorative tree to print?

Lists → Editing tools → 🌳 Decorative tree → ＋: fan (half circle, 240°, three quarters 270°), wheel, drawn tree (trunk, branches, foliage), tree of boxes from bottom to top, or ancestry table from left to right. Up to 12 generations for the fans and the wheel, 8 for the drawn tree, 7 for the boxes (the number offered follows the shape). The tree then opens in the vector drawing so you can retouch everything.
0hbstwc: How do I create my own style or my own size for the decorative tree?

In the tree window: “＋” next to Style (or 🎨 My styles): a name, the starting style, the font, and each colour (paper, ink, title, the person’s box, paternal and maternal sides, empty boxes, trunk, leaves) with a preview. ⚙️ next to Size (or ⚙️ My sizes): your sizes in cm (from 5 to 500), and for all of them, sizes as well as styles, tick the ones you see and arrange them with ↑ ↓. The same settings are in Settings → “Editing, retouching, page layout and sound” → 🌳 Decorative tree, with the shape, size and style offered at the start.
0s8zf81: How do I arrange the shapes of the decorative tree or give them a shortcut?

“⚙️ Customise” in the tree window, or Settings → “Editing, retouching, page layout and sound” → Buttons and options → 🌳 Decorative tree: hide or arrange the shapes and buttons. Just below (and in Settings → Keyboard shortcuts), give a key to a shape, to “My sizes”, “My styles” or to “Create the tree”.
1agbn5f: How do I choose a custom size for a map (width, height, unit, resolution)?

Lists → Editing tools → 🗺️ Map → “＋ New map”: in “Size”, take a size from the list (A0 to A6, US Letter, postcard, square, 10 × 15, 13 × 18 photos…, 16:9 screens) or “✎ Custom size…”: width × height, the unit (mm, cm, px, inches), ▯ Portrait / ▭ Landscape and the resolution (dpi) for export as an image. The size is remembered for the next map and stored in “⭐ My sizes” (at the top of the list, in all tools); “× Remove from My sizes” takes it away. To print the screen (a map included) in a custom size: 🖨 Print → “✎ Other…”.
0q5vq4m: How do I change the size of a drawing or a map after creating it?

In the vector drawing: File → “📐 Document size / artboards…” (also in the 📄 Document tab): the size from the shared list or a custom size, the unit, the orientation, the resolution suggested for export, the background (colour or transparent) and the bleed (3 mm at first, added around each page when exporting “with bleed and crop marks”). The objects stay in place, are rescaled with the artboard, or keep their size and are recentred. ↶ (⌘Z) goes back to the previous size; 💾 Save keeps it with the drawing.
1lr4nvn: Where do I put the title, author or rights of a drawing, a book or a retouched photo?

File → “ℹ️ Information…” in the vector drawing (title, author, subject, description, keywords, rights, language, date: in the exported SVG and PDF), in the page layout (title, author, subject, description, keywords, language and optional ISBN, checked: in the PDF, HTML and ePub) and in photo retouching (title, author, rights, description, keywords, date, linked people: written into the PNG or JPG image, readable by Photoshop, Lightroom or the file explorer). This information is kept with the document; ↶ undoes it.
0viadvt: How do I change the page size of a book I have already started?

In the page layout: File → “📐 Document size…” (or ⚙️ Document tab): page size (shared list or custom size), orientation, facing pages, margins, columns and bleed. “Apply the size to”: all pages, the page shown, or some pages (“2-5, 8”) — a page with its own size prints on a sheet of its size. The objects stay in place or are rescaled. ↶ (⌘Z) goes back; 💾 Save keeps everything.
13wfekd: How do I enlarge or shrink a photo, or add a margin around it?

In photo retouching: Image → “📏 Image size…”: width and height (pixels, %, cm, mm, inches), 🔗 keep proportions, resolution (dpi), resample or not and the method (bicubic smoother for enlarging, sharper for reducing, nearest neighbour to keep sharp pixels); “Fit to a size” takes a size from the shared list. Image → “⬚ Canvas size…” enlarges or crops the canvas around the photo: anchor on 9 points, coloured or transparent background, “Relative” to write what is added. The area appears around the photo and the final size is shown below; everything is applied when you save or export the image, and ↶ undoes it.
1obb4bn: How do I rotate a photo (on its side, upside down, mirrored)?

In photo retouching: Image → “🔄 Image rotation”: ↻ 90° clockwise, ↺ 90° anticlockwise, 180°, “Angle…” (a free angle: the canvas grows, transparent or coloured corners, and “✂️ Crop to remove empty corners”), “📐 Straighten the horizon” (draw a line along the horizon or a wall: the angle is suggested automatically), horizontal or vertical flip. The whole image turns as one: layers, masks, selection, texts, shapes, adjustment layers; width and height swap, the resolution stays. A single step: ↶ undoes everything. A phone photo still on its side offers “↻ Put it upright”. The commands can have their own shortcut (⚙️ Customise → retouching shortcuts). In quick retouching: ↺ ↻ in the left column and the Image menu. The original is kept: saving makes a new version.
10eap5f: How do I draw a house to the nearest centimetre?

In the plan, when drawing a wall (▬), a dimension (📏) or a free room: click the starting point then type the length on the keyboard (350, 3.5 m, 35 mm) and Enter; add the angle with @ (350 @ 90: upwards; 0 to the right, 180 to the left). With the room tool (⬚), type “420 x 350”. At the top left: the mouse position, the length and the angle of the current line. 🧲 Snap: grid (1 to 100 cm), corners, middles of walls, along walls, alignments (pink guide lines), angle step (90° to 1°). Alt: without snapping. The arrows move what is selected by 1 cm (⇧: one grid step). In Properties: length, angle and coordinates of walls, distances from a door or window to the ends of the wall, X and Y of furniture.
0zhkav3: How do I compare two periods of the house?

In the plan, the 👻 layer menu (next to the floors) offers “🕰 Previous period”, “🕰 Next period” or a period of your choice: the same floor, as it was, appears in sepia dotted lines under the one you are drawing (same transparency as the floors layer). Switch on “Legend: ― added · ┄ gone” in the Floor tab: walls added since are underlined in green, those that have gone are dotted, with their number at the top of the plan. In 3D, the “🕰 Other period” switch shows its walls transparently. With the 🕰 Year slider (🏠 House tab), “👻 Show the previous period as a ghost” always keeps the previous period underneath.
1hoj0pd: How do I make a mezzanine, a double-height living room or a stairwell?

The simplest: click the room (the living room) then, in Properties → “▨ Floor”, “🏗 Mezzanine open onto this room”: the floor above is added if missing, the mezzanine covers part of the room, the rest becomes a void with its railing, and a staircase arrives at the edge of the mezzanine. By hand: on the floor above, the ▨ “Void” tool (O key) and drag diagonally; or tick “No floor: void onto the floor below” on a room. The plan shows a hatched “VOID”, the floor below “double height” in dotted lines; in 3D the floor is cut open; during the visit you cannot walk into the void. The railing (wood, metal, glass, low wall or none, height of your choice) is placed automatically along the edges without a wall.
1oolz0q: How does a staircase cut through the floor above?

A staircase placed (straight, turning, spiral, miller’s ladder) automatically opens the stairwell in the floor of the storey above, with a railing around it except on the arrival side; on the floor above, its outline is drawn in dotted lines with “↓”. Its height follows the floor height plus the thickness of the floor (untick “Height: that of the floor…” to fix it). The panel gives the number of steps, their height and the tread, and warns if the staircase is too steep (Blondel’s rule, 2 h + g between 60 and 66 cm). “⇅ Reverse the direction of climb”, quarter turn to the left or right. For a house drawn before: “Open the stairwells of all staircases”. During the visit, going up you arrive just after the last step.
0wg1k45: How do I add dormers, an eyebrow dormer, roof windows (Velux) or gutters?

Floor tab → “🏠 Roof (3D view)”: “＋ Roof window”, “＋ Dormer” (two small slopes) or “＋ Shed dormer” (one slope rising towards the roof). For each: the slope (front or back), its place along the roof, its width and height; × removes it (↶ puts it back). The “Gutters and downpipes” box places them along the eaves. Everything is visible in the 3D view.
1dityqa: My house is L-shaped (or T, U): how do I get the right roof?

Floor tab → “🏠 Roof” → “One roof per wing”. The house is cut into rectangular wings according to its rooms; each one gets its own roof, at the same pitch: where two roofs meet, the valley is made automatically. Dormers then have a “Wing” choice.
1h8xs69: How do I make an attic with a sloping ceiling (and the Carrez law area)?

On the top floor, with a sloping roof: Floor tab → “🏠 Attic” → “Attic: the ceiling follows the slope of the roof”, then the height of the low walls (knee wall). The plan hatches the places under 1.80 m, the bottom of the screen gives the ceiling height under the mouse, each room shows its “Carrez law” area, and the 3D view, the section and the visit follow the slope.
08yre1j: How do I make a curved wall (round tower, apse, arched wall)?

Click the wall, then in Properties → “⌒ Curvature (sagitta)”: how far its middle bulges out from the straight line (+ on one side, − on the other; 0 = straight). The plan, 3D, the visit and the section follow the curve: the room’s floor too, the dimension gives the length of the arc and the sagitta, and doors and windows are placed on the curve.
0zoyeu0: How do I see the house in cross-section?

🏠 House tab → “🧰 House tools” → “✂ Draw the section line”, then two clicks on the plan (the red “A — A” line stays drawn). The section shows the floors, the hatched floor slabs, the cut walls with their doors and windows, the staircase, the roof and the heights; “🖨 Print…”, “⤓ Export as SVG” or “as PNG”.
1rj6noj: How do I know the living area of the house, room by room?

🏠 House tab → “🧰 House tools” → “📐 Areas per room”: each room, each floor and the whole house, on the ground and according to the Carrez law (only where you can stand up, 1.80 m and more). “🧾 In the spreadsheet” opens the same table in the Spreadsheet, with the totals as formulas.
1ya0sw0: How do I check that the house plan holds up?

🏠 House tab → “⚠️ Check the plan”: a list in the style of the Database check (🔴 impossible, 🟠 to check, 🟡 curious) — a door wider than its wall or placed on a wall that has gone, a window cut by the floor or under the slope of the roof, a room without a door, a staircase that is too steep (Blondel’s rule) or that does not cut through the floor, a void that opens onto nothing… A click on a line takes you to the object.
1nydnem: How do I see the house change over the years?

Create dated periods (🕰 The periods, 🏠 House tab); “🧰 House tools” then has a “🕰 The year” slider: as you drag it, the plan and the 3D view take the most recent period before that year. “▶ Watch it change” plays through them.
1pnxacn: How do I see who lived in a room during the visit?

Click the room → “🕯 Memories of the room” → “The people of the room” (the usual picker, main and secondary, a role on each badge: their bedroom, born here, servant…), then their years. During the visit (🚶 Visit), when you enter the room, a small card shows these people; a click opens their record, “✦” the memories of the room.
005exde: How do I prepare a guided tour of the house?

3D view → “🚶 Visit”: position yourself, look at what should be shown, then “📍 Stop here” and write what is said at that spot. Then, 🏠 House tab → “▶ Guided tour”: you move from one stop to the next by sliding, and the text is read aloud. “✎ The stops” to rewrite or reorder them; “⤓ Tour images” gives one image per stop and the texts, to drop into 🎬 Video editing to make a film.
0jiskqo: How do I compare an old photo with the house today?

During the visit, stand where the photo was taken, turn in the same direction, then “📷 Period photo here” and choose the photo (images window). It shows over the 3D view with a “Then ⟷ Now” slider. A 📷 marks it on the plan and in 3D; a click on it takes you back there.
1ugygoe: How do I show the hamlet, the farm and its outbuildings?

Draw each building as a house in the list (the barn, the bread oven, the house next door…), then in the main house: 🏠 House → “🏘 Buildings on the land…” → ＋ each building (picker), and set its offset and rotation. They appear in dotted lines on the plan and in 3D in their place. The census household number is noted in the same place.
1cqsetf: How do I send the house tour to someone who does not have the app?

🏠 House tab → “📤 Share the tour”: an .html file to send (e-mail, USB stick). It opens with a double-click in any browser, without the Internet: the house in 3D, its plans and the guided tour, read-only. It contains neither the inhabitants, nor the memories, nor the notes, nor the photos.
1i73iif: Can the house be shown in simple mode?

Yes: Settings → Accessibility → 🧓 Simple mode → “The big buttons” → “＋ Add a tile” → “🏠 The house”, then choose the house. In simple mode, this big button shows the house in 3D turning slowly, with big buttons to turn, move closer, change floor and listen to the guided tour — without being able to change anything.
1qkj9ou: How do I make the video of the house’s guided tour?

🏠 House tab → “🧰 House tools” → “🎬 Tour video…” (you need stops: 3D view → 🚶 Visit → 📍 Stop here). Choose the format (landscape, square, portrait) and the opening title: the camera glides from one stop to the next and the text of each stop is shown as a subtitle. “⤓ Export the video” gives an MP4 or WebM file (depending on the computer); “Also keep a copy in the media” stores it with your videos. “⤓ Tour images” is still there for Video editing.
0hqopom: Can I put a glass roof or an exit on a flat roof?

Yes: with a flat roof (Floor tab → 🏠 Roof → Shape “Flat”), the buttons become “＋ Glass roof”, “＋ Roof lantern” (a glazed peak) and “＋ Roof structure” (the small building of the exit onto the roof). Each one can be set (place, crosswise, width, depth) and is visible in 3D and in the section, like the dormers of a sloping roof.
121r3jf: How do I walk around the house in simple mode?

In simple mode’s “🏠 The house”, the “🚶 Walk around inside” button: big buttons ⬆ Forward, ⬇ Back, ⬅ ➡ Turn, ⏫ ⏬ change floor, and “🏠 See the whole house” to go out. No keyboard or mouse needed; nothing can be changed.
05xjjkj: How do I show who lived in a room, with their role?

Click the room → “🕯 Memories of the room” → “The people of the room”: the usual picker with the two areas “★ Main” and “☆ Secondary” and a role on each badge (their bedroom, born here, servant… or a free word; a person without a record is possible). The years are noted just below. Roles written before are kept as they are.
09532lj: How do I measure in the house’s 3D view?

3D view → “📏 Measure”, then two clicks on the house: the distance, the ground distance and the difference in height. “Dimensions” shows the length of each wall and the ceiling height; “Top”, “Front”, “Side” position the camera. The thickness of the floors between two storeys is set in the Floor tab.
16dnb32: How do I line up a floor with the one below or above?

At the top of the plan, next to the floors: “👻” chooses the floor shown transparently (below, above, both, or none). Its walls and the outline of its rooms are shown in dotted lines, brown for the one below, blue for the one above. The transparency is set in the Floor tab.
1y79otb: How do I move a room with its walls?

Drag the room: its walls (doors and windows included), its furniture and its texts follow; neighbouring walls attached at a corner stretch to stay joined. A wall shared with another room does not move. To move only the floor: ⇧ while dragging, or untick “🔗 Walls and furniture follow the room” in its properties.
0zye7ch: How do I get more furniture and objects in the house plan?

“Furniture” tab: 700 objects old and new, sorted by room (Bedroom, Living room, Dining room, Kitchen, Bathroom, Laundry room, Hall, Study, Children, Garage, Garden…) and by kind (Lighting, Decoration, Appliances, Music, Storage, Farm and animals, Structure). Type a word in “Search”: box bed, kneading trough, lamp, guitar, living room, bathroom, toy… (the number of objects found is shown; Esc empties the box). Click on the object: it is placed in the middle of the view. Each object has its real dimensions, its drawing seen from above and its 3D shape; its colour, second colour and material can be changed in “Properties”.
0dofgcd: Does the house plan get slow with a lot of furniture?
No: in 3D, each piece of furniture is grouped into a few volumes (one per material), even with 200 objects placed. If the 3D view stays slow on an old computer, untick “All floors” or use “Top”.
1izmis8: How do I create my own object for the house plan?

Furniture → “＋ Create an object”: “Start from an existing object” takes the size, shape and material of a piece from the catalogue (a linen cupboard, a dough bin…), then you change what you want: its name, its category (or a new one), its size in cm, its shape seen from above and in 3D, its material (oak, walnut, cast iron, copper, wicker, earthenware…), its colour and a second colour (legs, handles), its legs, its height from the floor, its direction, its rounded corners, its doors and drawers, its period, and if you like a photo seen from above (from the computer or “🖼️ A photo from the media”). The preview shows the object in 2D and 3D. It is kept for all your houses, in its category and in “My objects”; ✎ to edit or delete it.
1hfgf0o: How do I put an image in a frame or on a painting in the house (recreate a painter’s studio)?

Choose the frame, the painting, the canvas, the easel, the poster, the mirror or the gallery wall: in its settings, “🖼 Image” section, “🖼 Change” opens the window of images from your media (filtered on the house’s first inhabitant). You can also drag an image from the computer straight onto the object, in the plan or in the 3D view: it goes into the media and is placed on it. A memory attached to the object can serve as the image. Settings: fill, fit or centre, drag and zoom in the preview to crop, rotate by 90°, mat and frame (colour, width). Gallery wall: one image per frame (badges 1 to 6). The house only keeps the media number and its settings; if the image no longer exists, a plain canvas replaces it.
1yo63kv: What trade and workshop objects are there in the house plan?

Furniture → “Trades, workshop”: more than 100 objects sorted by trade — painter (studio, field and table easels, stretched canvases from size 6 F to 100 F, stacked canvases, canvas racks, palette, paint box, side table, model’s platform), sculptor, blacksmith and farrier, joiner and cabinet-maker, cooper, wheelwright, shoemaker, tailor and seamstress, weaver, potter, baker, butcher, grocer, apothecary, clockmaker, printer, bookbinder, photographer, schoolteacher, doctor and midwife, barber, miller, winegrower, beekeeper, washerwoman, lacemaker, instrument maker, notary and town hall, post office, miner, fisherman, sailor, rural policeman. Look for the trade (“baker”, “clockmaker”…) in the Furniture search box.
1jnokgh: How do I find antique furniture and objects from the past?

Furniture → tick “🕰 Antique only”: only furniture and things from the past remain (linen cupboard, dough bin, longcase clock, Breton dresser, settle chest, box bed, wooden cradle, spinning wheel, butter churn, oil lamp, Godin stove, andirons, mantelpiece, treadle sewing machine, school bench…), in each category and in the search. Untick to see everything again.
1jwgvjl: How do I change the material, the legs or the second colour of a piece of furniture already placed?

Click on the furniture → Properties → “🎨 Material, legs, details”: the material (oak, walnut, cherry, cast iron, copper, stone, marble, wicker, straw, earthenware, fabric…), a second colour (legs, handles, trims), legs (straight, turned, ball, glides, castors), rounded corners, the number of doors and drawers (wardrobes, sideboards, chests of drawers) and its period. The 3D view follows straight away.
04qegc2: How do I link a house to people or censuses?

In the house, “House” tab: “＋ An inhabitant…” for a person, “＋ A census…” for one or more censuses (tick “Also add the people of the household” to make them inhabitants in one go). At the top of the tab, “🔗 Linked to” shows everything that is linked; a click opens the record. In Lists → “🏠 Family houses”, “Linked to” shows it too (▦ Cards or ☰ Table).
1170g30: How do I add a house to a census?

Open the census (the person’s record → Censuses → ✎). At the bottom, “🏠 House”: choose the house and its period, then “🔗 Link” (it is saved straight away), or “＋ New house” to draw it, already linked. “↗ Open the house” opens it directly at the period of this census.
1o2vsxl: Where can I see a person’s houses?

On their record, the “🏠 Houses” block: the houses where they are an inhabitant, linked to a room, or in a linked census, with their image, the period and “↗ Open”. It can be arranged like the other blocks (Settings → Appearance → record blocks).
0q311tg: How do I see the house change over the years?

In the house, “🕰 Periods” (at the top): the house you drew becomes the first period (a name, a year or a date), and “＋ New period (copy of this one)” makes a copy at another date (1900, 1936…) that you change: a room added, a wall knocked down, other furniture, another roof. ‹ › or the menu at the top move from one period to another, in 2D as in 3D; “▶” plays them in date order. House tab → “🕰 The periods”: ✎ to rename, change the date or link the period to a census, × to delete it.
0z17m7s: How do I link a period of the house to a census?
House tab → “📋 The censuses”: the menu next to each census chooses its period (or ✎ on the period → “Linked to the census”). From the census window, “↗ Open the house” then opens it at that period.
0gat62m: How do I download free, royalty-free 3D furniture?

Furniture → “📦 Online library”: models from Poly Haven, royalty-free (CC0), can be searched and imported in one click. “ZIP pack” tab: download a CC0 pack (Kenney, Quaternius…) from the author’s site, choose the .zip file and tick the models to keep. They arrive in “My objects”, with their licence, author and source (✎ to see them).
097ftg6: How do I hide or arrange the furniture categories and objects?
Furniture → “⚙️ Arrange”: tick what you want to see and arrange the categories with ↑ ↓, then the objects in each category. “↺ Reset to default” goes back to the original order.
0hu3mtu: How do I make a map to the right scale, without distorting it?

Lists → Editing tools → 🗺️ Map → “＋ New map”: choose the size, then locate the map (the place and the width covered): the scale is then correct. The “Scale grid” (100 m, 1 km… squares, never printed) helps place each thing in its place, and a selected object shows its real length or area.
1a2yo92: What are “Coat of arms mode” and “Map mode” at the top of the drawing for?
Tick them to show on the right the coat of arms or map tab and menu; unticked, they stay hidden to keep the editor simple.
1u4qyh8: How do I grey out (or not) the rows I have unticked in lists to arrange?

Settings → “Menus, column and lists” → Column tab → “👁 Hidden rows in lists to arrange”: “Leave them as they are”, or “Grey them out” with the level of grey you want. It applies to all the lists where you tick what is shown (menus, lists, Reorder, Customise…).
1wf5aqp: How do I arrange the lists (or the Settings pages) into groups?

At the bottom of the left column, “Reorder”: tick or untick “Arrange in groups”. In groups: arrange, rename, create or delete groups, move a list to another group, choose whether groups are open or closed. As a single list: arrange with ↑ ↓. Each way keeps its settings, you find them again when switching. “My lists” always stay at the bottom, apart: they can only be arranged among themselves. The same setting is in Settings → “Menus, column and lists” → “Lists” tab (for Lists, “Reorder” takes you straight there).
0e2ubfo: How do I put a drawing into a group or a layer?
Layers tab: drag the row onto the group (it turns blue); or choose the object then “📁 Put into…”. Double-click on a name to rename it.
0xm3r6d: How do I arrange or hide the buttons of the House tool, or give it my shortcuts?

In the tool, “⚙️ Customise” (at the top), or Settings → “Editing, retouching, page layout and sound” → “🏠 House (plan and 3D)” editor: top bar, tools in the left column, 3D view bar and panel tabs, to tick and arrange, to keep as named sets; and below, your keyboard shortcuts for each command.
1ak9zs8: Can “Ask a question” calculate, not just list?

Yes (Research → Ask a question in French). Besides lists (“Which ancestors were bakers in Lille before 1850?”), it answers questions that need a calculation: the relationship between two people (“What is the relationship between Jean Dupont and Marie Durand?” → second cousins, cousin once removed, common ancestors, civil degree); records (who lived longest, died youngest, largest family, married youngest or latest, biggest age gap between spouses, oldest ancestor); averages (age at marriage, at death, at first child, children per couple); the most frequent (first names, surnames, occupations, communes, months and seasons); one person (“When was… born”, “Where did… die”, “How old was… at their marriage”, “How old would… be today”); periods (“Who lived through the Great War?”, “Who was 20 in 1914?”, “Who was alive in 1900?”); counts (“How many ancestors do I have?”, by generation). You can add “men”, “women”, “ancestors”, “in the 19th century”… The list of examples is under the box: “And also questions that need a calculation”. The questions are typed in French.
1bfm6tu: Does the app recognise faces in photos?

Yes, on your computer only: Lists → Media → “👤 Faces” (this tool brings together the old “Face detection” and “Who is who?”). Step ① Find the faces: choose the photos, then “🔍 Analyse”; the list “Photos with faces to name” opens each photo in the viewer with the faces framed (click on a frame to say who it is). Step ② Who is it?: first identify a few faces by hand, at least once per person; “💡 Suggestions” then says “this is probably Marie Martin” (very likely or likely, with the percentage of likeness): ✓ Yes, Someone else… or Ignore, or accept them all at once for the very likely ones; “👥 Grouped unknowns”: faces that look alike from one photo to another, to name in one go. Each confirmed face becomes an ordinary identification on the photo; “↶ Undo” removes it. The model (≈ 13 MB) is downloaded once, checked by its fingerprint; the photos are not sent anywhere.
1j6dsup: How do I read a ten-year index with the app?

Lists → Record indexes (or Research → Archive record index) → “📑 Read a ten-year index”. Five steps: ① the photo of the index (media window), the commune, the period (“1853-1862”) and the kind of records; ② drag the blue lines between the columns (Surname, First names, Date, Kind of record…) or take a known template, then “↧ Find the rows”; ③ the app reads each row on this computer (printed index), or with the handwriting reader if it is installed; otherwise you type it in by hand, with the row’s strip in front of you; ④ you check the grid, with the image alongside (uncertain cells are in yellow, dates without a year take the one from the row before, a date outside the period is flagged); ⑤ the “Ten-year index” record index is created (with “↶ Undo”), then the app suggests the records: 🔗 Link or ＋ Create the record (with the birth or death).
06gg7ux: The reading engine does not load: can I still index my table?

Yes. In “📑 Read a ten-year index”, at step ③, “✍ Type the rows by hand”: a quick grid (Enter or ↓ for the next row), with the strip of each row of the image above. The engine (printed text) is downloaded once with the Internet; the handwriting reader is installed in Settings → Handwriting recognition.
1tmttas: How do I find a photo in the database from another one (reverse search)?

“🔍 Search for a similar image”: in the viewer (button under the photo), in the ⋯ or right-click of a thumbnail in Lists → Media, or at the top of Media. Start from a photo in the database, or drop / paste (⌘V) an image from your computer: it is only used for searching, it does not go into the media. The results are sorted: ＝ identical (the same file), ≈ very close (resized, re-saved, retouched, another format), ⬚ cropped / zoomed (a piece of the photo, framed in blue in the preview), ～ similar (same scene, another shot), with the percentage. “See” puts the two images side by side; “🔍 Compare two photos” opens the comparison tool. Everything is calculated on this computer: the app keeps a “fingerprint” of each photo (calculated in the background, in small batches; if you close, it resumes where it left off; a retouched or rotated photo is recalculated by itself).
1sydrst: How do I find duplicate photos, even retouched or cropped?

Lists → Media → “👯 Duplicate images” (it replaces the old “Duplicate search” and also finds duplicate sounds and PDFs). The groups are sorted into Perfect (the same file), Retouched, Cropped / zoomed, Resized and Other format; “Sensitivity” suggests more or less different photos. In each group, the largest is suggested as “★ Kept” (“★ Keep” to choose another), then “👯 Keep ★ and merge”: its links gather those of the others (records, events, labels, albums, collections, investigations, portrait, face areas put back in the right place). The others go “🗑 To the bin” (the file stays on the disk) or “🗂 As versions” of the kept photo. “↶ Undo” puts everything back as before, and the “🗑 Duplicates bin” lets you “↶ Restore” a merge later. “🙈 Not a duplicate” is remembered (“🙈 Not duplicates” to go back on it).
1hffexp: How do I compare two photos to see if it is the same person?

“🔍 Compare two photos”: from the viewer (“🔍 Compare with…”), Lists → Media, a record’s Media block (🔍), or Comparison → Images. The two photos side by side, as a fade (slider) or as a curtain, with the same zoom; “✨ Find the eyes automatically” (face model, on this computer) or “👁 Place the eyes” (two clicks per photo) brings the two faces to the same size; black and white, contrast, notes. The calculated likeness stays cautious: “this is not proof” (age, light, family resemblance…). “💾 Save” keeps the comparison, linked to the two photos and the people: Lists → Editing tools → 🔍 Compare two photos.
1343y1n: How does the 👤 Faces tool work?

Lists → Media → “👤 Faces”. Two tabs: ① Find the faces (the app spots the faces in the chosen photos and calculates their “fingerprint”) and ② Who is it? (it suggests a name based on faces already identified). Start small: the app picks the lightest batch automatically, often “Photos marked with faces” (the person’s photo, a record’s portrait, faces already identified, “portrait” or “face” label). You can also take the photos shown in the Media list (with your search), those of a person, a label, an album or a folder, a period (“between 1900 and 1950”), the N most recent, or all. “Skip photos already analysed” avoids redoing the work.
164it19: Face analysis takes a long time: can I pause or stop it?

Yes. The analysis runs separately, without freezing the app: you can keep clicking meanwhile. The bar shows how many photos are done, the time per photo and the estimated time remaining. “⏸ Pause” stops after the current photo, “▶ Resume” starts again; “■ Stop” cuts straight away. Progress is kept: even after closing the window, “▶ Resume” starts again where you stopped. An unreadable photo, or one that takes much longer than the others (at least a minute and a half), is skipped and noted, without blocking the others; “↻ Retry the skipped photos” does them again.
0alw4li: DNA: how do I group my matches and guess where to place a cousin?

DNA tab → “🔗 Automatic groups”: matches that match each other (shared matches noted or imported, overlapping segments) form clusters, shown in a coloured matrix; each cluster gets its frequent names and places, its side, and the common ancestral couple (certain if a match is already linked to a record, probable from the names in the tree). One click sorts them into groups. “📍 Place a cousin”: for a match (or cM typed by hand), the possible relationships (Shared cM Project) then the couples in your tree they probably descend from, with a percentage and the clues (side, names, places, cluster, age); “Keep” notes it in the match. The test must be linked to the record of the tested person. It is a lead, never a proof.
1wyd47l: On which sites should I look for an ancestor? (🌍 Where to look?)

On the record, the “🌍 Where to look?” block (or ⋯ → “🌍 Where to look?”, or Research → Type of research → “🌍 Where to look?”) suggests the sites to consult, the most useful first, according to their places (country, department), their period, their life (soldier → Mémoire des hommes and military registers, sailor → maritime register, emigrant → Ellis Island, Castle Garden, notary or inheritance → Minutier central…) and what is missing (unknown birth → the registers of their commune…). Each line says why; “↗ Search” opens the site in your browser with their name already filled in. “✓ Already searched” notes the result (Found, Nothing found, To review) in the Research log; ⋯ → “＋ Make it a lead” adds it to their investigation. “Free only” hides paid sites (the same setting as in Online archives). Any new site added to “Search the Internet” is taken into account automatically.
0cqyhs2: What is a “brick wall” and how do I work on it?

An ancestor where you are stuck: one or both of their parents are unknown. Research → Type of research → “🧩 Brick walls” lists them automatically, from the nearest generation to the most distant (Sosa), along with those you marked by hand (record → ⋯ → “🧱 I’m stuck here”, or “＋ Add a wall…”). “Open” shows what has already been searched (Log, letters, leads), the sites to try (🌍 Where to look?), the clues in your database (same name, born 20 to 50 years earlier; godparents and witnesses; household in a census; DNA) and a note. The status (To search, In progress, Solved, Abandoned) changes in one click, with “↶ Undo”; when the parents arrive in the database, the wall turns “Solved” by itself, with a well done. The “🧩 Brick walls” widget shows them on the dashboard, and “🗓 My research week” suggests one per week.
11bwjmr: How do I prove that an ancestor really is the son (or daughter) of someone? (⚖️ Proof file)

Open a proof file: on the record, ⋯ → “⚖️ Proof file…” (choose the question: a parent, a couple, a date, a place, “same person as…”), or click the 🛡 badge next to a parent, or right-click on a box or a line of a tree in Charts. In the file: the question, the clues 👍 for and 👎 against (a text, the source or citation chosen in the picker, the kind of clue: direct, indirect or negative, the quality of the source: original, derivative or authored), the searches done (linked to the Research log), the conflicts between sources and how you resolve them, your conclusion and your level of certainty (proved, probable, possible, disproved, to check). Everything is saved by itself; a removed line comes back with “↶ Undo”. 🖨 Print and “📝 In the word processor” turn it into a document. All the files: Lists → Research and organisation → “⚖️ Proof files”.
1u87dl3: What is the “proof standard” the proof file talks about?

The method of professional genealogists, in 5 steps: search widely (and note what you did not find), cite the source of each clue, weigh each clue (a record written on the day itself is worth more than a memory), explain the conflicts, write your conclusion. The proof file follows these 5 steps; “💡 How to reason?” recalls them in the window.
0sxj84x: What does the small 🛡 badge (Proved, Probable, Assumed, No source) next to the parents mean?

It is the strength of the parent-child link, calculated by the app without changing anything in your database. In order: the proof file for this link if it has a conclusion; otherwise your choice by hand; otherwise the sources. Proved: a birth, baptism or marriage record of the child is cited and it names the parent (same source on the parent’s record, or their name written in the citation). Probable: a source names the parent elsewhere, or the birth record is cited without showing that it names this parent, or the citation is marked “secondary source”. Assumed: sources about the child, but none about this link (or marked unreliable, or a “doubtful” date). No source: nothing cited. Click the badge to see why, open the file or choose the level by hand (↶ Undo).
0hc3e86: How do I see the weak links in my tree? (🛡 Strength view, Weak branches)

In Charts, on the ancestor tree, the descendant tree or the hourglass, switch on “🛡 Strength view”: each line takes the colour and thickness of its level (legend at the top; thick green = proved, blue = probable, yellow dashes = assumed, grey dots = no source, red = disproved). Lists → Research and organisation → “🛡 Weak branches” lists your Sosa ancestors whose link is assumed, without a source or disproved, from the nearest to the most distant, with “⚖️ File” and “🌍 Where to look?”. Also: the “🛡 Weak branches” widget and, each week, a “🛡 Link to strengthen” in “My research week”.
1s6cov5: Where can I see everything I have already searched, so as not to search the same place twice?

Research → Type of research → “🗓 Research log” (the same log is in Lists → Archives and sources). Everything that has been searched, from the most recent to the oldest: record indexes, shelfmarks from archive visits done, investigation leads, communes of search sweeps, requests (records to order). Each line says where (service, shelfmark, commune, years), when, and the result (Found, Nothing found, Partly). The top bar searches for a shelfmark, a commune or a name, and filters by kind, result, person, archive service or commune; “List | Cards”, sort, “⤓ Export as CSV”. A click opens the item in its tool.
1pxn65n: How do I note the result of a record index and who I did it for?

Research → Archive record index → ✎ Edit (or ＋ Add a record index). “Result”: Found (green badge), Nothing found (grey) or Partly (yellow), in addition to the state and the free text. “People searched for”: choose the records of the people for whom you opened this register (several possible) — they stay separate from the people noted in it. The record index then appears in the “🔍 Already searched” block of their record.
19uo3in: What does “⚠️ Already in your tracking” mean when I type a shelfmark?

While you fill in a record index, a request (records to order) or an archive visit shelfmark, the app checks whether you have already searched in the same place: the same shelfmark (in the same service), or the same archive service + the same commune + the same type of record over overlapping years. If so, the message says what, with the result and the date (“Nothing found, on 12 March 2025”) and “↗ Open”. You can still save.
1r8nn9t: After a visit to the archives, how do I note what I found?

Lists → Archive visit planner → on the mission sheet, “✓ Done on…”: give the day of the visit. The sheet moves to the “✓ Visits done” tab (the past stays readable). For each shelfmark, choose the result (Found, Nothing found, Partly, Not consulted); “Edit” adds a note (“Record no. 12, image 34”). “＋ Create the record index” creates the shelfmark’s record index and links it (or links an existing record index with the picker in “Edit”). Each shelfmark goes into the Research log.
0h2cg4j: How do I sort my documents by archive service (departmental archives, municipal archives, notaries…)?

Lists → Archives and sources → “🏛 Archive services” → “＋ New service” (you can start from a department’s Departmental Archives: name, acronym and website fill in). On the service’s record: address, opening hours, website, series (“3 E — Notaries”), and “✓ Already consulted there”: all your record indexes, visits done and requests made at this service, sorted by series. In a source’s window and in a media item’s window, “🏛 Archive service” is chosen with the picker, with the series and the shelfmark. If you wrote a service by hand in your research (“AD 19”), the list offers to create its record; its other names (“AD Corrèze”…) are noted on the record.
19nbppx: How do I get a ready-made citation of a source, in Evidence Explained or Chicago style or for a forum?

On the record, next to each source (and each source of an event), “❝”: the same source written in four styles — classic French, Evidence Explained, Chicago, Geneanet / forum —, as a note and as a bibliography entry, each with “📋 Copy”. “⭐ My style” puts it first everywhere. “❝” at the top of the “Sources & citations” block gives all the record’s citations in one style: “📋 Copy all”, “⤓ Export as text”, “🖨 Print”. In a page layout, Text → “📚 Cite a source” has a “Style” menu (the note and the bibliography are written in that style); the research report (Settings → Exports) ends with the bibliography in your style.
0j67obh: How do I compare two hypotheses (“born in Naves or in Tulle?”) and update the record?

On the record, the “⚖️ Hypotheses” block → “＋ New hypothesis”: the question, the event concerned and the kind (Place, Date…). Then “⚖️ Compare”: one column per answer (the record’s value is already there; “＋ Another answer” adds a place, a date or a text). In each column, “👍 For” and “👎 Against”: add a source, a media item or a record index with the picker (or write the evidence), and give it a weight (weak, medium, strong). The column with the highest total (for − against) is “Leading”. “✓ Keep …” changes the place or the date of the event on the record and confirms the hypothesis; “↶ Undo” puts everything back as before. All hypotheses: Settings → Hypotheses.
034q1vu: On a person’s record, where can I see what has already been searched for them?

The “🔍 Already searched” block: the record indexes in which they are searched for or noted, the shelfmarks of visits done that concern them, the leads of their investigations, their search sweeps and the related requests — where, when, the shelfmark and the result, with “↗ Open”. “🗓 Log” opens the whole log filtered on them. The block can be arranged, set and hidden like the others (Settings → Appearance → record blocks).
0yiw7hv: What is missing from my genealogy, and where should I look for it?

Research → Type of research → “🔍 What’s missing?”. For each ancestor in the line (up to 12 generations): the missing birth, marriage, death or parents, but also censuses (1836-1936), the military register (men born from 1847 to 1921), the estate and the marriage contract; with the commune, the window of years, the archive service (Departmental Archives of such-and-such department, according to the place) and the series to consult according to the period: parish registers before 1792, civil registration and ten-year indexes afterwards, notaries (3 E), registration (3 Q), recruitment (1 R), censuses (6 M). Sort by archive service, commune, ancestor or kind of record; “📌 To tracking” adds the search “to do” in the Archive record index, and what is already there is shown. “🖨 Print” makes the list for a visit to the archives.
1jyz4e7: How do I extract an ancestor’s signature or create a monogram, a wax seal?

Lists → Editing tools → “🔤 Signatures and seals”. ✍️ Choose the image of a record (media or computer), frame the signature by dragging: yellowed paper, stains and the lines of the register disappear (threshold set automatically, to fine-tune), the ink becomes a clean vector line, in its original colour or a chosen ink; the cut-out image (transparent background) can also go into the person’s media. 🔏 For a monogram: interlaced initials (copperplate, round hand, Gothic, Roman capitals, Didot), in a wax seal, an ink stamp, a medallion, a shield, a lozenge or a bookplate, with a legend going around it (“MARTIN FAMILY · TULLE 1832”). Everything opens in the vector drawing to be retouched, printed or exported.
0p13fu7: Page layout: how do I see whether text overflows and make it continue in another box?

At the bottom of the page layout, an indicator: 🟢 “No errors”, or 🔴 with the number of errors (text overflowing its box, fact contradicted by the records). It updates by itself while you write; a click opens the detailed check with “Go” for each problem. A box whose text overflows has a small red + at the bottom right: click it, then click the text box that should receive the rest (on any page) — the text continues there, as in InDesign. Also: Object → “➜ Thread the text box to another…”, “⤵ Flow the text onto new pages” and “Break the thread”. Esc cancels.
01pwhxu: Page layout: is the text of a book checked against the records?

Yes. When a text names a person in the database (“Jean MARTIN, born on 28 August 1923 in Tulle”), the date and place of birth, baptism, death, burial or marriage are compared with their record. A different date counts as an error (🔴), a different place (even without a date: “born in Tulle” while the record says Naves) or a name carried by several records as “to check” (🟠), and a fact missing from the record is pointed out so you can add it. “He” or “she” refer to the person named just before; the “date Birth — place” lines of a record page refer to the name in the title. Nothing is changed automatically: you correct the text or the record. The details are in File → “✅ Check before printing” (or a click on the indicator).
0o9li01: How do I write text that follows a circle or a curve?

Vector drawing → Object → “➰ Text on a curve…”: circle, arc, wave, the chosen path, or the templates “motto around a seal” and “name on a ribbon”. In Properties → Text: position on the path, offset, side (underneath to write the right way round at the bottom of a circle), spread the letters. The shape is changed with Direct selection (A).
0qva33z: How do I print a coat of arms in black and white (heraldic hatching)?

Coat of arms mode → “🖨 Heraldic hatching”: or = dots, argent = plain, gules = vertical lines, azure = horizontal, vert = diagonals from dexter, sable = cross-hatching, purpure = diagonals from sinister. “Back to colour” cancels; “＋ Legend” adds the table of hatchings.
1bhpxrz: How do I make a gradient with several colours or hatching in a drawing?
Properties → Colour → Kind of fill: linear or radial gradient (“＋ Add a colour”, position of each), or Pattern (hatching, dots, grid, cross-hatching, chequerboard).
1mp2r0m: Where can I find fleurons, frames, corners, drop caps for a drawing?
The “Ornaments” tab of the vector drawing: 44 old ornaments with search and categories; click to place in the centre, or drag onto the drawing. The Colour palette recolours them.
1220iha: How do I align or distribute objects in a drawing?

Properties → Position and size: six alignment buttons and two to distribute, relative to the selection or to the artboard (the page, the panel). When moving, enlarging or drawing, pink lines snap to edges and centres; hold ⌘ (or Ctrl) to do without.
1rqr1y0: How do I make a double-sided or folded announcement card, with its envelope?

Announcement window → Folding (double-sided, folded in 2, 3 or 4 panels) and “✉️ Matching envelope” (size chosen automatically or as you like, recipient taken from the people, sender). In the drawing, the pink lines are the folds. ⤓ Export → PDF (one page per side) or “🗞 Double-sided on A4” (sides placed, crop and fold marks).
0ylhwgp: Do I need to click “Save” in Settings?

No: each change is saved straight away. “✓ Saved” appears to the right of the page title, and a message at the bottom left offers “↶ Undo” to go back on the last change. “↺ Reset to default”, always to the right of the title, puts back the original settings (and “↶ Undo” brings yours back).
1fg8lzm: Where have the other buttons at the top of a page gone?

At the top of each page: the main button in blue, two others at most, then “⋯” which opens the rest (Assemble photos, Retouch, Export…), and ⭐ to add it to your shortcuts. The small blue text above the title says where you are (e.g. “Lists · Media and documents”); the number of items is written under the search bar.
1xbok4k: How do I see a list as thumbnails?

At the top of the list, “List | Cards”: in “Cards”, each item has the same thumbnail everywhere (image, name, two useful lines, badges, date), with “Open” and “⋯” for Edit, Rename, Duplicate or Delete. The choice is remembered for each list.
17hl29n: How do I keep, export or import a saved setting?

In a “💾 Saved settings” frame (click its title to open it): “＋ Save the current settings”, a name, then Enter. Each setting has “Apply” and a ⋯ menu: replace with the current settings, rename, duplicate, ⤓ export (lcnda-reglage-….json file), delete (with “↶ Undo”). On the other computer, “⤒ Import” at the bottom of the frame. A file from another tool is refused with a message; if the name already exists, the app asks for another one.
0aj1k5d: How do I export a drawing, a page layout or a plan?

“⤓ Export ▾” at the top of the tool always opens the same window: PDF, PNG, JPG, SVG, Print, the tool’s file (to reopen later), with the quality, bleed and crop marks, the file name and a copy in the media.
1iqb245: How do I put a family tree in my book?

In the page layout: Object → “🌳 Insert a family tree”. Choose the person, the shape (ancestors, descendants, hourglass or fan), the number of generations and the style of the boxes. The tree follows your database: it remakes itself on opening, or with File → “↻ Update the dynamic objects”.
0zvy0zb: How do I add a footnote or cite a source in a book?

Double-click in a text, place the cursor, then Text → “¹ Note” or “📚 Cite a source” (“AD Corrèze, 3 E 123, f° 12”). The numbers put themselves back in order. Document → Footnotes: at the bottom of the box or at the end of the chapter. Object → “Insert the bibliography” lists the sources cited.
1pnnhr9: How do I make an index of places or occupations?

In the page layout: Object → “📍 Insert an index of places” or “🔨 … of occupations”. The index looks for the places and occupations of your database in the text and notes the pages. You can also mark a word with the “Place to index” or “Occupation to index” style.
1t28z5h: How do I make an e-book (ePub)?
Page layout → ⤓ Export → “📱 ePub”. The file opens in Books, Kobo or Calibre, with the cover, the table of contents, the images and the notes.
0b8tll8: How do I get a cousin to proofread my book?

Choose some words or an object, then Review → “💬 Comment” or “✎ Suggest”. To send it: ⤓ Export → “💬 Review”. Your cousin imports the file into 📐 Page layout, comments and sends you theirs back; you do Review → “⤒ Import their comments”. Suggestions are accepted or refused in one click. The “📝 Annotated PDF” can be read on paper.
1sy4v1p: What does the red indicator of the page layout check?

Overflowing texts, dates and places that contradict the records, impossible dates (30 February), impossible or wrong ages (“died at 140”), misspelt names (“Jean MARTAIN” → MARTIN?), places unknown to your database and wrong Sosa numbers. Click the indicator to see the details.
0u65yt7: How does the app write a person’s biography?

On the record, the “📖 Biography” block writes their life in French from what the record contains (“Jean naît le 3 mai 1832 à Tulle, fils de…”), without inventing anything, in the feminine or masculine, with “vers 1784” for an approximate date. Choose the length (Short, Normal, Detailed), the tone (Neutral, Warm) and, in “⚙️ What is included”, the occupations, the witnesses, the censuses and the sources (in brackets or as notes). “✎ Edit” then “💾 Keep my version”: your version is used everywhere (family book, page layout with the {biographie} field). “↻ Regenerate” shows what has changed (green: added, red struck through: removed). “Place in ▾” puts it into a Note, a book or a presentation.
1982b6d: How do I tell “a day in the life” of an ancestor (⏳)?

On their record, ⋯ → “⏳ A day in their life…” (or, in the “📖 Biography” block, the “⏳ A day…” button). Choose a day of their life (an event, or the shortcuts Birth, Marriage, Death…) or “✎ Another date” (“7 May 1925”, “12 Thermidor Year II”).
