The app writes a short story in French using only its own rules, without the Internet: their age, their family that day, their village (village page, recorded population, church, your notes), their occupation (dictionary of old occupations), the day of the week, the saint of the day, the Republican date, the weather of the past if the data is installed, the big events of the year and, only when a reliable figure exists, a price or a wage from the table supplied with the app. Each sentence has its mark: ✓ from the record (with “↗ See the event”), 📚 reference (source cited in the Landmarks), 💭 imagined (in italics); the “No imagined sentences” switch removes them. Then: 📋 Copy, 📝 In the word processor, 🔊 Read aloud, “Place in ▾” (page layout, media, end of their biography, with ↶ Undo). A confidential record does not leave the app; for a living person, the window says so.
1179git: What was happening in the world during my ancestor’s life?

On the record, the “🌍 The world around” block puts their life next to the major events in France and the world (wars, epidemics, laws, inventions, regimes, mostly 1500–1960) with their age: “Jean is 38 when the war of 1870 begins”. Local events (department, commune) only appear if they lived there. “＋ Add a local event” for a flood, a fire, a village fête. The whole list and the source of each event: Lists → History → “🌍 The world around”. The Timeline shows them too (“Historical timeline” box).
1yhfl6w: What did a clog-maker, a day labourer, a weaver do?

On the record, click the occupation (Identity → “Occupation / activity”, it has a 🛠️): the occupation’s page opens — what they did, their tools, the old words, the ancestors who practised it (list, map, timeline) and the images in your database about it. “✎ Complete the page”, “＋ Add images” or “📒 Make it a Note” to enrich it. The complete dictionary (more than 500 occupations with their spelling variants): Lists → People and families → “🛠️ Old occupations”.
17ct0f5: How do I see my ancestors’ occupations in a tree (🧬 Occupation tree)?

Charts → “Occupation tree” (or, on a record, ⋯ → “🧬 Occupation tree”; or ⌘K “occupations”). Choose the person in the “Person” box, then “⬆ Ancestors” or “⬇ Descendants” and the number of generations. Each box shows their occupations (record, “Occupation” events, censuses), with a colour per broad sector: agriculture, crafts, industry, trade, transport, services, army, clergy, liberal professions… (the classification comes from the dictionary of old occupations). A thick coloured line and “＝ same occupation”: the child took over their parent’s occupation; “⇄ other occupation”: they changed; dotted lines: one of the two has no occupation recorded. At the top: filter by sector (badges with the number) or search for an occupation; “🔒 Without living people or confidential records” to show or print. At the bottom: the legend and “Passing on the occupation” — the share of sons who took over their father’s occupation (and of daughters their mother’s), by century, in the tree and in your whole database. A click on a box opens the record. “⤓ Export”: PDF, PNG, JPG, SVG or 🖨 Print.
1a27k00: How do I see all the places of a person’s life on an animated map (🗺 Life map)?

On the record: ⋯ → “🗺 Map of their life”; or Map → left column → “🗺 Life map” (in Route mode: “▶ Animated life map”); or ⌘K “life map”. Their events (birth, baptism, marriages, residences, occupations, death…), their censuses, their journeys, their placements, their military service and their schools (🎓 block) become numbered stages, in date order, on a map background supplied with the app (no Internet needed). ▶ starts playback (⏸ to stop, speed 🐢 / Normal / 🐇), ◀ ▶ move from one stage to the next, ⤢ shows the whole life; the timeline at the bottom and the list on the right are clickable. Places without a position are listed separately (open the place and give its position so that it comes onto the map). “👪 With the family” adds the spouse and the children (in pink and green). “🎬 Export as video” makes an MP4 or WebM video of the stages, with a copy in the media if you like; living people and confidential records are never in it. “📊 Keep as a diagram” stores it in My diagrams (the “Storytelling map”).
0g2e3eg: How do I tell a life story as a slideshow?

On the record, click ✨ (or Presentation and slideshow → “✨ Life story”). Choose the person, the length, the style, the photos and music if you like. The slideshow prepares itself from the record: birth on a map, baptism, marriage, children, occupations, censuses, moves, events of the time, death, grave, descendants. Missing information does not produce a slide. Everything can be changed afterwards.
0mo41wn: Reminders for you, for example the sources of the story. They are not visible during playback and become the speaker’s notes in a presentation.
033q8de: How do I export a slideshow, a sound or a video edit?
“⤓ Export ▾” at the top: a single window for all formats (video, images, PDF, MP3, WAV…). Tick “Also keep a copy in the media” to keep it in the app.
00jhxfl: How do I drag a file into a tool?

Drag (or paste with ⌘V) a photo or a sound onto the slideshow, the presentation, the video edit, the sound waveform, the image of a record, the drawing or the page layout: it goes into the media and is placed in the tool.
1hzlqe6: How do I export a table, a diagram or a chart?
Click “⤓ Export”: a single window offers PDF, PNG or JPG image, SVG (diagrams), Print, or the tool’s file. Choose the quality and the file name, and tick “Also keep a copy in the media”.
00vr1dj: Why can’t I make a PNG image of a chart?
The browser (Chrome, Edge, the app) refuses to turn an app chart into an image. Choose “PDF” in the export window: the file is sharp, to print or to send.
0yhle0p: Can I drag files instead of choosing them?

Yes: in “Add media”, on a table, an investigation, the photos of a collection, the favourite image on the dashboard, the file areas of records and in the tools (drawing, page layout, retouching, slideshow, video editing). The area turns blue on hover; you can also paste (⌘V). A .csv file dragged onto a collection’s spreadsheet fills the cells.
0bm9s62: How do I choose a font?
The “Aa All fonts…” button opens a single list: search, recent fonts at the top, fonts from the app and from the computer, each written in its own font.
1tpyq3k: How do I sort a list?
At the top of the list: “N items · Sort:” and the menu (newest, oldest, A → Z…). At the bottom, “See the next N ↓” loads the rest.
0gyncxg: How do I create my own theme (colour design)?

Settings → Appearance → “✎ My themes” → “＋ New theme…” (or “Duplicate” on an existing theme). Choose while looking at the preview: the main colour (buttons, links), the background of the page, of panels and of cards, the text, the colour of the lines around frames and their thickness (from 0 to 8 px; 0 = no lines). Tick “Dark theme” for a dark background: the app switches to dark mode. If the text is hard to read on a background, a yellow message says so. Save: it is added to the “Preset” list, in “✎ My themes”; choose it then “Apply”. “⚙️ Manage the presets” arranges, shows or hides themes, and for yours: edit, rename, duplicate, export, delete (with “↶ Undo”).
02lb3ut: Why “⚠️ On this background, this colour is hard to read” under “Main colour”?

The main colour is also used to write links, small badges and texts. With some backgrounds (especially a dark theme and a dark colour, such as blue #0066cc on “Dark”), it is hard to read: the app measures the difference in brightness (the contrast, as in “✎ My themes”) and warns when it is below 4.5. It is only a warning: your colour stays chosen. “Use the theme’s colour” puts back the one suggested by the Preset (saved straight away, “↶ Undo” to go back). The warning goes away by itself as soon as the colour or the Preset reads well. In Charts → Statistics, in dark mode, figures written in a statistic’s colour are lightened to stay readable; the bars keep your colours.
01bb38i: How do I change the thickness or colour of the lines around frames?

With a theme of your own: Settings → Appearance → “✎ My themes” → “＋ New theme…” (or “Edit”). “Lines around (borders)” gives their colour, separate from the text colour, and the “Thickness of the lines around” slider their thickness, from 0 to 12 px (2 px at first, double-click to go back to it). The app’s themes keep their 2 px black lines.
1gwwzei: How do I add my own avatar shape?

Settings → “Portraits and avatars” → “1 · The shape” → “＋ Create a shape”. Three ways: “📚 Library” (the shapes of the tables: hearts, coats of arms, stars, trees… with search and families), “✏️ Draw a polygon” (click to place the points, drag them, double-click to remove one; triangle, star, shield templates…), or “⤒ Import an SVG” (drag or paste the file: only its filled paths are kept, never a script). Give it a name and “＋ Create the shape”: it is chosen straight away, and stays in the row of shapes (with ✎).
19sl542: How do I have the same portrait (circle or square of initials) everywhere?

Settings → “Portraits and avatars”. “1 · The shape”: one shape for everything (circle, rounded square, square, tilted square, diamond… and yours), which applies to portraits and to the small numbered squares of the blocks; it is saved as soon as you click. “2 · The portrait”: “Start from” As before (at first, each screen keeps its own drawing), Single circle (the same circle everywhere, in the colour of the gender) or Record square (black border, photo in black and white). Below: rounding, size of initials, border, colours for man / woman / unknown / animal, the record’s photo, black and white, one or two letters, Sosa badge; the preview shows the record, a list, the picker, the tree and the badges. “↺ Reset to default” goes back to “As before”.
1dm877q: How do I change the left column (style of entries, numbers, tabs, width, on the right)?

Settings → “Menus, column and lists” → “Column” tab. “Where?”: left or right. “The column’s design”: “Start from” As before (at first) or New (consecutive numbers, the same tabs everywhere, “List | Cards” above the list), then each choice as a picture: style of entries (framed buttons by default, continuous list, airy list, buttons without shadow, side bar, rounded badges, binder tabs, cards with a marker, soft background), top tabs, numbers (consecutive, original letters or none), size, “List | Cards” and width (240 to 420 px). The preview follows each click. It applies to all the columns (People, Charts, Map, Investigations, Research, Comparison…).
0e0w2cr: How do I change the shape of the app’s elements (rounded corners, thin lines, plain, compact…)?

There is no longer a “Designs to choose from” page: each shape is stored where it is used. The style of records (lines, shadows, corners: As before, Soft, Old paper, Plain) in Settings → “Person and animal records”, with the shape of the header: it only changes the records of people and animals; the lines, corners and shadows of the left column in “Menus, column and lists” → Column; the page background in “Theme and colours” (🧩 Page background); Movements in Settings → “♿ Accessibility” → “🎞 Movement” tab; Density, Icons and Lists in Settings → “Menus, column and lists” (one tab each); Buttons at the end of “Notifications and buttons”; the header of records in “Person and animal records” → “Shape of the header”; the boxes of trees in Charts → “🎨 Colours of statistics and trees”. For each: click the large card you prefer (👍 / 👎 to help you), then fine-tune in “More settings”; the preview shows real screens of the app with your data. It is saved straight away (“✓ Saved”), with “↶ Undo”. The font, the text size and the colours are set in “Theme and colours”.
0mds0jo: Where have some settings gone (order of lists, of charts, widget library, language, DNA)?

They are now where you use them. The order of the lists: Lists → “Reorder” (a window). The order of diagrams and statistics: Charts → “⠿ Reorder the charts” (under the colours). The widget library: Dashboard → “🧩 Widget library”; the widgets in place: “Reorder the widgets” and the ✎ of each widget. The language, the default calendar and the player: Settings → “Theme and colours”, after “Displayed name”. The DNA display: DNA → ⚙️ Settings. The order of the Settings pages: “Reorder” at the bottom of the Settings column.
1fdnhhn: Where do I set the tree boxes (white, male / female colours, with photo, mini)?

In Charts → “🎨 Colours of stats and trees” (at the bottom of the left column), “🌳 Tree boxes” section: choose a card (the preview shows a real tree with your data), then the width of the boxes, the lines, the dates and the Sosa badge. Just below, “Colours by sex” brings everything together: the colour of each sex (bands and pale background of the “Male / female colours” boxes, and round portraits) and the background and text of the “White” boxes. Everything is kept with “Save”. These boxes used to be in Designs to choose from: your choices are carried over as they were.
1vblinp: Where have the “Ready-made sets”, the font and the dashboard of the designs to choose from gone?

They have been removed: they duplicated Appearance and sometimes stopped it working (for example, with “Old archives”, changing the font or the Preset no longer did anything). The font and text size are chosen in Appearance (“Font”, “Text size”); for an archive atmosphere, take the “Paper archive” Preset in Appearance and, if you like, “Old paper” in Designs to choose from → A1. The dashboard stays as before (widths 1, ½, ⅓…). Your old choices are cleaned up by themselves: the rest of your designs is kept (Movements becomes A7, Lists A8).
1w9k0bk: Why are some settings switches and others checkboxes?

A switch (the little button that slides) changes what you see straight away: it is a setting, kept by itself. A checkbox is for choosing items in a list, or an option that only counts when you click the button (“Save”, “Create”, “⤓ Export”…).
0t8yuzz: How do I write a time or a duration?

As you would say it: “14 h 30”, “14:30”, “9h05” or “noon” for a time; “2 h 15”, “1 min 30”, “90 s” or “1:30” for a duration. Just below, the app writes what it understood (“✓ Understood: 1 min 30 s”) or warns you (“⚠️ Impossible time”). For numbers, the unit (px, mm, cm, %, s…) is written inside the box, on the right.
11frgoq: Do the designs to choose from change my Accessibility or Appearance settings?

No. The first frame of Appearance (Preset, Main colour, Font, Text size, Tab menu…) always comes first: a design only changes the shape (lines, shadows, corners, density, icons, record header, tree boxes, buttons, lists, movements), never the font, the text size or the colours. The colour of the record lines follows the colours of your Preset; a theme of your own that has its own lines (✎ My themes) keeps them. Accessibility also keeps priority: if “Reduce animations” is ticked, nothing moves, whatever the movements. The male / female colours of the tree boxes are the same as those of the portraits (Appearance → 👤 Portraits): changing them in one place changes them in the other.
1rx0wnw: How do I arrange or hide the shapes offered?

Settings → “Portraits and avatars” → “1 · The shape” → “⚙️ Manage the shapes”: untick a shape to hide it from the row, drag ⠿ (or ↑ ↓) to arrange it, then “Save the order and the shapes shown”. Your own shapes can be edited, duplicated, exported and deleted (with “↶ Undo”). “↺ Reset to default” puts back the original order and shows all the shapes.
1bsstjg: How do I hide the big frame at the top of a record (for a slideshow)?

Settings → “Person and animal records” → “Record header” → Frame: “Hide the whole frame” (kept straight away). Records then start with the parents, spouses and children, then the blocks. To put it back: same place, “Show the frame”.
02yt3kg: How do I hide or arrange the buttons at the top right (split screen, new window, 🔒, 🧓, 🧮, My genealogies)?

Settings → Appearance → “Buttons at the top right”: untick a button to hide it, drag its handle ⠿ (or Alt + ↑ / ↓) to change the order; it is kept straight away (“↶ Undo” at the bottom left), and the preview shows the top bar. “↺ Reset to default” puts back the app’s order, with all the buttons except 🧓 (hidden at first). The 🧮 and 🧓 buttons also follow their own switches (calculator settings; Settings → Accessibility → 🧓 Simple mode): it is the same setting. Kept with the 💾 Saved settings of Appearance and the site defaults.
0teq1qz: How do I arrange the square buttons at the top of a record, or put them in 2 columns?

Settings → “Person and animal records” → “Record header”: drag the buttons (✨ life story, 👁＋ new observation (animal records), 🔖 bookmark, 🗑 delete, 🔓 lock, 🕘 history, 🧩 This person was…, hidden at first: tick it to show it) or use ↑ ↓, untick those to hide, choose “In 2 columns” if you like: it is kept straight away (“✓ Saved”, “↶ Undo”). The preview shows the result. It is kept in the “💾 Saved settings”.
1d0682t: Where do I put the “🧩 This person was…” link at the top of the record?

Settings → “Person and animal records” → “Record header” → “🧩 This person was…” link: a square 🧩 button in the column of buttons, or at the bottom of the column of badges (under To check, Outside the genealogy, Artist). It is hidden at first: tick 🧩 in the list of buttons to show it (untick it to hide it again). A click opens the person’s profiles page (or the choice of their profiles if they have none yet). Not on animal records.
19zeni1: How do I add a birthday to my calendar (phone, Google, Apple, Outlook)?

On an event of the record, click 📅: every year or just once, with a reminder the day before. For the whole family: Lists → Family calendar → “⤓ Export the birthdays (.ics)” (direct ancestors, the whole database, a branch, living only). Open the file to add it; importing it again creates no duplicate. Approximate dates or dates reduced to the year cannot go into a calendar.
0155pxq: How do I restore an old photo in one go?

Retouch → 🧭 Restore tab (or Image) → “✨ Restore in one go”. Tick the steps (denoising, dust, creases, contrast, sharpness, colourisation) while looking at their previews, set the strength, then “Apply”. Each step becomes a “✨” layer that you can hide or adjust; ↶ undoes everything at once.
0dsfuwx: How do I repair a crease or a tear on a photo?

🪡 Repair tool (R key): paint over the crease and it is rebuilt from what surrounds it. “🔍 Find the creases” finds the fine lines and shows them to you in red before filling them in (to check: it can also mark real lines).
1dz4glu: How do I compare before and after a retouch?
Under the photo, “◧ Curtain”: drag the line, ⇅ changes the direction. ⤓ Export → Before / after saves a side-by-side or curtain image, with a caption.
0i2gkoy: How do I make portraits in the same format?

Retouch → Image → “🪪 Crop as an ID photo”: the eyes are made horizontal, at the same height, in 3:4; “Use as portrait” sends it to the record. For several records: Editing tools → Retouch → “🪪 ID portraits”.
1yzbfbd: How do I see my projects as large thumbnails?
Lists → Editing tools: next to “Sort”, choose “Cards” (one card per project) or “List” (the table). The choice is kept for each tool.
0fx4cyi: How do I see a list as cards rather than rows?

Above each list, just before “Sort”, click “List” (one row per item: small image, name, details, date) or “Cards” (one card per item with a large image). Each list remembers your choice and your sorting: Boards can stay as cards and People as a list.
10j5yfl: Can I sort the cards like the table?
Yes: in “Cards” mode, the “Sort” menu arranges the cards like the columns of the table (by name, by date…).
14n4dsw: How do I change the big buttons of simple mode?

Settings → Accessibility → “🧓 Simple mode” tab → 06 “What is shown” → “The big buttons”. For each tile: ⠿ or ↑ ↓ to arrange it, the switch to show or hide it, ✎ to change its name, its short sentence, its icon and its colour (↺ resets the tile to default). “＋ Add a tile”: ⭐ A person (opens their record in sentences), 📸 An album (its photos as a slideshow) or 💌 A note from the family (a text in large print, read aloud with 🔊); ⧉ to make another one the same, × to remove it. Just below, “Layout”: how many per row (1 to 4), height, spacing, title size and font of the tiles. Everything is kept in the “💾 Saved settings” of simple mode.
1jhpjry: How do I show the tree to an elderly person (simple mode)?

“🧓 Simple mode”: very big buttons (🌳 The tree, 📷 The photos, 👥 The people, 🎂 On this day), sentences read aloud and nothing that can be changed or deleted. Open it with the “🧓 Simple mode” button at the top of the app (hidden at first: tick “Show the button…” at the very top of the “🧓 Simple mode” tab), the dashboard widget or Settings → Accessibility → “🧓 Simple mode” tab → “▶ Open simple mode”. The first time, the app first shows you its settings. So that a tablet always opens on it: “Open the app directly in simple mode” (on this device), or the address …/#mode-simple.
1we61u2: How do I leave simple mode?

On the home screen only: keep your finger pressed on “🔒 Leave simple mode” (3 seconds at first, adjustable), or hold the Enter key down. If a 4-digit code has been chosen, the app then asks for it. The code is kept hidden (hashed), never in plain text; it is not real protection, it only avoids leaving by mistake. Esc only does “Back”.
1v3ynsl: How do I set up simple mode (who is watching, colours, size, voice)?

Settings → Accessibility → “🧓 Simple mode” tab. Eight sections with their “Why?”: who is watching (to write “your mother”, “your great-grandson”), colours (the contrast is checked live, “Fix” raises it to 7:1), sizes, font (Atkinson Hyperlegible, Luciole, OpenDyslexic…), voice, what is shown, slideshow and photo frame, exit. The preview on the right shows the tablet. Each change is kept straight away (“↶ Undo” at the bottom left); “Ready-made sets” applies everything at once, “💾 Saved settings” keeps, exports and imports your settings. Your “♿ Whole app” settings also apply here, unless you choose “Specific to simple mode”.
0ruh6qb: What can you see in simple mode?

The tree with the person in the middle, their spouse, their parents and their children, the relationship written in plain words (“your grandmother”, “the husband of your granddaughter Émilie”); the photos in large size with “🔊 Listen” and “👥 Who is there?”; a simple record whose story is written in sentences (birth, baptism, marriage, occupation, death); the people by family, by first name or by searching (big keyboard, 🎤 dictation); “On this day”: birthdays, marriages, photos of the month and what is coming soon. Living people can be shown, reduced to their first name or hidden; confidential records are never shown; removed photos and records are not shown (without being deleted).
1psl3wt: How do I simplify the screen (“one thing at a time” mode)?

Settings → Accessibility → “🧩 One thing at a time”. The app hides the rarely used tools (DNA, comparison, split screen, dashboard settings, deleting or locking a record…) and enlarges the main buttons. Nothing is deleted: the “Simple mode — Show everything” banner, at the bottom right, brings everything back in one click.
1775d81: How do I have a screen reader read the description of images?

Settings → Accessibility → “Describe the images”. Each photo in your media is read with its description, otherwise its title, its date, its place and the people linked to it. To write it yourself, open a media item: “Image description (read aloud)” field.
1pgpq3b: How do I always show the subtitles of videos and montages?

Settings → Accessibility → “Subtitles always shown”. Videos that have subtitles show them automatically; in the montage, the “Subtitles” track is visible during playback even if it is hidden. The exported video does not change.
1i2ut34: How do I fill in a field by speaking (voice dictation)?

Settings → Accessibility → “Voice dictation”. A 🎤 appears in the field you are writing in: click it (or Ctrl + Shift + Space), speak, and the text is written at the cursor. Say “comma”, “full stop”, “new line”… for punctuation, Esc to stop. If your computer does not offer dictation here: on a Mac, the system dictation (🎤 key or Fn twice); on Windows, Windows + H.
1wpmflz: Which font should I choose to read more easily (dyslexia)?

Settings → Accessibility → Text → Font. “Very legible” (Atkinson Hyperlegible) and “OpenDyslexic” are stored in the app: nothing to install, and they work without the Internet. “Comic Sans” is your computer’s font: if it is missing, the app uses OpenDyslexic instead.
0wvqy06: Can I ask a question with a precise date?

Yes: “Who was born on 7 May 1950?”, “born in May 1950”, “born on 15 Brumaire Year II”, “born in Year II”, “died aged 70”, “died before age 5”. If the date does not exist, the app tells you instead of listing everything.
0nk95rh: How does the question in plain language know who I am talking about?

“How many ancestors does Jean Martin have?” counts those of Jean Martin; without a name, it is the starting person, and the app says so. A first name alone is enough if it is unique; otherwise the app shows you the records to choose from.
1kqpfpb: Can I ask for cousins, half-brothers or inconsistent dates?

“The first cousins of Louis Martin”, “the half-sisters of…”; “brothers and sisters” separates those who have the same parents from the half-siblings. “Who died before being born?” or “inconsistent dates” lists the dates to check. Animals are not counted among the people; ask “who are the animals”.
051vohd: What does “pedigree collapse” mean in the Sosa list?
An ancestor who appears at several Sosa numbers (for example cousins who married each other): this is normal, it is not a duplicate to merge.
1yvu9qj: Why does the Date box accept 29 February 1500?
Before 1583, the Julian calendar was used, in which every year divisible by 4 has a 29 February. Years before 1000 are understood, but the app does not sort them yet (yellow warning).
1ilh0ss: What happens when I remove a parent?
The other parent remains the child’s parent. If you put the parent back afterwards, the child returns to the couple.
1qvauss: How are half-brothers and half-sisters arranged?
If someone had several spouses, a child added is no longer automatically put with one of them: add the 2nd parent and the child joins the right couple. A child never has three parents.
0i2lu44: Why can’t I remove a spouse?
A couple who have a marriage, sources, notes, media or children together cannot be separated with one click: the message says what to remove first.
0otkr01: What does the lock on a record block?
A locked record no longer changes at all: events, sources, photos, labels, name variants, hypotheses, family links, notes. Unlock it to edit it.
040k8mn: You cannot merge two spouses, nor an ancestor with their descendant: they are not the same person.
0onci73: Do I need to type accents to search?
No: “helene” finds Hélène, “jean-baptiste” finds Jean Baptiste. The quick search also looks in the other names of a record (variants).
14l76uu: Why does Lists → Places show fewer places?
The list only shows the places of your genealogy (and those you created), not the 80,000 reference communes. Lists → People does not show animals, and a marriage shows both spouses.
1qz7zo8: What does a GEDCOM export keep?

Labels, animals, note titles and dates in the Republican or Julian calendar are kept, and the import reads them back. An impossible link (someone who would be their own ancestor) is ignored on import and reported.
1dfhx1p: How are Republican and very old dates sorted?
A Republican date (“15 Brumaire Year II”) gets its Gregorian equivalent and its year, for sorting and ages. Years before 1000 are understood (“about 845”).
1fhwz00: While saving, the button waits: a double-click or a repeated Enter no longer creates a duplicate. It goes back to normal as soon as it is finished, even if there is an error.
0hti78p: What does the Enter key do in a window?
In a one-line box, Enter saves the window (like the blue button); it no longer closes it and loses what was typed. In a large text, Enter goes to a new line.
18ga7qf: What does “changed in another window” mean?

If the same record, the same board or the same layout is open in two tabs, LCNDA no longer silently replaces what the other one saved: reload to see the other version, or choose “Save anyway” / “Keep my version”.
05jviyw: The message “No connection with LCNDA” says so, what you typed stays in the window and “Try again” restarts the saving. If you close or reload the tab with unsaved input, the browser asks first.
0t49hl4: Esc closes windows and tools (drawing, house…) when nothing is in progress. If there are changes, it asks first, and pressing several times no longer makes you lose anything. In a search box, Esc empties it first.
1fpdzrl: What does ⌘Z (Ctrl+Z) do outside the editors?
It immediately undoes the last record created (if nothing has been added to it), a lock or a family link, with “↷ Redo”. Otherwise it explains how to undo by hand.
17l3h95: What happens to the witnesses and godparents of a deleted record?
Deleting a record or an event also removes its witnesses and godparents; restoring puts them back.
1cchr5u: How do I reopen an exported slideshow?
A file exported with “⤓ Export → 💾 File” is reopened with “⤒ Import a slideshow” in the list of slideshows.
0gna7nh: How do I zoom on a phone?
In the house, the drawing and the presentation, two fingers zoom the plan or the slide, not the page.
0hoannf: Can I get back a widget removed from the dashboard?
Yes: “↶ Undo” in the message at the bottom left. An empty dashboard offers “＋ Add a widget”.
0hvq8dn: What is the bar above the lists for?

All lists now have the same bar, always in this order: 🔍 Search (“/” key to go there, Esc or × to empty it), “Filter ▾”, “List | Cards” and “Sort”. In “Filter ▾”, each section shows its choices with their number (Kind, State, Place 📍, Person 👤, Label 🏷, Period…); the chosen filters appear under the bar as blue badges (“Women ×”): a click on a badge removes it, “Clear all” removes them all. “Sort” always starts with “Newest, Oldest, A → Z, Z → A”, then the list’s own sorts; clicking a column heading also sorts. Each list remembers your settings, even after closing the app. A list that is still empty shows no bar, only the button to get started. The Treasures (Letters, Candles, Shares, Places passport, Missing records, Gazettes) also have the bar: “Lit” or “In progress” is the starting choice, as a badge (× to see everything); a sealed letter is never searched in its text. The two calendars (My diary, Family calendar) only have 🔍 and “Filter ▾” (Kind, Person, Place): the search works in all views. In “My lists”: “List | Cards” and “More ▾” for the other layouts (by group, draggable columns, timeline, gallery), “Filter ▾” has a section per column (the ▾ of a column heading opens it) and these filters are stored in the list; “⤓ Export ▾” and “🖨 Print” are at the top, Edit, Duplicate and Delete in “⋯”.
0hpuuzy: Why doesn’t the app ask me “Are you sure?” before deleting any more?

For a note, an event, a row, an item in a tool…, the deletion happens straight away and a message at the bottom left offers “↶ Undo” for 6 seconds (hovering over it pauses the time). After Undo, “↷ Redo” does the deletion again. The question remains only for what cannot be recovered: a whole record, a database, emptying the bin.
0q08ukx: Are the CSV files I download safe?
Yes: a text beginning with =, +, - or @ is preceded by an apostrophe, so that Excel, Numbers or LibreOffice do not take it for a hidden formula.
1ccvl3l: How do I visit my house as if I were there?

House → 3D view → “🚶 Visit”. Walk with W A S D (or Z Q S D) or the arrows, Shift to run. Click the view to look around with the mouse, Esc to release it, Esc again to leave. You go through doors, not through walls. On a staircase: E to go up, C to go down (or the ⬆ ⬇ buttons). The small map shows where you are; a click on it takes you there. The eye height can be set (1.60 m, or 1 m to see like a child). On a tablet, walk with the circle at the bottom left.
0o5myne: How do I see the sunlight in my house?

3D view → “☀️ Light”. Choose the time and the day (Winter, Summer…), or “▶ See the day”. The sun is calculated for the location of the house (otherwise the centre of France). Set “North of the plan” if the top of your plan does not face north. At night, the lamps, chandeliers and candles placed light up. Also in the House tab → “☀️ Orientation and light”.
1ps0v6v: How do I trace my house over the Napoleonic cadastre?

⤒ Import → “📐 An old plan, a cadastre” (or Floor tab → Old plan): choose the image in the media or import it. Click both ends of a known length and give its real length (metres, toises, French feet…). “↻ Straighten” makes a wall straight in two clicks. Set the transparency, lock, then “✏️ Trace the walls” and draw over it.
1edtihi: How do I link a memory to a piece of furniture or a room?

Click the piece of furniture or the room, then “🔗 Link a memory”: a photo or a document, a story, a person, or a family memory. A ✦ appears on the plan and in 3D; a click on it (even during the visit) shows the memory. House tab → “🏷 The memories of the house” to see them all.
09te358: How do I change the wallpaper, the stone or the colour of the walls?

Click a wall. In “Colour and texture”, each side has its covering (render, cut stone, brick, half-timbering, panelling, wallpaper, toile de Jouy, tiles, limewash…) and its colour. “Pattern size” enlarges the bricks or the paper. “Same for: the room / the whole floor / the whole house” copies the choice. In a room, “🧱 Room walls” changes all its walls at once. Floor tab: plain or beamed ceiling.
1ffe94s: How do I keep or share my house settings?
🧲 Snap → “💾 Saved settings”: “＋ Save the current settings” (snapping, grid, wall thickness, eye height, light), then ⋯ → “⤓ Export” for a .json file and “⤒ Import” on another computer.
190p5t3: How do I export my house?

“⤓ Export”: the floor plan as PNG, JPG, PDF or SVG, printing, an image of the 3D view, or the house file (.json) to import again with ⤒ Import. “Also keep a copy in the media” keeps the image in your media.
0usbcij: Does colour blindness correction also apply in the editors?

Yes: Settings → Accessibility → “Colours easy to tell apart” corrects the whole screen, including the 3D house, drawing, layout, retouching, tables, the map and full-screen windows. Your own colours are not replaced: the correction makes them distinguishable.
1x1a9gs: How do I make the app easier to read or use (colour blindness, large text, voice)?

Settings → Accessibility. Colours: choose your type of colour blindness (protanopia, deuteranopia…) — the app corrects its colours, with colours that are easy to tell apart and shapes (✓ ⚠ ⛔, hatching) in addition; “See as…” shows the screen as a colour-blind person sees it, to check an announcement or a chart. Text: size, line spacing, spacing, very legible font or one for dyslexia, underlined links. Also: high contrast, visible keyboard outline, big buttons, big pointer, fewer animations, messages shown for longer, and reading aloud (select a text then 🔊, or “Read the record”; Esc stops). “↺ Reset to default” puts everything back as at the start (“↶ Undo” in the message to go back).
0d98735: How do I choose a person, a place or something else in a tool?

Everywhere, the same box: type 2 letters (surname, first name, town…). For each person the list shows their initials or photo (blue male, pink female, orange 🐾 animal), their dates and places, and their Sosa number; for a place, first those in your genealogy (blue marker, number of events), then the communes of France and the cities of the world (white marker) — the list scrolls without limit, and you can narrow it down by typing the department, its number or the country (“saint-martin 32”, “springfield usa”). ↑ ↓ to choose, Enter to confirm, Esc to close; “＋ Create the record” if it does not exist. Once chosen, the person becomes a badge with “↗ Record” and × to change. You can also type “sosa 12” or “#45” (record number).
1isrnu4: How do I choose an image from my media in a tool?

Everywhere (announcements, layout, retouching, slideshow, presentation, montage, boards, museum, seals, dashboard…), the same window opens: your media as thumbnails. Type a title, a reference, a name, a place or a year; the buttons at the top filter (Photos, Documents, Sounds, Videos, the tool’s person, 🕘 Recent, ⭐ Portraits) and show how many there are. Click an image to see it large on the right (with its size and the format it prints well in), double-click or press Enter to take it. When you can take several, tick them (click or Space) then “Use these images”. An image from the computer? Drag it into the window, paste it (⌘V) or “📁 Import…”: it goes into your media and is ticked. The thumbnail size (large, small, list) is remembered.
18d5d2d: Vector drawing: how do I cut out a group or a layer with a shape (mask)?

Place the cutting shape (circle, oval, heart, outline of a commune, escutcheon…) at the very top of the group or layer, then, in the Layers panel, click ✂️ on the line of the group or layer: you only see what is inside the shape (portrait in a medallion, map cut to the outline of a commune, motif in a coat of arms). Nothing is erased: a 2nd click on ✂️ removes the mask and the shape goes back to the very top. The coloured ✂️ shows what is masked. For a few objects without a group: select them with the shape on top, then Object → “Clipping mask” (⌘7).
1johpaw: Announcements: more formats, and adding, removing or hiding fields?

In the announcement window, “Format” offers cards (10 × 15 to 16 × 22 cm), squares (12 to 21 cm), long formats (DL, menu, bookmark, banner), posters (A4 to A1, 40 × 60, 50 × 70, 60 × 80 cm), screen formats (social networks, story, email, 16:9) and “Custom” where you type the width and height in cm. Each field has a checkbox (unticked: the field stays in the window but is not printed), ↑ ↓ to arrange it and 🗑 to remove it. “＋ Add a field” creates a new one, with its size (small, normal, large, calligraphic title), italic and bold. “Put back a removed field” and “↺ Reset to default” go back to the template. The chosen fields and format are remembered for next time.
0e7dsdo: How do I organise a family reunion?

Lists → Research and organisation → “🎉 Family reunions” → “＋ New family reunion” (or ⋯ on the ancestor’s record → “🎉 Organise a family reunion…”, or Lists → Editing tools). Choose the ancestor, or the couple: the app finds all their living descendants (and their spouses, if you tick it), arranged by branch, with their relationship to the ancestor (“grandson of…”) and to a reference person, usually you (“second cousin of…”). A person with no death recorded, born less than 100 years ago, is marked “Living?”: check. Confidential records are never shown.
0b6xn10: Where do I put the addresses and replies of the family reunion guests?

“👥 Guests” tab: the ✓ box says who is invited; the address, email and phone come from the directory of the living or from the last address on the record. You change them here without touching the record (unless you tick “also in the directory of the living”). The reply (yes, no, maybe), the number of people and the diet are noted on each line. “⤒ Import a list…” reads a table (CSV, Excel .xlsx, LibreOffice .ods) with a line of headings (First name, Surname, Email, Reply…); “↶ Undo” undoes it.
1vn1ihu: How do I send the invitations for the family reunion?

“✉️ Invitations” tab: write the text once ({foyer}, {date}, {lieu}… are replaced by themselves); one invitation per household (the descendant, their spouse and their minor children). “🖨 Print the invitations…” (one page per household, the address for a window envelope, “⤓ PDF”), “📝 In the word processor”, “📰 Announcement (drawing)”, “📁 Copy in the media”. “✉️ Email ready” opens your email program with the text: nothing is sent by the app.
06wf4bo: How do I make the badges, the big tree and the seating plan for the family reunion?

“🏷 Badges”: an A4 sheet (6, 8 or 10 badges), the first name in large print, the branch in colour, the relationship, the small photo and a QR code if you like. “🌳 Big tree”: all the descendants in large format (A2, A1…), one colour per branch, boxes to stick the photos of the day; it opens in the drawing tool to export it as PDF for the printer (bleed, crop marks). “📅 D-day”: the attendance list, the seating plan by branch (a household is never separated, ↶ Undo) and the photo album. “📊 Figures”: guests and replies by branch, and the colour of each branch.
0tnhs9r: Do the family reunion addresses leave the app?

No: they stay in the family reunion project. No export (GEDCOM, website, simple mode, view-only mode) reads them. The only file that takes them out is “⤓ Export ▾ → Guest table (CSV)”, and the addresses, emails and phone numbers are only in it if you tick the box.
00dbve9: How do I make an announcement, an invitation or a poster for a family reunion?

Lists → Editing tools → “📰 Announcements and posters” (or Charts). Choose the kind (birth, baptism, marriage, death, family reunion, golden wedding, old newspaper article, invitation), a style (Belle Époque, Art Nouveau, Art Deco, 1950s, classic, modern, mourning) and a format; choose a person from the tree: names, dates, places, ages and family fill in by themselves. The result opens in the vector tool: each text, ornament and the photo can be edited, then you print (or PDF) and export (PNG, JPG, SVG).
12scl7x: How do I make a slideshow or the story in pictures of an ancestor?

Lists → Editing tools → “🎞️ Presentation and slideshow”. “✨ A person’s story” builds the slideshow of a life by itself: a title, their photos, a map where the route of the places of their life is drawn, their biography. You then add photos (with a slow camera movement), titles, route maps (a migration: places to add, or those of a person’s life), your voice on each slide (🎙), music that lowers when the voice speaks; you play it full screen and export it as a video (Media or download).
09k7m40: How do I make a presentation as with Keynote or PowerPoint?

Lists → Editing tools → “🎞️ Presentation and slideshow” → “＋ New” → “🎤 Presentation (Keynote style)”, then choose a theme and a format (16:9, 4:3, square, vertical, A4, custom). On the left the slides (drag them to arrange them; ⧉ duplicate, 👁 skip during playback, § start a section that folds up); “＋ Slide ▾” offers the layouts: title, title and text, title and photo, full-page photo, photo and text, two columns, quote, section, key figure, a person. At the top: insert a text, a shape (rectangle, ellipse, star, arrow, bubble, line…), an image, a table, a chart, the record, the portrait, the small tree or the timeline of the life of a person from the database, a video or a sound. An object can be moved, enlarged (⇧: proportions, ⌥: from the centre), rotated (top handle) and aligned with the others thanks to the guides; ⌥ while dragging copies it. On the right, the inspector: Format (font, size, bold, lists, colours, border, shadow, cropping and masking of photos…), Animate, Slide (colour, gradient or image background, notes), Objects (front, back, hide, lock) and Document (theme, fonts, format, music). ⌘Z undoes, ⌘C ⌘V copy (also from one presentation to another), ⌘G groups, ⌘L locks.
0r467jh: How do I animate a presentation (transitions, builds, magic move)?

In the presentation, “✨ Animate” tab on the right. The transition plays when arriving on the slide: fade, dissolve, fade through black, push, slide, reveal, wipe, zoom, swap, flip, cube, or “magic move”: duplicate the slide (⧉), move, enlarge or rotate the objects on the copy, and they glide from one place to the other during playback (objects with the same name work too). Choose an object then “＋ Build in” or “＋ Build out”: appear, fade, arrive from one side, grow, bounce, drop, wipe, blur, swirl, typewriter for a text; each animation starts on click, with the previous one or after it, with its duration and its delay; “Animation order” arranges them (↑ ↓) and “▶ Preview” shows them.
079l17m: How do I present with my notes, the next slide and a timer?

In the presentation: “▶ Play” (from the beginning, or “⏵ From here”) goes full screen; → space or click: next, ←: previous, a number then Enter: go to that slide, B: black screen, W: white screen, L: laser pointer, Esc: quit. “🎤 Presenter” (or P during playback) opens a second window to put on your screen: the current slide, the next one (or the remaining animations), your notes (A− A+), the timer and the time. Notes are written under the slide (📝 Notes) or in the Slide tab. A slide can also move on to the next by itself, and the presentation can loop (kiosk, exhibition).
01n892m: How do I import a PowerPoint, a LibreOffice file, Keynote or a PDF?

Lists → Editing tools → “🎞️ Presentation and slideshow” → “⤒ Import a presentation”, or “⤒ Import” in an open presentation (added after the slide shown, or in its place). PowerPoint (.pptx) and OpenDocument / LibreOffice Impress (.odp): each slide with its texts in place (sizes, bold, colours, lists), its images (stored in Media), its shapes, its tables, its charts, its notes and its transitions. Keynote (.key) has a closed format: in Keynote, File → Export to → PowerPoint, then import the .pptx. A PDF gives its images (scans, photos), one per slide: its text cannot be read here. Also: photos (one slide per photo), a text or Markdown (“# Title” starts a slide, “-” makes a bullet, “---” separates, “Notes:” the notes) and the .json file of a presentation from the app.
0cavmg6: How do I export a presentation as PDF, images or video?

In the presentation, “⤓ Export”: PDF or printing (one slide per page, or with the speaker notes under each slide; in the print window, choose “Save as PDF”), the slide shown as PNG, all the slides as PNG (a .zip file), a WebM video (each slide for its duration, with the music; to keep in Media or download) and the presentation file (.json, to reopen elsewhere with “⤒ Import”). A simple slideshow can become a presentation: “🎤 As a presentation” in the slideshow.
0q6vkpy: How do I arrange or hide the presentation buttons and choose its starting settings?

In the presentation, “⚙️ Customise”: each group of buttons at the top (insert, arrange, playback, file), the bar above the slides, the bottom bar, the inspector tabs and the sections of each tab (Position and size, Text, Image, Animations…) can be shown, hidden and arranged; a layout is kept under a name with “💾 Saved settings”. It is also in Settings → Montage, retouching, layout and sound (“🎤 Presentation” editor), with the theme, the format, the starting transition and layout, snapping, the colour of the laser pointer, full screen on opening and your own keyboard shortcuts.
1bn0o3s: How do I restore an old damaged photo?

Lists → Editing tools → Photo retouching → “🧭 Restore an old photo”, or in Retouch: the “🧭 Restore” tab (Image menu). Eight steps, each optional: straighten and crop; remove yellowing and revive the colours; find and remove dust and small spots automatically; fill scratches, creases and tears (healing brush, stamp); reduce grain; make a face sharper (surrounded with the ellipse); colourise (automatically, or with a brush and a palette of period tints); compare before / after and save as a new version (the original stays).
03gawhw: How do I transcribe a record (baptism, marriage, death, notarial deed)?

Lists → Editing tools → “📜 Record transcription”, or in an image viewer: “📜 Workshop”. The image of the record is on the left (zoom, contrast, negative, rotation), the text on the right (with old characters: ſ, œ, [illegible]…). Choose a passage then draw its area (▭ Area): a click on one highlights the other. “Read (printed)” reads a typed text and places the areas line by line; “✨ Read the record” reads handwriting (see the question “Read the record”). “🧭 Spot” finds the names and their role (godfather, witness, son of…), dates even written out in words (“l’an mil sept cent quatre-vingt-dix”) or in the Republican calendar (converted), places and occupations, and suggests the records that resemble them. “📋 Template” gives the outline of a record to complete.
0c1tx6u: How do I change the size of an area in a record transcription?

Click the area: it shows 8 handles (the corners and the middle of the sides). Pull a handle to change its size, drag the inside to move it; it does not leave the image and keeps a minimum size. With the keyboard: the arrows move it, Shift + arrows change its size, Alt to go point by point, Delete removes it (“↶ Undo” puts it back). ⌘Z undoes the last area change, ⇧⌘Z redoes it. The area stays linked to its passage in the text. It also works with the image rotated (⟳), straightened or mirrored, and with a finger (pinch to zoom).
0qrk1zw: What is the ⤢ button for in record transcription?

It changes how the image fits at each click: “Whole image” (you see the whole record), “Width” (the image takes the full width: best for reading a record from top to bottom), then “100 %” (actual size). The mode is written on the button; after zooming by hand (＋, －, the wheel or two fingers, always centred on the mouse or fingers), the button shows the percentage and a click returns to “Whole image”.
0kbameu: How do I read a pale, yellowed or stained record better?

In record transcription, the “🎚️ See better” settings: Sharpness (and its radius), Local contrast (brings out the writing everywhere, even in dark corners), Colour channel (All, Red, Green or Blue: brown ink often stands out better on blue), Remove the background (yellowing and stains disappear, the ink remains), Black and white threshold, Levels (black point, white point, gamma), Straighten to a tenth of a degree, Mirror (to read a text seen through the paper), Negative, Grey, and the 🔍 Magnifier that follows the mouse (the wheel changes the magnification; L key). “💾 Remember for this record” keeps these settings with the record; “↺ Original image” resets everything (with “↶ Undo”). Everything is calculated on your computer, without freezing the screen, even on a very large image. In “More ▾”, “Read and export the improved image” reads (printed or handwritten) and exports the image with these settings.
0pl05tg: How do I arrange the record transcription bar?

With “⚙️” at the end of the bar, or in Settings → Montage, retouching, layout and sound → “📜 Record transcription: toolbar”. Two layouts: A (everything in the bar, which wraps onto a new line if needed) or B (a short bar and the “🎚️ See better ▾” panel, arranged into Bring out the ink, Black and white, Position, with a badge that counts the active settings). Tick what is shown, arrange with ↑ ↓ or by dragging ⠿, and in B choose what goes in the bar or in the panel. “↺ Reset to default” puts everything back as at the start; “💾 Saved settings” keeps a bar under a name. On a small screen, the settings go into “See better” by themselves.
1dxas1q: I can’t read an old record (Latin, abbreviations, long s): where can I find help?

In record transcription, “📜 Reading help” (or Tools menu): first choose a word in the text, it is looked up automatically. Also: quick search (⌘K, type “filius”, “vve”, “dudit”…), ⋯ of the record, Settings → Glossary. Three tabs: 🔍 Dictionary (Latin of the registers, formulas for baptism, marriage and burial, abbreviations — including those of the censuses: cult., jlier, Vve, id., d° —, old words), filtered by kind and by record; ✍️ The letters (long s, round r, e and c, u and n, ligatures, barred p… drawn, with the letter not to be confused with); 🎓 Exercises: read a text written as in the register, type your reading, “✓ Correct” colours each word (right, to review with the explanation, forgotten, extra).
1ful8zn: How do I read a record in German, Italian, Spanish, Polish, Dutch, Latin or Greek?

“📜 Help reading old records” (record transcription, quick search ⌘K, Settings → Glossary): at the top, the “Language” badges (with the number of words) keep a single language in the three tabs. 🔍 Dictionary: the words of baptism, marriage and death, the months (with the old names and 7bris, Xbre, Jänner, Hornung…), numbers and ages in words, occupations, kinship and whole formulas translated (“Im Jahre…”, “L’anno…”, “En la villa de…”, “Działo się…”, “Anno Domini…”). Type without accents: “malzonkowie” finds małżonkowie, “grossvater” Großvater; in Greek, write in Greek letters without accents or in Latin letters (“huios” finds υἱός). ✍️ The letters: German script (Kurrent, Sütterlin), the Greek alphabet and its handwritten forms, with a converter for Greek numbers (͵αωνβʹ = 1852). 🎓 Exercises: a model text per language, corrected word by word. In the transcription, choose the “Language of the text”: the help opens in that language, and “🧭 Spot” or “✨ Read the record” show the known words with their translation. The lists come from the FamilySearch “Word Lists” and from GenWiki.
1thqrg0: And for a record in Swedish, Danish, Norwegian, Czech, Slovak, Hungarian, Romanian, Croatian, Slovene, Lithuanian, or in Occitan, Breton, Basque?

The same “📜 Help reading old records”: choose the language badge. For each: the words of baptism, marriage and death, the months (with the old names: Torsmånad, Boldogasszony hava, Gerar, svečan…), numbers and ages, occupations, kinship and translated formulas, plus a model exercise (example people) corrected word by word. Type without accents or signs: “szuletett” finds született, “brezna” března, “soen” Søn, “rodjen” rođen. Good to know: in Swedish, Danish and Norwegian, the surname changes with each generation (-son, -sen, -datter) and “aa” = å; in Hungarian, the surname comes before the first name (“Kovács Jánosné” = Mrs János Kovács); Danish counts in twenties (halvtreds = 50, a small converter is in the Dictionary); Romanian before 1860 is written in Cyrillic (alphabet in ✍️ The letters). Occitan, Breton and Basque are rare in registers: you will find them mostly in nicknames, place and house names, graves and a few notes by the priest.
1rp3n3a: And for a record in Portuguese, Catalan, English, Russian, Ukrainian, Hebrew, Yiddish, Armenian or Arabic (graves included)?

The same “📜 Help reading old records”: choose the language badge (“＋ other languages” to see them all). For each: the words of birth, marriage and death, the months, numbers and ages, occupations, kinship, translated formulas and a model exercise (example people) corrected word by word. English also has the census abbreviations (Ag. Lab., Unm., Do) and those of the Ellis Island lists (S.I., L.P.C.). For Russian, Ukrainian, Hebrew, Yiddish, Armenian and Arabic, you can search and answer in Latin letters: “krestianin”, “tichri”, “geshtorbn”, “krikor”, “marhoum”. Russian before 1918 (ѣ, ъ, і, ѳ) is explained in ✍️ The letters, with the pitfalls of handwriting. Hebrew and Arabic are displayed right to left; the formulas on graves are translated (פ״נ, תנצב״ה, المرحوم…) and a small converter reads the letter-numbers (תרנ״ה = 655, i.e. 1894-1895; Armenian ՌՋԺԵ = 1915; abjad and the digits ١٣٢٠).
1t9sew9: What are 300 livres of 1780 or 1,200 francs of 1880 worth today (Old money converter)?

“🪙 Old money converter” (Settings → Calendar / measures, quick search ⌘K, ⋯ of the record, record transcription): 💰 Money tab, write the sum as in the record (“12 livres 10 sous 6 deniers”, “1 200 francs”, “45 NF”, “3 écus”) and the year (“1780”, “an X”). You get the equivalent in today’s euros (≈), in bread and in days of work, and “The calculation, step by step”. From 1901, it is the INSEE price index (the same calculation as its franc-euro converter); before 1901, an order of magnitude. Exact parities: 1 livre = 20 sous = 240 deniers, 81 livres = 80 germinal francs, 1 new franc = 100 old francs, 1 € = 6.55957 F. “📋 Copy” puts the result on the clipboard.
1na8fee: How much is an arpent, a toise, a boisseau? And the Republican calendar?

“🪙 Old money converter” → 📏 Old measures: choose the region (Paris, Lyon, Brittany, Normandy, Burgundy, Provence, Lorraine, Alsace, Flanders), write “3 arpents”, “12 toises 3 pieds”, “2 setiers” (or “1.5 ha” for the reverse): the value in metres, ares or litres, the other measures of the region and the same measure elsewhere. → 📅 Republican calendar: “12 thermidor an II” or “14 July 1794”, both ways, with the day of the week and the 13 months of the year. In a record, a date in Year II is already understood (“✓ Understood: … (30 July 1794)”); “🪙 Convert” next to it opens the converter.
12g8ru9: Where do I find all my record transcriptions?

Lists → Archives and sources → “📜 Record transcriptions”: each record with its thumbnail, its kind, its date, its place, its reference, the number of lines and areas, the people spotted. Search in the title, the text, the people, the place or the reference (without worrying about accents); filter by kind of record, person, place, period, state (to do, in progress, finished), with areas or linked to a record; List or Cards (with the first lines of the text); sort by date of the record. A click reopens the record; “＋ New transcription” starts by choosing the image; 🗑 deletes with “↶ Undo”. The state is chosen at the top of the tool.
0oursrr: How do I print a beautiful large-format tree (fan, wheel, drawn tree)?

Charts → “🌳 Decorative tree to print”, or Lists → Editing tools → “🌳 Decorative tree”: choose the person, the shape (fan, open fan, wheel, drawn tree with trunk, branches and foliage), the number of generations, the format (A4 to A0, posters), the style (parchment, classic, botanical, heraldic, modern, black and white) and what is written (years, dates, places, occupations, Sosa numbers, empty boxes, portraits). The tree opens in vector drawing: everything can be retouched (colours, fonts, ornaments, coat of arms), then File → Print / PDF or Export as PNG.
1jpzxhe: How do I draw a town or village plan or a map of a region?

In Vector drawing: Plan menu → “Plan mode”, or the 🗺️ Plan tab on the right. Choose what you are drawing in the palette (road, street, path, river, forest, field, building, church, mill, place name…), then one click per point: roads join up, rivers widen, names follow the streets. Period styles (État-Major, Napoleonic cadastre, Cassini, parchment), scale, compass rose, cartouche and automatic legend. “Base map of a place” or “Reference image” lays a map or an old plan underneath, transparent, to trace over; “Places from the database” places your places; each object can be linked to a person or a place and have its years (time slider).
1pli3dg: How do I make a hemicycle, a horseshoe or the timeline of a group’s members?

Charts → “My diagrams” → “＋ Create a diagram”: 25 drawings (parliament in a hemicycle, arc, horseshoe, Westminster, circle, hall; members timeline in the Wikipedia style, timeline of lives, schedule; columns, pie chart, pyramid, flow, organisation chart, Venn, word cloud, gauges…). Type your figures, paste them from a spreadsheet, import a CSV or take them from the app (“From the app”, with “Keep up to date”). It can then go in a widget, a note, a person’s record, an investigation, the Workshop (“Link” tab) or the layout (Object → Insert a diagram).
0su2yi5: How do I create my own chart (formerly “my own statistic”)?

Settings → Chart editor (formerly “Statistics editor”) → “＋ New chart” (or “＋ Create a chart” at the bottom of Charts). Start from scratch (count people, events, one of your lists… by occupation, by place, by decade, by century), from one of the app’s statistics (Surnames, First names, Places, Birth years…) redrawn your way, from one of your widgets or from an example. Eight drawings: bars, columns, pie, ring, line, area, mosaic, table. It appears in Charts → “My charts”, and can also go on the dashboard or in one of your tabs.
0sw9grm: How do I put many conditions in a chart (e.g. woodcutters within 4 km of Pernay, married, with two children)?

In the Chart editor, start from one of the app’s statistics (Surnames, First names, Places…) or from a chart from scratch, then “＋ Criterion” as many times as you like: occupation, first name, surname, place, within … km of a town, between two precise dates, had an event (marriage, divorce, journey…), number of children (“2 and 2” = exactly two), number of unions, number of events of a type, age at an event, lifespan, sex, label, my ancestors. “✨ Suggest a caption” writes the sentence that sums up the criteria.
1puplhy: How do I share a chart on a forum or with an association?
Charts → My charts → your chart: “🖼️ PNG image” (to post), “📄 CSV” (the figures for a spreadsheet) or “🖨 Print / PDF”.
02mr9ec: Where do I display my chart: in Charts, on the dashboard, in a tab?
In the editor, “Where to show it”: tick Charts and/or the dashboard. For one of your tabs: add it from the left column of the tab, or in Settings → Tab editor.
1ad1dl3: Name and saint of the day: how do I see the people concerned?

Charts → Statistics → Name and saint of the day, at the very bottom: the list of people who bear the first name of the saint of their birth or baptism day (or all of them), sortable by date, by day of the year, by name or by saint. Click on a period or a family in the tables to keep only that one.
0f50q3j: First names: the family and France, how do I see everyone?
In the “In the family” column, click “＋ 12 people” (the number varies) to unfold the full list, and “Fold” to close it again.
0d0jchd: Where does an ancestor’s first name come from (godfather, grandfather, brother who died before…)?

Charts → Statistics → “Passing on of first names”: for each child, the app looks for the most likely lead — their godfather or godmother (the “godfather” and “godmother” witnesses of the birth or baptism), a brother or sister who died before their birth (the first name “taken up again”), a paternal or maternal grandparent, the father or mother, an uncle or aunt, or the saint of their birth day. Each lead states its rule (“same first name as their godfather”) and a confidence level (strong, medium, weak); Jean and Jeanne, Louis and Louise count as the same first name. At the top: the transmission arrows (one line per first name, the years across; click on a circle = the record), filterable by first name, by branch and by period; then the share of children who bear their godparent’s first name, period by period. On the record, the small line “👶 First name received from…” (Identity block) has a ⋯: “That’s right”, “That’s not it”, another lead, or “Choose the person…” with the search menu; “↶ Undo” right after. Nothing is written without your click; living people and confidential records are never counted or named.
1myepdc: How do I compare my family with French averages (age at marriage, children, mortality, signatures, occupations)?

Charts → Statistics → “Your family and the history of France” (just after “Family averages”): for each period, your family’s average (orange dot) next to that of France (blue dot, “≈”): age at first marriage of men and women, children per couple, infant mortality before age 1, life expectancy, share of spouses who signed their marriage record (“signed” box of marriages), share of farming occupations. Each French figure has its source at the bottom of the page (Louis Henry and Jacques Houdaille, Yves Blayo, INED, INSEE, Maggiolo survey…); when a figure was not certain, it was not included. Filters: branch and period; a click on the number of people shows who is counted; “⤓ Export” like the other statistics. A family has few records (“⚠️ few” under 10) and babies who died are often missing from trees: the comparison should be read broadly.
0f2hl9g: How do I keep a chart’s settings?
At the bottom of the Charts column, “💾 Save the view”: the diagram, the person, the depth and the colours are kept in the “Saved” tab.
0x9a96z: How do I quickly find a person or a place?
⌘K: type a name, a place, a search sweep or the name of a screen.
1dk660v: Can I ask a question in plain words?
Yes: Research → Type of search → “Ask a question in plain words”, for example “Which ancestors were bakers in Lille before 1850?”. The search can then be saved.
0slk814: How do I search for a word in the page?
⌘F: the words found are highlighted and counted.
184b0yi: How do I go back to the previous screen?
⌘← and ⌘→ on a Mac, Alt+← and Alt+→ on Windows and Linux. All the shortcuts: F1 key.
1yn66tg: How do I make my own list (e.g. all divorces between 1850 and 1920)?

Settings → List editor → “＋ New list”: choose events, people, or rows you write yourself (stands at a fair…); combine criteria, choose the columns, add your own columns to fill in (text, menu, checkbox, link, person from the database) and labels. You can also start from a list of the app (Births, Marriages, SOSA…) or from one of your lists, show it in the Lists tab, and share it with a relative (“Share” button, then “Import a list…” on their side). Can be exported as CSV and printed.
1o1s6sg: How do I know what to do today and this week in my research?

Add the “🗓 My research week” widget to the dashboard (or to the Follow-up page; it replaces the old “Daily work list”): everything waiting for you on a single list, the most urgent first — today’s and overdue reminders, letters without a reply (for how many days), upcoming archive visits, open leads and hypotheses, searches suggested by “What’s missing?” (including “search on SocFace”), what needs checking (SocFace readings, 🔴 / 🟠 alerts from the Database check), help requests, and what you did this week. On each line: ↗ to open it, ✓ when it is done, ⏭ to postpone to tomorrow or next week (“↶ Undo” at the bottom left). ✎ to choose “Today” or “This week”, sort by urgency or by kind, hide or reorder the kinds and the number of lines; ⛶ to see everything in large.
0uiwsb9: Which records should I look for first?
Add the “💡 Research suggestions” widget to the dashboard: the gaps in your Sosa line (birth, marriage, death, unknown parents), with the place and the years to search, the closest generations first.
1ycdsyo: Where can I see the history of a village?

Lists → Village record: the families, the occupations, the church, the population over the censuses and the Cassini map. ⚙️ “Organise the record” arranges, hides or widens each part; the census plan and a notepad are there too.
0gfnd28: How do I hide, arrange or add columns in a list?
In all the table lists of the Lists tab, the “⚙️ Columns” button.
0pbjnn9: How do I see the anniversaries to celebrate (Dates to celebrate)?

Dashboard → “🎂 Dates to celebrate” widget (the former “Today’s anniversaries”): today, this week or this month. Living people with their age (“Marie is 40”), ancestors “150 years ago”; round anniversaries are highlighted (🎉, golden wedding…). Filters All, Living, Ancestors, ⭐ Sosa; with the pencil ✎: a single branch, only births, marriages or deaths, only round anniversaries. 🔔 on a line sets a reminder (the day before, a week before or on the day) in Lists → Reminders. Confidential records are never there; in view-only mode 🔒, a living person appears only by their first name.
0ojreac: How do I file an old postcard and find it on the map?

Lists → “🏞 Postcards” → “＋ New postcard”: the front (the view) and the back (the written side), the publisher, the number, the date sent, the postmark, who wrote it and to whom, the address, the text on the back (“📜 Transcribe in the workshop” for the image of the back), the place shown and, if you like, the direction of the view. The cards in your media sent as “front/back” are already there, marked “To complete”. On the Map, the “🏞 Postcards” button shows them at their location, with a cone for the direction; the place’s page (Municipality monograph) and a village record have a “🏞 Postcards” block.
0dl60ql: How do I say where an old photo or a postcard was taken, when I am not sure?

Open the image (viewer) → “📍 Where was it taken?”, or Lists → “📍 Images of places” → “＋ Add an image”. Add one or more hypotheses: a place in your database (picker), a precise point on the map, or an area (◯ circle or ⬠ polygon) if you only know the neighbourhood; the street and the address; the direction of the view (🧭, a cone on the map); the certainty (certain, probable, possible, to check) and why (shop sign, bell tower, caption, publisher…). The ★ hypothesis chosen becomes the image’s place everywhere in the app. Also note the date the picture was taken (“about 1905”) and the publisher or photographer.
0zaftpn: How do I compare an old postcard with the same place today?

In “📍 Where was it taken?” → “🪟 Compare with today”: choose or import a current photo taken from the same spot. The comparer opens as a curtain (drag the line in the middle of the image) or as a cross-fade. “📌 Place 2 markers per photo” (the top of the bell tower, the corner of a roof) aligns today’s photo with the old one; “Adjust by hand” rotates and enlarges it, and “Drag moves photo B”. “💾 Save” keeps the comparison.
0wzovd3: How do I ask for help to locate an old photo?

In “📍 Where was it taken?” → “🙋 Ask for help”: the app prepares the text (what can be seen, your leads with their certainty, your questions), to copy onto a forum, Geneanet’s mutual help, a Facebook group (the request is stored in Lists → 🤝 Help requests), or a small ad (stored in ✉️ Small ads). “⤓ Download the image” to attach it. When someone answers, “📨 Note an answer”: their lead becomes a new hypothesis, with their name (↶ Undo possible). Nothing is sent by the app.
0jkbnuu: Where can I see the old images of a street or a village?

A village record and a municipality monograph have an “🖼 Images of the place” block: the images arranged by street, then by period, with the map (areas and directions of view). Lists → “📍 Images of places” also sorts them “By street” or “By period”, with the filters Place, Street, Period, Certainty, Kind, No place. On the Map, the “📍 Images of places” button shows them at their location.
11cpexx: How do I note my appointments and family birthdays?

Lists → My diary: fairs, archive visits, reminders, letters, tours, by day, by week, by month… Lists → Family calendar: the events of the records by day, by month or by year, with an “anniversaries” mode and the date in other calendars (Julian, Republican…).
1686may: How do I make a map with my photos and videos?

Lists → “Photo maps” → “＋ New map” (or Maps → “📸 Photo maps” mode: at the top, one badge per map to go from one to another, “🗺 All my maps” and “＋ New map”; the ⚙️ button next to them chooses which ones get a badge: the most recent, the oldest (with their number) or those you pick by hand; the others are in “🔍 N other maps…”, which opens the search). Add photos from the app (“＋ Photos from the app”) or drag files into the “📁 Drag…” area: they go into the media, and those with GPS coordinates (JPEG, HEIC, PNG, WebP photos, MP4 and MOV phone videos) place themselves. The others go into “To place”: drag their thumbnail onto the map, or 📍 to choose a place from your database.
11m6d9w: A photo is in the wrong place on my photo map, how do I fix it?

Drag its thumbnail to the right place: “↶ Undo” appears at the bottom left. The original GPS position is kept: ✎ (or right-click the thumbnail) → “↺ Back to GPS”. Several photos in the same place form a cluster with their number: click it (or zoom) to separate them.
0uycc3r: How do I see my photos over time on the map?

Under the map, the timeline shows how many photos there are per period (wheel to zoom: from centuries down to minutes; double-click to see everything). Drag on the timeline to choose a period. “▶ Play” fills the map over time; ⏮ ⏭ step forward. The step is typed freely: “3 d”, “1 month 12 d 3 h”, “2 years 6 months”, “90 min” (or the quick choices 1 h, 1 d, 1 wk, 1 month, 1 year, 10 years); the window is cumulative (everything before stays) or sliding. The exact time of a photo (read from the file, or written “7 May 1925 at 14:30”) is the local time it was taken; a date without a time is placed at noon.
0qnpqwi: Can I combine all my photo maps?

Yes: “🗺 All my maps” (in Lists → Photo maps, or in Maps). Each map has its colour; the legend on the right lets you tick and untick the maps, with the same filters (📷 Photos / 🎬 Videos, period, timeline). The “📸 Photo map” widget can also go on the dashboard, in your tabs and in a note.
09rsw5f: How do I put the record of a specific village in a widget or a tab?

Widget editor (kind “App screen”) or Tab editor: “Village record…” or “Municipality monograph…” screen, then the commune. Tick the parts to show and arrange them (⠿ or ↑ ↓): this organisation only applies there, the village record in Lists keeps its own.
1q3r02b: A place is in the wrong spot on the map, what should I do?

Settings → ✅ Database check, “📍 Places” badge: the app spots unlikely coordinates (0, 0, outside the country, latitude and longitude swapped, namesake in another department), shows the map above the list and offers “✎ Fix” in one click (with “↶ Undo”).
0r4muuv: How do I choose an icon or a base map when there are lots of choices?

Click “✎ Change” next to the icon (or the background): a grid opens. Type a word in the 🔍 box (“church”, “boat”, “heart”, “Cassini”…), or click a section at the top; your recent icons come first. The keyboard arrows move around the grid, Enter chooses, Esc closes. For base maps, each thumbnail shows a piece of the background. The “×” of the badge removes the icon when you can do without it. It is the same grid everywhere: event types, base maps, icons of sections, tabs, widgets, the big buttons of simple mode, notes…
049rvkl: How do I find a setting in a long Settings page?

The long Settings pages (Keyboard shortcuts, Event types, Appearance, Glossary…) have a 🔍 box just under the title, which stays at the top when you scroll. Type a word (“sosa”, “print”) or a key (“ctrl p”): only the lines that contain it stay, the letters found are highlighted, the frames without a result fold up into a grey line. “/” puts the cursor in the box, Esc or × empties it, “Show all” brings everything back. Nothing found? “🔍 Search all Settings” takes the word to the box in the left column.
0vcqnhf: How do I change the base map?
Map → map settings: Cassini, État-Major, IGN, satellite, old cadastre… A village record also has its own choice.
1lf6tw0: How long did it take to go from one village to another in the old days?

Map → “🧭 Tools ▾” → “Distances and travel times”: choose the start and the destination (or a person, to follow their movements) and the year. You see the distance and the duration on foot, on horseback, by stagecoach, by boat and by train, with a sentence like “It took about 4 days to go from Tulle to Paris in 1820”. The speeds come from historians (Braudel, Arbellot, Studeny, Caron…): the sources are in “⚙️ Speeds and sources”, where you can also change them. On the record, the “🧭 Their journeys” block appears as soon as the person lived in two places placed on the map.
1oxl6pz: How do I print a large family map (A3, A2, A1, A0)?

Map → “🧭 Tools ▾” → “Large map to print”: format A3 to A0, portrait or landscape, 5 styles (old, État-Major, modern, black and white, midnight blue and gold), cartouche (title, family, dates), legend, compass rose, scale, places of birth, marriage and death, migrations, a single branch, portraits in medallions. “⤓ Export…” gives a PDF, a PNG, a JPG or an SVG; “🖨 Print” opens the print window. Living people and confidential records are never on it. The background is drawn by the app (Natural Earth, IGN), without Internet tiles: their terms of use forbid downloading them in bulk for printing, and a drawing stays sharp at every size.
113xw6s: How do I see the relief around the family villages in 3D?

Map → “🧭 Tools ▾” → “3D relief”: choose the centre place and the radius, set the exaggeration of the relief; the family’s places are pins. Drag to rotate, wheel to zoom; with the keyboard ← → ↑ ↓, + and −, 0 to go back. The altitudes come from the relief map supplied with Weather of the past (14 European countries): elsewhere, the app tells you there is no altitude for this area.
14ymq94: How do I draw my own areas, paths and notes on the map?

Map → “✏️ My layers”: create a layer, then 📍 Point, 📝 Note, 〰 Route or ⬠ Area and click on the map (Enter or double-click to finish, Esc to stop). Each layer has its colour, can be shown or hidden, and its ⋯ offers Rename, Frame, ⤓ Export as GeoJSON or KML, Delete (with “↶ Undo”). “⤒ Import…” takes a GeoJSON or KML file (Google Earth, uMap…). Click a shape to edit or delete it.
089g6yr: How do I make a custom map (certain data, between two dates, for certain people)?

Map → “🗺 My maps” → “＋ New map”: give it a name, tick the first layers. In “⚙️ Layers”, add what you want to see (births, marriages, deaths, burials, residences, censuses, migrations and journeys, a person’s places of life, surnames, occupations, houses, images of places, war memorials, sources, placed media, tracked animals, historical events, your drawn or imported layers) and open each layer to filter it: between two dates, one or more people with their ancestors or descendants over N generations, Sosa, father’s or mother’s side, branch, labels, around a place or within a drawn area, certainty, kinds of events. Each layer has its style (colour, shape, size, clustering, heat map, place names). Everything is kept straight away, with “↶ Undo”. A “🖼 Images of places” map is ready from the start.
1mw281f: How do I run time on one of my maps, and share it?

At the top of one of my maps: ▶ runs through the years (everything up to the year, or a window of N years: ⚙️ Layers → “Time”), the slider chooses a year, “All” brings back all the years. “⤓ Export ▾”: image or PDF, GeoJSON, KML; 🖨 prints it; “⋯” puts it on the dashboard, in a layout book or tells you where to find it in My website (“🗺 One of my maps” block). What leaves the app never shows a living person or a confidential record. “💾 Share the definition” gives a file with the settings only (layers, filters, styles), never the data.
01oal58: How do I find my ancestors in the 1836 to 1936 censuses (SocFace)?

The SocFace project used artificial intelligence to read the nominal lists of the 1836 to 1936 censuses; they are in FranceArchives’ “name database – censuses”, department by department. On a person’s record (Censuses block), in Research → “🧾 SocFace censuses” or in “Search the Internet” → “🔍 Online archives…”: the common window opens on the FranceArchives line, with “Also: 🧾 Censuses 1836-1936 (SocFace)” and the census years. The surname, first name, commune and years (between birth and death) are filled in; the search opens on FranceArchives in your browser. The app never connects to that site: only the address you see is opened. “What’s missing?” also suggests one line per census (“1906 census in Tulle”) with the link ready and “✓ Found / Not found”, noted in the Research log.
1aj0gcd: How do I import a census found on FranceArchives (SocFace)?

On FranceArchives, “Download the entry as CSV” (one person) or “Export the results” (a search); you can also copy the whole text of an entry (with “See the other members of the household”) and use “📋 Paste the text of an entry”. Then “⤒ Import SocFace censuses”: “Here is what will come in” shows each household, and for each person “Is this the same person?” with the close records from your database. Nothing is linked without your choice, nothing is replaced in your records, a household already imported does not come in twice.
