Each census gets its source (link to the entry and to the image, with the note “Automatic SocFace transcription — may contain errors: check on the image”) and the “TO CHECK” badge until you tick “Checked on the image”. “↶ Undo” removes the whole import. The FranceArchives CSV does not say who lives with whom: people with the same surname, commune and year are put together (untick those who do not belong); the text copied from an entry gives the real household.
19epxh7: Why does the app tell me “SocFace reads born about 1922, your record says 1921”?

After the import, what SocFace reads (year and place of birth, sex, relationship to the head of household) is compared with your linked records. The differences appear on the record, in the import preview and in Settings → Data quality → “✅ Database check” (kind “🧾 SocFace census”, 🟡 curious or 🟠 to check, never 🔴: the machine can be wrong, and ages declared at censuses were often approximate). The tolerated difference on the year is set in “⚙️ Check thresholds”. Look at the image: if your record is right, “This is not a mistake”.
1469x93: What mistakes can automatic reading make (SocFace, ✨ Read the record)?

A machine reading handwriting always makes the same kinds of mistakes. Letters that look alike: u and n (“Lavand” for “Lavaud”), m and rn or nn, a and o, e and c (“Jcan” for “Jean”), i, l and t, the long s ſ and f, v and r, cl and d, h and b, and old capitals S/L, I/J, T/F. Digits: 1 and 7, 3 and 8, 5 and 6, 0, 6 and 9, 4 and 9 — hence a son older than his father, a mother aged 8, a birth after the census. Shifted columns: an occupation in the first-name box, a commune in the surname box, an empty or absurd relationship (“son” for a woman, two “heads” in one household), a household cut in two at a page break. Abbreviations not expanded: “cult.” (farmer), “jlier” (day labourer), “dom.” (servant), “Vve” (widow), “id.” or “d°” (ditto: the same as on the line above). “🔍 Check this SocFace line” shows each box read, why it is suspicious (🟡 curious, 🟠 to check), one or more suggestions (“Lavaud?”) drawn from your records, the household, first names and communes, and the link to the image: nothing is corrected without your click, and “↶ Undo” goes back. The proofreading of “✨ Read the record” spots abbreviations and names close to those in your database in the same way.
0hs34bn: Where do I search for an ancestor in online archives? (one window for all the sites)

On their record, “Search the Internet” block → “🔍 Online archives…” (or a button in a block: Poilu, Military, Departures, Child in care, In the media, Awards, the record of a place, an employer, an object…). A single window brings together all the sites (Mémoire des hommes, Gallica, Archives nationales, FamilySearch, European archives, libraries…), one line per site, arranged by country then by theme: the badges say how many there are (“🇫🇷 France (69)”, “🎖 Soldiers and wars (15)”), the 🔍 box finds a site, “Free only” hides the paying ones, “For:” changes the person. A block button opens the window directly on its section (🎯 badge); “All” shows the rest. Each address is written as it will open in your browser; the app never connects to these sites. Then “⤒ Import what you found ▾” (or the small ⤒ on the line) opens the import that goes with that site, and “🔗 Paste a link” recognises the site of a pasted link and opens the right import.
16hsxun: How do I find a soldier “Mort pour la France” on Mémoire des hommes?

On his record, “Poilu 14-18” block (or “Search the Internet”) → “🔍 Mémoire des hommes”: the “Search the online archives” window prepares the search with his surname and first name for each database (Morts pour la France 1914-1918 and 1939-1945, war graves, deceased soldiers, sailors, his unit’s war diary) and opens it in your browser; the app never connects to the site. Then save the record found (image or PDF) or copy its link, and “⤒ Import what you found”: the document is stored in the media and linked to the record, a source is created with the link, and the app suggests the death “Mort pour la France”, the “Mort pour la France” box and his unit in the Poilu block — only if the record does not already have them (nothing is replaced, “↶ Undo” removes everything). What you read on these sites needs checking (namesakes).
1nmalbk: How do I find a Legion of Honour file (Léonore database)?

On their record, “🏆 Competitions and awards” block → “🔍 Léonore”: the search opens in your browser with their surname and first name (the Archives nationales’ Léonore database has the files of members who died before 1977). Download the pages of the file (image or PDF), then “⤒ Import…”: copy the rank, the date of appointment, the decree and the file number (reference) alongside; a “🎖 Decoration” award is added to the block, with the document and a source that keeps the link. To check on the file.
196ljs8: Where do I find an ancestor’s military register, and what is his class?

On his record, “Military” or “Poilu 14-18” block → “📋 Military register”: the app calculates his class (the year he turned 20: born in 1892 → class of 1912) and the department where he lived at 20, then opens the website of that department’s Archives (list of departmental Archives in the app) or FranceArchives’ name database. The registers are arranged by class then by recruitment office. Then import the page (image): you copy alongside the number, the class, the office, the description (hair, eyes, height, education), the campaigns, the wounds and the successive addresses; only the empty boxes of the Military block are filled in.
16l4dv8: How do I find a naturalisation decree, a notarial deed, a sailor, a deportee or the description of a church?

On their record, “Search the Internet” block → “🔍 Online archives…” (also in the Military, Departures, Probate inventory, Resistance blocks, on a place’s monograph, a house or a family object): Archives nationales (naturalisations 1883-1930, Minutier central), overseas archives (colonies, convicts), Service historique de la Défense (registered seamen, officers), Mémorial de la Shoah, Livre-Mémorial of deportees, Maitron of those shot, Journal officiel, old directories, Mérimée and Palissy, Belgium, Switzerland, Ellis Island (free account). The search opens in your browser with the fields filled in: the app never connects to these sites. Save the document, then “⤒ Import what you found”: it goes into the media with its source, and the app suggests what it says (naturalisation, marriage contract, inventory, departure, deportation…) after “is this the same person?”. Nothing is replaced, everything stays “To check”, and “↶ Undo” removes everything. A person who was deported or shot no longer appears in the games.
1w0hixj: How do I search for an ancestor in old newspapers (Gallica, RetroNews, Europeana)?

On their record, “📰 In the media” block → “🔍 Old press”: the full-text search opens in your browser with their name, the place and the period. Gallica (BnF) is free; RetroNews is partly paying (some newspapers and full reading require a subscription); Europeana brings together newspapers from all over Europe. To keep an article: image, PDF, screenshot or saved page, or “🔗 Paste a link” (the newspaper, the date and the page are filled in when the address gives them) → an “📰 In the media” entry with the newspaper, the date, the page, the link and the copied text. If a site changes its address: “⚙️ Site addresses”.
1o0259r: How do I find an ancestor on a war memorial (MémorialGenWeb, 1870, civilian victims)?

On their record, “Poilu 14-18” block: “🗿 War memorial (MémorialGenWeb)”; or “Search the Internet” → “🔍 Online archives…”, “Wars and memorials” section. You will also find the dead of the 1870-1871 war and the civilian victims of 1939-1945 there. The search opens in your browser (the app never connects to these sites). Then “⤒ Import the record…”: the photo of the memorial or the saved page goes into the media, a source is created with the link, the death and the unit are suggested (only if they are missing), everything stays “To check” and “↶ Undo” removes everything. In a municipality monograph, “🗿 War memorial” opens its memorial. The addresses of these sites could not be checked: if one no longer works, change it in “⚙️ Site addresses”.
0qk14q6: How do I find an ancestor’s grave and keep its photo?

On their record, “Cemetery” block: “🔍 Search for the grave” opens Cimetières de France, BillionGraves (with the GPS position) or Geneanet’s grave surveys in your browser, with the name and years filled in. Save the photo, then “⤒ Import a grave photo…”: it goes into the media and into the burial’s “Dated photos”; if the record does not have a burial yet, the app offers to create it (cemetery, commune, plot, GPS) and the interment if it is missing. Nothing is replaced; “↶ Undo” removes everything.
150q36q: How do I find a village’s population since 1793 and its old names (Cassini, EHESS)?

Charts → Municipality monograph → “🏘 Population since 1793 and old names”. “↗ Open the commune on the EHESS site” (“Des villages de Cassini aux communes d’aujourd’hui”) opens your browser; save the page or copy the table, then “⤒ Import the table…”, or “✎ Copy by hand” (“1793: 512”, one year per line; “✓ Understood: …” below). A year already noted is never replaced; “↶ Undo” removes the import. The old names are matched with INSEE’s changes since 1943 (old borders supplied with the app). The monograph then shows the population curve.
0zg0jrq: Where did my surname live between 1891 and 1990 (Géopatronyme)?

In “Search the Internet” (record): “Géopatronyme”; or in Charts → Surname map: choose a name, then “🔤 This name on Géopatronyme (1891-1990) ↗”. The map of births by department opens in your browser; the app does not connect to it.
1e5kj8b: How do I search the registers of Europe (Matricula, Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Ireland, Bohemia, Hungary, JewishGen) and among Huguenots or seafarers?

On the record, “Search the Internet” → “🔍 Online archives…”, “Europe · Registers and archives” section (Matricula is searched by place: the parish) or “Protestants and seafarers” (Huguenot refugees, merchant navy crew lists). Everything is free; JewishGen requires creating a free account. Then “⤒ Import what you found”: the image of the record or the saved page goes into the media, a source is created with the link and the page, and the record is suggested (baptism, burial, census, emigration…; never a second baptism or death). Pasted links from Matricula, Digitalarkivet, Riksarkivet or irishgenealogy.ie are recognised (register, page).
0vyhh0d: How do I import an article from a foreign newspaper (Chronicling America, Trove, Papers Past, Delpher)?

On their record, “📰 In the media” block: “🌍 Foreign press” opens the search in your browser (name and years filled in). Then “⤒ Import (foreign)…”: as for Gallica, the article becomes an “In the media” entry with its source and its link; the date and the page are read from the link when it gives them (Chronicling America, Papers Past). “↶ Undo” removes everything.
1647ugc: How do I find a prisoner of the Great War (Red Cross, ICRC)?

On their record, “Military” or “Poilu 14-18” block: “🌍 Prisoners 14-18, Arolsen…” (or “Search the Internet” → “🔍 Online archives…”). The ICRC site (grandeguerre.icrc.org) does not keep the name in its address: “📋 Copy the name and open” puts “SURNAME First name” on the clipboard and opens its search page; paste it into the box. Then copy the text of their entry or save the image, then “⤒ Import…”: the ICRC entry goes into the media, a source is created with the link, the “Prisoner of war” event (date and place of capture, camp) and their unit in the Poilu block are suggested. Nothing is replaced; “↶ Undo” removes everything. The app never connects to the site.
1rbjoup: How do I find out whether an ancestor was a deputy, a senator, an inventor, a doctor or a Polytechnique graduate?

“Search the Internet” → “🔍 Online archives…”, or the buttons in the “🔬 Science, inventions”, “🎓 Diplomas and education” and “🧩 This person was…” blocks: Sycomore (former deputies), former senators, invention patents 1791-1902 (INPI), medical theses (Sudoc, BIU Santé), registers of the École polytechnique, directory of learned societies (CTHS). When importing a copied entry: a patent becomes a 💡 invention with its patent (the “Inventor” profile is ticked), a thesis or Polytechnique a 🎓 diploma, a term of office a 🏛 mandate (political profile). Everything stays “To check” and can be undone with “↶ Undo”.
1quf0i5: Where do I search in Paris, in museums and in local history books?

Village record: “🌍 Books and archives on this place…” opens Internet Archive and Persée on the name of the place (local history books and journals), and, for Paris, the reconstructed civil registers (before 1860) and the electoral lists (1860-1932) of the Archives de Paris. The Joconde database (museums of France) searches for an artist by name. For a book or article found, “⤒ Import…” stores it as a source with its link.
1njwef0: How do I search for an ancestor in Italy, Spain, Portugal, the Netherlands, Flanders or Poland?

“🔍 Online archives…” (record, “Departures / emigration” block or village record): Antenati (search by name, in addition to the search sweeps’ link), PARES (Spain), Torre do Tombo (Portugal), Open Archives (Netherlands, Flanders), Geneteka (Poland). Open Archives publishes its data: “⤓ the results as JSON” opens in your browser; save the file then “⤒ Import…”: each line (baptism, death…) becomes an event if you tick it; a marriage stays written in the source, for you to place in the family yourself.
184cgbi: How do I search in England (FreeBMD, FreeCEN), Canada or the United States?

“🔍 Online archives…”: FreeBMD (births, marriages, deaths since 1837) and FreeCEN (censuses 1841-1911) are searched with a form: the name is copied, paste it into the box. Then copy the FreeBMD results page and “🔗 Paste a link”: each line read (quarter, district, volume, page) can be ticked to become an event. In Canada: BAnQ and Library and Archives Canada; in the United States: NARA and Find a Grave (the text copied from a grave suggests the burial, the cemetery and the memorial number).
1jz0ifs: How do I search the archives of Nazi persecution (Arolsen) and among the Righteous Among the Nations?

“🔍 Online archives…”, “Memory of the Shoah and of persecution” section: Arolsen Archives (documents from the camps and displacements) and Yad Vashem (Righteous Among the Nations). An imported Arolsen document stays sober on the record, and that record is never used in a game (like those of deportees). A Righteous Among the Nations becomes an award in “🏆 Competitions and awards”.
1uz2md5: Where are the addresses of the online archive sites? (an address no longer works, hide a site, add my own)

A single screen for all the sites: in the “🔍 Search the online archives” window, at the bottom left, “⚙️ Site addresses”. The sites are arranged by country then by theme, in sections that fold up; the 🔍 box finds a site. Write the new address with {nom}, {prénom}, {lieu}, {de}, {à}, {département}… in place of what is being searched; the switch shows or hides the site; “📒 My genealogy society” gives the address of your society for each department; “⭐ My sites” adds your own (it is also in “Search the Internet”). Everything is kept straight away (“↶ Undo”, “↺ Reset to default”), and the settings made before in each window are carried over. “Free only” (ticked at first) hides the paying sites. The badge says whether the app’s address has been checked, partly checked or not yet.
1ffqg4j: How do I search FamilySearch and WikiTree from a record?

“Search the Internet” block of the record → “🔍 Online archives…”: FamilySearch’s indexed records (surname, first name, place and years of birth filled in), its catalogue (which registers of a commune have been filmed) and WikiTree. FamilySearch requires a free account to see the results and the images. If the record has a FamilySearch identifier, its entry in the tree opens directly. The app never queries these sites: only the address is opened in your browser. Then “⤒ Import what you found” (or “🔗 Paste a link”): the source with the link, the missing events, and the FamilySearch identifier if there was none. A whole FamilySearch or WikiTree tree is imported as GEDCOM (Home → Import).
0vho43k: How do I find an ancestor who left for Quebec or Acadia?

“Departures / emigration” block of the record → “🌍 Quebec, Castle Garden…”: the Fichier Origine (the French who settled in Quebec from 1600 to 1865: baptism in France, parents, marriage in Canada) and the Centre d’études acadiennes in Moncton. Copy the entry found and use “⤒ Import…”: the baptism is added if it is missing, and a departure for New France goes into “Departures / emigration”, with the entry number. Nothing is replaced, everything stays “To check”, “↶ Undo” removes everything.
0q4ckgf: How do I find an ancestor who arrived in New York (Castle Garden)?

“Departures / emigration” block → “🌍 Quebec, Castle Garden…” → Castle Garden (arrivals from 1820 to 1892, before Ellis Island). Copy the passenger’s line (ship, port of departure, arrival date, age, occupation) and “⤒ Import…”: a journey is added to the “Departures / emigration” block, and a birth “about …” based on their age if the record has none.
19vgthx: Did my ancestor receive the Saint Helena Medal?

The soldiers of the Revolution and the Empire (1792-1815) still alive in 1857 received it: about 400,000 names. “Military” or “🏆 Competitions and awards” block → “🌍 Saint Helena medallists…” (offered if the person was born before 1810). “⤒ Import…” adds the medal to “🏆 Competitions and awards”, their birth if it is missing and their 1857 address.
0i00b0c: How do I find an ancestor in a factory’s staff registers (Archives du monde du travail)?

Lists → Employers → the employer’s record → “🏭 Staff registers (ANMT)…”: the Archives nationales du monde du travail in Roubaix keep the archives of many companies, searched by name. “⤒ Import…” (kind “Staff register”) adds to the record an occupation “Employer: …” (the person then appears in “The family at this employer”) and a line in the employer’s timeline.
1j49gj2: Where do I search for a railway worker, a gendarme or a police officer who died on duty?

“Search the Internet” → “🔍 Online archives…”, “France — soldiers, railway workers, gendarmes, police officers” section. The exact addresses of these memorials could not be checked: the app launches a Google search of the name with the occupation; if you know the address of the memorial, write it in “⚙️ Site addresses”. On import, the death “Died on duty” is only suggested if the record does not already have a death.
1vclvtz: How do I find a record of a French person born, married or who died abroad (consular civil registration)?

The registers of consulates and embassies are at the Archives diplomatiques in Nantes; they cannot be searched by name online. “🔍 Online archives…” → “Archives diplomatiques de Nantes” opens a FranceArchives search and copies the name for a request. The record received is imported as a “Record”.
1tnwcgj: Where do I find the history of a village or a department (Geneawiki)?

On a commune’s monograph (Charts) and on a village record: the “📖 Geneawiki: …” buttons open the page of the commune and that of the department on Geneawiki (online registers, archives, history, transcriptions).
168ju70: How do I search for a Soviet soldier or a victim of repression in the USSR?

“🔍 Online archives…”, “Russia and USSR” section: Pamyat Naroda (soldiers of 1941-1945; write the name in Cyrillic for better results) and Memorial (victims of political repression). What comes from Memorial stays sober on the record (“Political repression (USSR)”) and a record that carries it never goes into a game, as for deportees.
1enls12: How do I date a photo using the photographer’s name?

Treasures → “📷 Date an old photo” → “📷 The photographer…”: write the name and town printed on the back of the card, open the Daguerre database, Portrait Sépia or Gallica’s old directories, then paste the line that gives their years of activity (“active from 1862 to 1895”): “Put these years in the photo” adds them to the clues.
0lxckqm: Where do I search for the biography of an activist, a trade unionist or an elected official (Maitron)?

“🔍 Online archives…” → “Maitron”: the whole biographical dictionary of the labour and social movement (not just those who were shot). Copy the entry and “⤒ Import…”: it becomes a note on the record, with the birth and death if they are missing.
06s7xef: How do I find manuscripts or private archives about an ancestor (CCFr, Calames)?

“🔍 Online archives…”, “France — manuscripts and private archives” section: the CCFr (manuscripts and collections of libraries) and Calames (universities). “⤒ Import…” (kind “Archive collection”) creates the source with the reference and the library, and a note if you tick it.
1sgi5fi: How do I search the archives of 30 European countries (Archives Portal Europe)?

“Search the Internet” block of the record → “🔍 Online archives…” → “🇪🇺 Europe” section: the search opens in your browser, with the name and the place already written. The portal searches the inventories of the archives of 30 countries: it tells you in which collection and under which reference a register is. The app never connects to the site. Then “⤒ Import what you found” stores the document, creates the source and suggests the record (nothing is replaced, “↶ Undo” removes everything).
131i726: How do I find out whether an ancestor was recognised as “Righteous Among the Nations”?

“🔍 Online archives…” → “🇫🇷 France — Righteous and war memorials” section → “Comité français pour Yad Vashem” (the name is copied for the site’s box). If you find their entry, “⤒ Import” adds the distinction to “🏆 Competitions and awards”, soberly, with the file and the note “to check”. A record recognised as “Righteous” no longer appears in the games or in the playable Treasures.
11p44mi: How do I find the file of a foundling or a child in public care (Assistance publique)?

On their record, “👶 Child in care” block → “👶 Search for their file”: Archives de Paris (foundlings and children in care) and, for the other departments, FranceArchives’ inventories. “⤒ Import the file…” stores the image, creates the source and adds a placement (register number, admission, wet nurse) next to those already noted; a placement with the same register number is kept as it is.
06eo8km: How do I keep the photo of a commune’s war memorial (MonumentsMorts, University of Lille)?

Charts → the commune’s monograph → “🌍 European archives, memorial, old cadastre, society…” → “MonumentsMorts” (the commune is copied). Save the photo, then “⤒ Import for this place…”: it is linked to the place (and to a record if you choose one), with its source. From a record’s “Military” block: “🗿 War memorial”.
146s74y: Where do I find the free transcriptions of a department’s genealogy society?

“🔍 Online archives…” → “📒 Genealogy society transcriptions” section. Write the address of your society for each department in “⚙️ Site addresses” → “My genealogy society, by department”: it will open for anyone born in that department. Without an address, the app opens a search “genealogy society + department”, or the directory of the Fédération française de généalogie.
0sd0cjq: How do I find out which registers exist for a village abroad (FamilySearch Wiki, GenWiki, GOV)?

Charts → the place’s monograph → “🧭 How to search here (FamilySearch Wiki)”: the wiki says, for each country and often each parish, which registers exist, where they are and which are online. For Germany and Central Europe, the “🧭 Help searching in a place” section adds GenWiki (one page per village) and GOV (the old names and parishes of a place).
0vbpl03: How do I search for a German ancestor (CompGen, Archion)?

“🔍 Online archives…” → “🇩🇪 Germany” section: the village family books (CompGen, free) and Archion, the registers of Protestant parishes, marked PAYING (subscription). Untick “Free only” to see the paying sites: they always stay at the end.
12ub69r: Where can I see the old cadastre of a village in Bohemia, Moravia or Austria-Hungary?

Place monograph → “🌍 European archives, memorial, old cadastre…” → “🗺 Central Europe”: Archivní mapy (cadastre of 1824-1843, free) and Mapire (maps of the Habsburg empire, partly paying). The name of the place is copied for the site’s box. Save the plan, then “⤒ Import for this place…” → “Cadastre plan”: it is linked to the place with its source.
0s53acr: How do I search Hungarian newspapers (Arcanum ADT)?

“🔍 Online archives…” → “🗺 Central Europe” section → “Arcanum ADT” (PARTLY PAYING: the search is free, reading often requires a subscription). An article found is imported like those from Gallica: it goes into the record’s “📰 In the media”.
1e0s1nh: Can I use Ancestry for free?

Yes, but only in a library: many libraries and departmental Archives offer “Ancestry Library Edition” on their computers. “🔍 Online archives…” → “🏛 In the library” prepares the search (“Free in the library” badge); open it on site. At home, the “Ancestry” button opens the paying version.
0870rts: How do I add my own site to “Search the Internet”, try it and share it?

Settings → Appearance → “Search the Internet” → “My sites”: the site’s name, its search address with {nom}, {prenom}, {lieu}, {annee_naissance}, {annee_deces}, {de}, {a}, {conjoint} or {departement} in place of what is searched for, its section and an icon. “🧪 Try” shows the address filled in with the open record (or an example) and opens it. “💾 Saved settings” keeps your list under a name; ⋯ → Export makes it a file to give away, which is opened with “⤒ Import”.
12dwbp3: Where do I find old books and newspapers about my region (Normannia, Yroise, Rosalis, Numelyo…)?

On a village record (or a commune’s monograph), under the figures: the app suggests the digital library of its region — Numelyo and Lectura Plus (Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes), Rosalis (Toulouse, Occitanie), Mémoire vive (Besançon, Bourgogne-Franche-Comté), Normannia (Normandy), Yroise (Brest, Brittany). “↗” opens the search in your browser with the name of the place; “📚 Other libraries…” shows all the others, arranged by region. From a record: “Search the Internet” → “🔍 Online archives…”. If the site’s page finds nothing, “search this site with Google”. A page found is imported with “⤒ Import…”: it is linked to the place (or the person), with its source “to check”.
03l6xtx: My ancestor wrote a book: how do I find their author record (IdRef, data.bnf.fr)?

On the record of a person who published (a book or a work in their record) or who has an artist, writer, scholar, inventor… profile, the “✍️ IdRef · data.bnf (author)” button appears in “Search the Internet” and in the blocks of their profiles. The author record opens in your browser. Copy its text, or save it (IdRef: “Download” as XML or JSON; data.bnf: “Save as…”), then “⤒ Import…”: the app reads their dates and places of birth and death, shows you “Is this the same person?”, suggests the birth and death only if they are missing (nothing is replaced), and adds the link to their “Online records”. “↶ Undo” removes everything.
0wl30yo: How do I search for a name in transcribed old texts (Wikisource)?

“Search the Internet” → “🔍 Online archives…” → “Wikisource — search in the texts”: the full-text search opens with the name in quotation marks (and the place if you have written it). Wikisource transcribes books, directories, newspapers: a notable ancestor may be mentioned there.
1ovuj8c: My ancestor was a sailor: where are his maritime registration records?

“🔍 Online archives…” → “Seafarers” section: write his home port (Saint-Malo, Fécamp, Sète…). The app says which maritime district the quarter belonged to, which centre of the Service historique de la Défense (Cherbourg, Brest, Lorient, Rochefort, Toulon) keeps its registers, and gives the link to the departmental Archives of the port, where many registers have been transferred. This is an indicative breakdown: check on the site. What you find is imported as “Registered seaman” (Military block).
10wiy5w: How do I read a reference from the Minutier central of Paris notaries (MC/ET/XLVIII/312)?

MC = Minutier central, ET = étude (office), then the number of the office in Roman numerals (XLVIII = 48), then the article (the bundle). “🔍 Online archives…” → “Paris notaries” opens the search at the Archives nationales and the Salle des inventaires virtuelle; a record found is imported as “Notarial deed (Minutier central)”: marriage contract, probate inventory, will.
1ve0ncy: How do I search for a Finnish ancestor in HisKi?

“🔍 Online archives…” → “Finland” → “📋 Copy the name and open”: HisKi opens; choose the parish and paste the name. First names are in Swedish or Finnish there (Johan / Juho, Maria / Maija). Then copy the table of results, then “🔗 Paste a link”: each line becomes a record to tick (baptism → birth and baptism, burial → death and interment). A marriage is never added by itself: it stays in the source.
0m012n9: How do I find a trial in London (Old Bailey, 1674-1913)?

“🔍 Online archives…” → “United Kingdom” → “Old Bailey Online”: the search opens with their name. Copy the text of the trial (or save the page), then “⤒ Import”: the app reads the reference (t17800628-33 = 28 June 1780), the crime, the verdict and the sentence, translated, and suggests an event “Defendant (or Victim, Witness) at the trial” with the source.
0azo9gl: Why don’t Ancestry, MyHeritage, Filae or ScotlandsPeople appear any more?

Because “Free only” is ticked at first: the paying sites are hidden. Untick it (in “Search the Internet”, in the “🔍 Search the online archives” window or in Settings → Appearance → Search the Internet) to see them: they always come at the end, with the “PAYING” badge and a sentence saying what is paid for. Geneanet stays shown: it is free, only its Premium part is paying (“PARTLY PAYING” badge).
08cmu3c: How do I see the addresses of a census on a plan?

Lists → Surveys (“Plan” tab) or a village record: the households are placed from their address, for the year of your choice. Old street names and vanished streets are drawn by hand; favourite base maps are chosen in Settings → Appearance.
002fn48: How do I prepare a field trip?
Lists → Field tours: the stops (town halls, cemeteries, archives), the logistics and the practicalities of each. Lists → Archive visit planner for the references to consult.
0mk29lq: How do I note a cadastral parcel (a plot of land, a meadow, the ancestors’ house)?

Lists → Places and houses → “🗺 Cadastre” → “＋ Add a parcel”. Choose the commune, write the section (“AB”, “B”) and the number as they appear on the deed, the register or the plan, then “🔍 Search”: the outline, the area (in m² and ares) and the number come by themselves. You can also “🗺 Click on the map”. Then link the owners and occupants (with a role and dates: “from 1834 to 1872”), the house from the House tool, deeds of sale or division, an extract from the register, the scanned plan, a source. The parcel appears on the person’s record (“🗺 Owner of…”), the house’s and the village’s.
0ahqxqv: What can be retrieved from the cadastre, and under what licence?

Everything the app fetches is free of rights and free of charge, with no account or key: today’s cadastral plan (DGFiP, published by IGN: “Parcellaire Express”, Licence Ouverte 2.0 — you may reuse it by citing “IGN / DGFiP”) for the outline, the section, the number and the area (IGN’s API Carto, with the Géoplateforme as a backup); the nearest present-day address (Base Adresse Nationale, Licence Ouverte 2.0); sales since 2020 (“Demandes de valeurs foncières”, Etalab, Licence Ouverte 2.0: date, price, kind of land, never a name). It is your computer that asks, with only the commune, the section and the number (or a point on the map): no person’s name is sent. The answers are kept for 30 days. NOT free: the names of today’s owners (land files, restricted) and, often, the images of old plans held by the archives (conditions specific to each department).
0pjb8n3: How do I note who inherited what (will, division, probate inventory)?

Lists → Media and documents → “🏠 Inheritances and estates” → “＋ New deed”. Choose the kind (will, division, probate inventory, gift, sale between heirs, marriage contract with the dowry, estate declaration), the date as on the deed, the notary, the office, the place, the reference and the source; a probate inventory already noted can be linked too. In “The people”: ⭐ the deceased (or the donor), ★ the heirs and beneficiaries, ☆ the others (witnesses, guardian…), each with their role (heir, legatee, usufructuary…). In “The property”: a house (House tool), a parcel (Cadastre), a family object, or land, a sum of money, furniture written by hand, with the value, the share (“one third”, “in usufruct”) and the “To whom” boxes (nothing ticked: to all the heirs). The images of the deed go through the image window. What you note follows the deeds: the app gives no legal advice.
1kked4z: How do I see the chain of owners of a house or a family object?

Open the house (House tool, “🏠 House” tab → “Chain of owners”) or the object (Lists → Family objects → Edit): a timeline arranges, year after year, each deed that passes it on (from whom → to whom, the share, the notary); for an object, the “Transmission” steps noted on the object are mixed in. “＋ New deed for this house” creates the deed with the property already chosen. On a person’s record, the “🏠 What they received / passed on” block (Settings → Appearance → record blocks) sums up their inheritances.
061cyyx: What is the division diagram of an inheritance?

On a deed’s page (Lists → “🏠 Inheritances and estates”), “🔀 Division diagram” draws as a flow who gives what property to whom: by value when each item has a sum in the same currency, otherwise one item = one share (divided equally). “📊 Edit in My diagrams” takes it into the diagram editor to dress it up or export it. Next to a sum in livres, sous or francs, “≈ … € today” gives an order of magnitude (the calculation of the 🪙 Old money converter, which opens with a click on the 🪙 next to the sum), not an exact value.
14a6ry2: How do I see the parcels on the map?

Map → “▦ Parcels” switch: today’s cadastral plan is shown over the background (zoom in close enough), with your parcels in blue (a click opens one). “📍 Parcel here” then a click on the map: the parcel at that spot, which you can add to your list. The “Cadastre parcels (IGN)” background also exists in the list of backgrounds (Overlay mode), and the “▦ Parcels” switch in a village’s address plan.
16glwtv: How do I get the Napoleonic plan (old cadastre) of a commune?

The first cadastre (called “Napoleonic”, around 1810-1850) and its registers are in the departmental archives: the parcel’s page gives the link to the department archives’ website and a search on FranceArchives (links without guarantee: sites change). Many departments show them online; the conditions for reuse vary from one department to another (often: free personal use, publication on request). Download or photograph the section, then on the parcel’s page “＋ Align an old plan”: the image goes into the media, and you click 2 points (or more, which is better: the church, a crossroads, the corner of a house) on the image and then at the same spot on today’s map. The plan is laid on the Map with its transparency (“My old map”), and it is linked to the parcel. The old number is noted in “Old number”.
025tx0y: The parcel in my deed no longer exists in today’s cadastre?

Parcels have often been divided, merged or renumbered (land consolidation). Note the old number (“B 245 (1834)”) and the locality name, without an outline, or look on the map for today’s parcel at the same spot. “↻ Read online again” updates the outline and area of a parcel already noted.
18xbxet: A foreign place is not offered?
The cities of the world are prepared once at first launch (a few minutes). A place that cannot be found can always be typed by hand.
0b1lfqj: How do I make a maze, and look for ancestors in it?

Open the Game, choose “🌀 Maze” in “Game”. Set the shape (square, hexagons, round, heart, tree, France, star), the size, the corridors (long corridors, many dead ends, balanced, all random), the loops, the start and the finish, then the look (line, hedges, stones, parchment, colours of the walls, the floor and the path). The preview follows each setting; “🎲 Another one” changes the seed (the same seed gives the same maze again). In 3, “Things to go and find”: up to 12 ancestors, places, events, houses or photos from your genealogy, in the order you like, from the oldest to the most recent, or “Climb back up your line” (Sosa 16 → 8 → 4 → 2); the exit can stay closed until everything has been collected. Living people and confidential records are never in it.
11cxkgg: How do I play the maze with several people?

In “4 · The players”, add up to 4 players. “Each in turn”: everyone goes through the same maze and the times are compared. “All at once”: a race, with the arrows, W A S D, I J K L and the numeric keypad. You can also drag your piece with the mouse or a finger. Space pauses, H gives a hint (a few yellow dots), “👁 Show the solution” draws the path. At the end: the time, the steps, the stops, and ↗ the record of each ancestor met.
1g04i4i: How do I print a maze for children?

In the game: “🖨 Print” gives the maze on one page, the list of stops, and the solution on a second page. “⤓ Export ▾” saves it as a PNG image or an SVG drawing, with or without the solution. Your favourite settings are kept in “💾 Saved settings” (with four “Ready-made sets”: Easy for children, Big challenge, Looking for the ancestors, Tour of France’s villages).
0u6gjaf: How do I play “Guess Who?” with my ancestors?

Open the Game, choose “🕵️ Ancestors’ Guess Who?” in “Game”. Choose the people (your Sosa ancestors, one generation, a person’s ancestors or the whole genealogy) and the number of portraits. An ancestor is hidden: ask questions (“Is it a woman?”, “Born before 1800?”, “Was she a ploughman?”, “Born in Auch?”, “On your father’s side?”); the portraits that no longer fit are greyed out by themselves. Click a portrait to set it aside yourself. “🎯 I’ll make a guess” when you think you know (a wrong guess counts as 2 questions). With two players, each has their hidden ancestor, drawn at random or chosen in secret by the other. Living people and confidential records are never in the games.
16hf0g7: How do I play Portrait Memory?

Open the Game, choose “🃏 Portrait Memory”. Choose the kind of pairs (portrait ↔ name, person ↔ village of birth, person ↔ occupation, person ↔ year of birth) and the number of pairs (6 to 24). You turn over two cards; a pair found stays visible and the same player plays again. From 1 to 4 players, with the timer and the number of moves. With the keyboard: arrows then Enter or Space.
09k5p1d: How do I play “The right date”?

Open the Game, choose “📅 The right date”. You get a family event (birth, marriage, death… and, if you like, major dates in French history) without its date: drag it onto “⬇ Here” at its place on the timeline, or choose the place with the keyboard (Tab then Enter). Right: the card stays and you score a point; wrong: it moves to its real place and you lose a life. Set the number of cards, the minimum gap between two dates (the bigger it is, the easier) and the lives. “About” dates are marked “≈”; two dates that cannot be told apart go either way.
0gxcr7c: How do I play noughts and crosses with my own rules?

Open the Game, choose “❌ Free-rules noughts and crosses”. Choose the grid (from 3×3 to 30×30), how many in a row to win (3, 4, 5…), whether diagonals count, gravity (the pieces drop, as in “Connect 4”) or a grid that grows when you play at the edge. From 2 to 6 players, each with their symbol (❌ ⭕ ⭐ 🌳 ♥…, a letter or an ancestor’s portrait) and their colour; a player can be the computer (simple or medium). “↻ Play again” starts a new round keeping the evening’s scores; “↶ Undo the last move” to make up for a mistake. Ready-made sets: Classic noughts and crosses, Connect 4, Five in a row, Endless grid. “🧮 Play until the grid is full” option: you don’t stop at the first line, each line scores a point (a line twice as long is worth two), and the most points wins.
11b6i65: How do I make a jigsaw puzzle with a family photo?

Open the Game (games table in the archive room), choose “🧩 Jigsaw” in “Game”. Take the image from your database (“🖼 Choose from the database”), a person’s record photo (“👤 A person’s photo”), or drag an image from the computer: it goes into the media. Choose the number of pieces (12 to 1000, or “Other…”), the shape (real pieces or squares), rotated pieces if you like (right-click or R to turn them), then “Start”. The pieces snap into the right place and against their neighbour; wheel or pinch to zoom, ⛶ for full screen. The timer runs while you play: Space or ❚❚ to pause (the image blurs); it also stops when you switch tabs. The game is stored in your genealogy database: it saves itself (a few seconds after your last move, on pause and when you leave the screen), “✓ Saved” shows it in the bar, and “💾 Save” (⌘S) does it straight away. Click the name at the top to change it. You find it again in the left column, even on another computer or after restoring a backup, exactly where you were (pieces, groups, time). If the app stops responding, the game is kept in the browser and goes into the database as soon as possible. At the end: your time, your record for this image and this number of pieces, and the history of finished puzzles.
1lfu58c: How do I play patience (solitaire card games)?

Open the Game, choose “🂠 Patience (card games)” in “Game”, then the game among 131 patiences arranged by family (Klondike, FreeCell, Spider, Yukon, Forty Thieves, Castles and gardens, pairing games). Drag a card (or a sequence) onto another pile, or click it then click where to put it; double-click: onto a foundation; click on the stock: draw. In pairing games (Pyramid, Elevens, Thirteens…), click the cards that go together.
10l8vhu: Twenty-three more, with their rules in the game’s “📖 The rules”: Agnes Sorel, White Horse, Four Seasons, Chameleon, Double Canfield, ForeCell, Fan with cells, Mrs Mop, Black Widow, Three Blind Mice, Gypsy, Irmgard, Queenie, Brisbane, Blockade, Good Fortune, Cadet, Martha, Morehead, Montana (the gaps: you arrange each row from 2 to King by sliding cards into the gaps, “🔀 Redeal” twice), Nestor (pairs of the same value), Pairs and All in a row.
0yfu2cx: How do I play cards against the computer (Belote, Tarot, Hearts…)?

Open the Game, choose “🂡 Multiplayer card games” in “Game”, then the game: War, Crazy Eights, Hearts, President, Belote (with 4, you and North against West and East, with declarations), 4-player Tarot (bid, guard, kitty, Excuse, Petit au bout), Rummy (gin, for two) or Crapette (for two). The number of players follows the game; you are the only person at the table, the others are the computer 🤖, each at their level (easy, medium or hard). The rules are in the “?” of the game bar. Click a card in your hand to play it (with the keyboard: ← → then Enter); ↶ undoes your last move (⌘Z), 💡 gives a tip, Esc pauses.
1uj314f: Card games: can the Kings, Queens and Jacks have my ancestors’ faces?

Yes: in “New game”, leave “🖼 Kings, Queens and Jacks with my ancestors’ portraits” and choose the people (your Sosa ancestors, a generation, a branch or the whole genealogy). The Kings and (in Tarot) the Knights are men from the oldest generations, the Queens women, the Jacks younger men; their photo is taken from their record. Never a living person or a confidential record. “🤖 The computer bears ancestors’ names” also gives their names to the computer players.
1evd9bs: Patience: how do I undo a move or get help?

“↶ Undo” (or Ctrl+Z / ⌘Z) undoes moves without limit during the game. “💡 A possible move” shows in yellow a card to play and where to put it. “⬆ Move all up” sends to the foundations everything that can go there; “⟲ Same deal” replays the same cards from the start. Each game keeps your record (time and moves).
007gq3f: ☢ The bunker: where can I see my achievements and my best games?

The bunker is hidden in the archive room (photo lab, three clicks on the red lamp). On its home screen, or in the game (⋯ at the top, and at the end of a game): “🏆 Achievements and records”. About thirty achievements (hold out 30 days, ten inhabitants, no deaths, build everything, a winter without a stove, a birth, fend off 3 raids, all the plans found, ten items made, one per scenario won…), some hidden (“?”) until you earn them. Each achievement earned is announced at the bottom left and keeps its date; a table shows the best games (days held, inhabitants, scenario, difficulty). Everything stays on this computer, never in the database.
09s04p1: ☢ The bunker: how do I play with my ancestors in 1709, 1720, 1870, 1910 or 1940?

In “New game”, choose a scenario from “📜 In history, with your ancestors”: the great winter of 1709 (extreme cold), the plague of Marseille in 1720 (epidemic), the siege of Paris in 1870 (rationing, shells), the great Paris flood of 1910 (flooding), the exodus of 1940 (refugees, scarce petrol). The line below says how many ancestors of your family were alive at that date (born before, died after): they go down into the shelter, those from the region first; if some are missing, invented inhabitants of the period complete the group, and the game says so. Never a living person or a confidential record. The setting follows the period: no electricity in 1709, 1720 and 1870 (candle, fireplace, workshop by hand), the town crier and the gazette instead of the radio, period odds and ends and plans.
18z1qol: ☢ The bunker: can I go back after a mistake?

Yes: every morning at 6 a.m., the game is saved (the last 7 mornings). “⋯ → ⏪ Resume on the morning of day…” (or the button at the end of a lost game) shows the list of mornings with the inhabitants and the supplies; “Resume that morning” asks nothing, and “↶ Undo” in the message at the bottom left brings you back to where you were. An achievement rewards those who hold out 30 days without ever going back.
18jphuj: ☢ The bunker: where do I find the plans for new items?

By searching the town. Each plan comes mostly from certain places (the beehive and the cider press at the farm, the accordion at the church, the fish traps at the harbour, the compass at the library…); the 🛠️ Workshop tab → “❔ To find” says so for each one; “rare” plans are found much less often. About twenty extra items, each with a real effect: well (water without rain), smokehouse, beehive, press, fish traps (food), eiderdowns (less cold), lanterns, clock, accordion, chess, wine cellar (morale), herb garden, grandmother’s medicine chest, stretcher (health), gutters, trap pit, arrow slits, compass, sledge, washtub, dovecote (news without electricity), solar oven and small turbine (not in the old-time scenarios). The places sometimes turn up a notebook of plans in the morning.
0ftppr9: ☢ The bunker: how do I send an expedition into the region?

“🗺️ Region” tab: the map of the surroundings, drawn by the game (other towns — often those in your tree —, villages, farms, abbeys, depots, forests, mines, harbour), linked by roads that are more or less long and dangerous (green safe, yellow, orange, red very dangerous; dashed along the water). Click a known place, then “🧭 Form a convoy…”: who goes, to do what (search, trade, help, attack), which way (the shortest or the safest), the transport, the tools taken and the provisions (“＋ Plan just enough for the road”). The convoy leaves for several days: those who have left do not work at the bunker. You follow the convoy on the map and on the radio (or through the town crier): ambushes, accidents, finds, someone who joins you… It comes back with what it found, plans, wounded, news, new inhabitants, a pack animal — or not at all. “📻 Come back!” makes it turn around.
06hkgbk: ☢ The bunker: who are the other groups of survivors?

In the “🗺️ Region” tab, at the bottom: friendly neighbours, traders and rival gangs, each settled somewhere on the map, with a reputation from −100 to +100 (Enemies, Wary, Neutral, Friendly, Allies). It rises when you share, trade honestly, give (🎁 Give…) or come to help them, and falls when you refuse a request for help, rob a trader (“🦹 Steal” button at the hatch: everyone ends up knowing) or attack them. What it changes: better deals with those who like you, help from your allies when things go badly, and gangs who hold a grudge attack more often and harder (paying them what they ask calms them for two days). The groups also sometimes ask for help: “🤲 Share” or “Refuse”.
0lwgl4n: ☢ The bunker: what are the ruined buildings in the town for?

On the town plan (“🏙️ Town” tab): a farm, a well, a mill, an infirmary, a forge… (with the period name). “🔨 Start the building work” takes the materials, then you have to send inhabitants to work there (“👷 Work 8 h”) until the work is finished. Then the building produces something every day (food, water, medicines, parts…), kept on site for up to three days: go and collect it (“🧺 Go and collect”). A building that is not visited can be looted or damaged (it then has to be repaired); a palisade protects it better.
0wyp2b0: ☢ The bunker: how does an inhabitant learn a trade?

In the “👥 Inhabitants” tab, an expert inhabitant (their trade, or ×1.4 in a skill) or an elderly one (60 and over) has the “🎓 Train an apprentice…” button: choose the skill and the apprentice. Each evening when both are at the bunker, the apprentice progresses (never beyond their master); the log reports it week by week. When the master dies, their knowledge stays with the apprentice (and after two weeks, their notebooks help catch up to their level).
1fn4kfp: ☢ The bunker: can inhabitants become friends, fall out, form a couple?

Yes. Their bond grows by working together, going on a convoy, between master and apprentice; it drops with difficult characters and old quarrels. Friends keep their morale better and work faster when they do the same job; those who can no longer stand each other work more slowly. Two adults who get on very well can form a couple (never two close relatives according to your tree, nor a child); a baby can only be born within a couple. Everything can be seen on the inhabitant’s card (📔 Log → “💞 Their bonds”) and in the game log.
0avv0x3: ☢ The bunker: what are “Memories of the ancestors”?

An option in the game settings (switch in the ⚙️ Settings tab, on at first). When an inhabitant taken from your database finds something linked to their real life — their occupation (a joiner in front of a saw, a midwife at the infirmary), their village (a convoy arriving in the town where they were born), a place on their record (the house where they were born) — they tell a short anecdote drawn from their record: their occupation, their birth, their marriage, their children. In a historical scenario, only what had already happened by that date. It appears in a speech bubble and in the log. Never anything about a living person, a confidential record or one hidden from sharing, and nothing is written in your database.
0sabxdc: ☢ The bunker: how do I bring back more (bags, wheelbarrow, donkey, boat…)?

What you bring back is counted by weight: water, metal and petrol are heavy, cloth, plants and medicines light. On each person’s back, in addition: rucksacks, back basket, trunk with straps. Only one vehicle per outing, the best for the day’s terrain: wheelbarrow (bad in mud), cart, sledge (only on snow), cargo bike, bike trailer, shopping trolley and reinforced pushchair (present day only, on the road), horse-drawn cart (with a horse: the biggest load), boat (only on water: flooded streets in 1910, riverbanks), mine cart (on rails laid towards a nearby place). Pack animals (donkey or mule, horse), found on farms or traded with a group, carry a lot (+5 with pack saddles and straps) but they have to be fed and watered (on expeditions, in the provisions) and they can get hurt. Vehicles wear out: eventually they need repairing, and you need a workbench. 📦 Supplies tab → “🚚 Transport”.
16t5zbh: How do I play battleships or cables?

Open the Game, choose “⚓ Battleships” (against the computer or for two, with ships named after your ancestors) or “🔌 Cables” (turn the cable ends to connect all the stations to the server, with or without wrap-around edges). Games are kept in this browser.
0azw0ya: How do I play chess, draughts, dominoes or Yahtzee?

Open the Game, “＋ New game”, then choose “♟️ Chess”, “⛀ Draughts”, “🁫 Dominoes” or “🎲 Yahtzee” in “Game”. For each player, “Who plays”: a person or the computer (easy, medium or hard). With two people, you play on the same screen (in dominoes, a hand-over screen hides the others’ hands). The pieces, counters or computers can bear your ancestors’ names (never a living person or a confidential record). Games are kept in this browser, nothing is written into your genealogy.
0mm8b1w: Board games: what are the buttons in the bar for?

At the top of the game: who is playing and the scores, the timer, “↶” (⌘Z) which undoes the last move (against the computer, its move too), “💡” (H) which shows a good move (the number says how many are left), “⏸” (Esc) which pauses and hides the board, “?” which explains all the rules, and “⋯” (flip the board, offer a draw, resign). With the keyboard: the arrows to move from square to square, Enter to pick up a piece then put it down. Your record against each computer level is kept with its date.
1whtn8s: Chess and draughts: which rules are followed?

Chess: all the official rules — castling (not allowed if the king is in check or passes through an attacked square), en passant, promotion of your choice (queen, rook, bishop or knight), checkmate, stalemate, draw by threefold repetition, by 50 moves without a capture or pawn move and by insufficient material; optional clock (3 to 30 minutes, with or without seconds added per move) and notation in French (R, D, T, F, C). Draughts: international rules on 10 × 10 (compulsory and majority capture, backward capture, flying kings) or English draughts on 8 × 8. A multi-path capture is played square by square.
0w1y0tx: Yahtzee: how do the score sheet and the bonus work?

Three rolls per turn: touch the dice to keep (they turn blue) before rolling again, then touch a free box in your column (the number of points shows in advance). At the top, the 1s to 6s; if they make 63 points or more, the bonus adds 35 points (“… missing” tells you where you stand). At the bottom: three of a kind, four of a kind, full house (25), small straight (30), large straight (40), Yams (50) and chance. The “American” sheet (Yahtzee) counts three and four of a kind with all 5 dice and gives 100 points for each extra Yahtzee. ↶ undoes the last box filled.
1qy3hl3: Where can I see all my documents (records, letters, photos) as a list of people?

Show the “📄 Documents” tab: Settings → Appearance → menu tabs (it is hidden at first). The list is on the left, from A to Z with the index letters, or arranged in 📁 folders (like “My diagrams” in Charts: drag a document onto a folder, or “📁 File” from its page; each filing can be undone). The page on the right shows the image in large size, the reference, the date, the people, the transcription; “✎ Edit” opens the media viewer. These are the media of your database: nothing to type in again, and hiding the tab does not touch any document.
0h2h24g: How do I see an artist’s catalogue raisonné by albums, by songs or by period?

Show the “🎨 Catalogue raisonné” tab: Settings → Appearance → menu tabs (it is hidden at first). Choose the artist at the top of the column, then “Sort:” — 💽 by albums (the tracks in order, sides A and B), 🎵 by songs (“on 3” shows the albums it appears on), by label, by genre; for a painter 🕰 by period (“⚙️ Periods…”: one per line, e.g. “Blue period 1946-1952”, otherwise by decade), 🖌 by technique, 🏛 by place where it is kept, 🔢 by no.; everywhere by year or A → Z. The sort is remembered for each artist. The record appears on the right; “✎ Edit” opens its catalogue.
0cxdo5a: Where are the Family treasures (letters to descendants, birth sky, gazette…)?

The ✨ Treasures tab is hidden at first: show it in Settings → Menus, column and lists → Menu. There you find letters to descendants sealed until a date, “At your age…”, dating a photo, the birth sky, the candle, the sound atmosphere, the gazette of the year, embroidery, the Happy Families game, the colouring tree, the passports and many more. Their lists are in Lists → ✨ Family treasures, and 13 widgets go on the dashboard.
03sbk4e: Treasures: how do I save, export or print what I have created (colouring, sky, announcement, gazette…)?

All the ✨ Treasures pages are laid out the same way: at the top, “← All treasures”, then the title; on the right the main button (blue), “⤓ Export ▾” and “🖨 Print”. “⤓ Export ▾” brings together the page’s formats (PNG image, SVG drawing, sound file, video…), “📐 Open in the layout” and, at the bottom, “📁 Store a copy in the media”. “🖨 Print” opens the app’s print window (preview, A4 or A5, ⤓ PDF). When the page has a preview, the settings are on the left and the preview on the right (one below the other on a phone).
19msozw: How do I change the look of a family record book?

On the record book: “🎨 Appearance”. Templates (blue record book of 1877, green of 1975, burgundy, old paper, plain), colours, fonts for the titles and the text (“See all the fonts on my computer” adds yours), sizes, layout, frame, and the order of the parts. A box makes it the look of all your record books.
1yyvdjo: How do I put a cover image, labels, or save the look of a family record book?

On the record book: “🎨 Appearance” → “Cover image”: choose one of the record book’s photos (“none” to remove it), as a thumbnail on the cover or as a background; it is also used as the image in the list of record books. “💾 Save this look under a name” keeps it in “My looks”, for all record books (× to delete one). Size of the text and titles: slider or box in px (text 8 to 60, titles 8 to 120). “The parts”: the width of each (1, 1/2, 1/3, 2/3, 1/4, 3/4), like widgets. “🏷 Labels” at the top of the record book adds labels (also in “✎ Edit”).
15dbg90: How do I delete a board, or say it is on hold?

In the board, at the top: the list “In progress / On hold / Finished” and the bin 🗑. In the gallery, the bin appears when hovering over a board. The left column sorts by state; the Workshop has the same filters (and the state is chosen in the project settings).
1y6382q: How do I make a record for a pet?

Lists → “Pets” (or People → Animals) → “＋ New animal”. Its record is the full record, like a person’s: name and kennel name, species, breed, sex, coat, markings, height, weight, birth and death, microchip, tattoo, passport, stud book (LOF, LOOF, SIRE…), registration number, DNA, breeder and kennel name, its owners (records from the family), titles and shows, vaccinations, health tests, vet, weight over time (with a curve), the moments of its life, its character, its story, memories, photos and documents (paper pedigree, health book). The animal appears on its owners’ records (“Pets” block, with “＋ An animal”) and in the dashboard’s “Pets” widget (with birthdays).
01jc0ic: Can an animal have a record like a person?

Yes, and it is now its only record: tree, events, photos, sources, tables, with its own blocks (🐾 Characteristics, 🌳 Pedigree, 🏆 Titles and shows, 🔖 Rings and markings, 👁 Sightings, 🩺 Health, 👥 Group, 🗺 Map / journeys) arranged in sections. Lists → Pets, People → Animals and “＋ New record” → 🐾 An animal all open this same record.
0vlbdcv: Does an animal still have two records?

No. Its record is now a single one, like a person’s, with everything the old animal record showed: characteristics, pedigree, titles, rings, sightings, health, group and map, arranged in sections (or tabs). Nothing is lost: an animal that only had the simple record got its full record by itself at the update (a message says so once in the list of animals), and the old links open the record, on the right section.
1nb9o5l: How do I arrange the blocks of a record in sections (Identity, Family, Life, Documents…)?

Settings → Appearance → Person and animal records → “Record sections”: the style of the titles (Line and title, Framed, Large title, Banner, Centred, or Tabs at the top with the place of the tabs and “▦ See all”), foldable sections (remembered from one record to the next), numbers (1, 2, 3 · I, II, III · A, B, C), block numbers running on or by section, number in brackets in the tabs, empty sections in grey or hidden, sections specific to animals. The drawing (lines, corners, shadows, tabs) follows Designs to choose from, the colour of the banner that of Appearance. Everything is kept straight away.
0jx6hjp: How do I change the order of the sections and blocks of the record?

Settings → Appearance → Person and animal records → “Order and visibility of blocks” (or, on a record, ⋯ → “⚙️ Arrange the sections…”, or the small ⚙️ at the end of the tabs). Drag the ⠿ handle of a section (its blocks follow it) or of a block (within its section, or onto another one: the blue line shows where it lands); with the keyboard: Tab to ⠿ then Alt + ↑ / ↓. A block’s ⋯: Move up, Move down, “Move to ▸”, Width, Hide. A section’s ⋯: Rename (or double-click its name), Change the icon, Duplicate, Folded at first, Move up, Move down, Delete (its blocks go to “No section”, “↶ Undo” puts it back). “＋ New section” at the bottom. “Editor layout: As before · New”, at the top of the page, only changes how this screen is drawn.
1fefake: How do I send a link that opens a record on the right tab?

Copy the page’s address: it gives the record and the open section, for example “#personnes/12/famille”. When it is opened (link, reload, new window), the record opens on that tab; with a style other than “Tabs at the top”, the page scrolls down to the section and unfolds it. The browser’s ← → arrows go from one record to another. A section that no longer exists simply opens the usual tab.
18w8scz: Does the preview in the record settings show a real record?

Yes. Settings → Appearance → Person and animal records → “Preview”: the real record, in small size, with its real blocks (read-only). Choose which one in “Preview with:” (by default the last one opened; with “🐾 Animals”, an animal). It changes straight away when you change a style, the order, a width or a section. “↗ Open this record” opens it for real. Nothing is changed.
12f0y40: I delete an animal’s record: what happens to its tracking?

It goes with it: its record, its animal record, its markings, sightings, health, group and journeys. To restore everything: Settings → Change log → “Restore” on the line of the deletion. In Lists → Pets, ⋯ → “🗑 Delete” does the same. An animal whose record had been deleted before this update asks you when it opens: “↺ Restore it” or “🗑 Delete the animal”.
1wsbopv: How do I arrange a single record differently from the others?

On the record: ⋯ → “⚙️ Arrange the sections…” → “For this record only”. The record shows it with a blue dot “Arrangement specific to this record”; “↺ Use the one for all records again” removes the exception (with “↶ Undo”). In Settings, the “Exception for …” frame does the same thing for the open record.
08ye9cd: Where do I put the “＋ New sighting” button of an animal’s record?

Settings → Appearance → Person and animal records → “Place of “＋ New sighting””: a 👁＋ square first in the grid of buttons (at first, also arranged in “Order and visibility of buttons”), a blue button above the grid, a badge under the name, a quick-actions strip (👁＋ Sighting · 🩺＋ Health · 📍 GPS track · 🔖 Marking), a floating round button, or hidden. The O key opens the window from the record (not in a text box); it can be switched off there, or changed in Keyboard shortcuts.
135ojuk: What does “👁 Last seen” at the top of an animal’s record mean?

The last sighting of the tracked animal: “yesterday, 17:40 · 📍 place · by …” (the full date on hover, a click opens the sighting). The badge is green up to the green threshold (7 days at first), yellow after that, red “Not seen for N days” after the “not seen again” threshold (30 days), grey “Never seen since ringing” with no sighting. It is set in Settings → Appearance → Person and animal records → “Order and visibility of the header items”: place (under the name, with the badges, at the bottom of the header), thresholds, “Show the place and the person” (off: only the badge). The “not seen again” threshold is also that of the “Animals to find” block in Tracking.
1ikwygp: Where has “A person’s record” from Designs to choose from gone?

It is now set in Settings → Appearance → Person and animal records → “Header shape”, just before “Order and visibility of buttons”: the same four cards (current header, photo banner, old record, identity card), the same “Extra settings” and the preview. Your previous choice is kept as it was. Designs to choose from has kept a small line that leads there.
1a2zq7n: Where has the “🎨 Designs to choose from” page gone?

It has been removed: its settings are now where they are used. The General style has become the “Record style” (Settings → Person and animal records, with the header shape) and now only affects the records; the left column has its own lines, corners and shadows (Menus, column and lists → Column); the page background is in Theme and colours (🧩 Page background); Movements in Accessibility → 🎞 Movement. The rest of the app keeps its original style. Your choices are kept.
1ahyw0p: How are words like “born”, “died”… agreed for a person who is neither male nor female?

In French, these words agree with the sex. On records of men and women (and of male or female animals), they agree by themselves. For records with the sex “Other / non-binary” or “Not given”, you choose the spelling in Settings → Theme and colours → “✍️ Word agreement”: as before (at first, nothing changes), feminine (as one says “la personne”), masculine, with a middle dot (“né·e”), in brackets (“né(e)”) or without agreement when a neutral wording exists (“Naissance le 12 mars 1888”, “Décès”). The two kinds of records are set separately, the preview shows the result straight away, and each choice is kept straight away (“↶ Undo” in the message). The setting travels with the 💾 Saved settings and the site default.
1avwkip: How do I change the page background (squares, dots, lined paper, my photo…)?

Settings → Theme and colours → “🧩 Page background”: 9 backgrounds (small squares at first, plain, dots, lined paper, graph paper, paper grain, canvas, gradient, your photo), then the size of the pattern, its intensity, its colour (pale blue, grey, main colour, sepia, your theme’s lines, a colour of your own) and the pages concerned (unticked: plain background). The preview follows straight away. Your photo stays on this computer (not in the database nor in the site default: there, plain background). These come first: Accessibility → High contrast and “One thing at a time” (plain background), and on a record the grain of the “Old paper” style. The background is never printed.
163ekxy: How do I make text bigger (or smaller) throughout the app?

Settings → Theme and colours → “Text size”: from “Very compact (13 px)” to “Very large print (32 px)”. It is the only text size setting: Accessibility → Text points to it (the old “Text size” slider in Accessibility was carried over by itself, to the nearest step). Line spacing, spacing between letters and words and the font stay in Accessibility. Simple mode, if it follows “Same as the app”, also takes this size.
0k22c79: How do I make a genealogy of animals (a breeding)?

Lists → Pets → “Base type”: 👪 Family, 🐾 Breeding or 👪🐾 Both. In Breeding, the left list, the counter at the top and the statistics start from the animals, and new records are animals; the root person (the starting record) can be an animal, and the tree then starts from it. The statistics never mix people and animals.
1vsgte2: How do I get a separate “Animals” tab?

Settings → Appearance → Order of the main menu: tick “Animals” (hidden at first). Then “People” only lists people and “🐾 Animals” only animals, each with its last record opened. Without this tab, in the left list, an “🐾 Animals” frame appears between “People” and “Bookmarks” as soon as there are animals (and “People” disappears if there are only animals).
0sjfp8n: How do I see the animals in the family tree?
Charts → Ancestors, Descendants or Hourglass: tick “🐾 with the animals” (not ticked at first). Each person’s animals are placed under their owner, with a dotted line; a click opens their record.
0gu7o63: How do I arrange an animal’s record (show, hide, move its parts)?

As for a person: Settings → Appearance → Person and animal records → “Order and visibility of blocks”, with “🐾 Animals” chosen at the top of Sections (or, on the record, ⋯ → “⚙️ Arrange the sections…”). Its six starting sections: 🪪 Record, 🔖 Rings and markings, 👁 Sightings, 🩺 Health, 👥 Group, 🗺 Map. The order you had chosen on the old animal record (“⚙️ Organise”) was carried over as it was.
04yn222: How do I arrange the blocks of animals’ full records without touching people’s?

Settings → Appearance → Person and animal records → “Record sections”: choose “🐾 Animals”, then “Order and visibility of blocks”: the order, the width and the blocks shown for all animal records, separately from people’s records. Next to it, “Exception for…” only sets the open record. If the open record is an animal, the “PERSON RECORDS” exception is greyed out (and the other way round for a person).
1gnsuuo: Where do I find an animal created from People or Animals?
Everywhere: it has only one record, whether it is opened from People → Animals, Lists → Pets, the picker, a board, a house or Animal tracking.
01luelw: On an animal’s full record, what does “Identity” show?

What matters for an animal (species, breed, sex, coat, birth, microchip…), never a person’s fields. “Edit” opens the animal’s form. Its other parts (🐾 Characteristics with identification and origins, 🌳 Pedigree, offspring, siblings, owners, 🏆 Titles and shows, 🩺 Health with weight and height, its life, its story, notes, photos, and tracking) are blocks of the record, each with ✎ to go straight to that part of the form. The “Censuses” block (and the other blocks specific to people: maternity, military, voters…) is hidden by default; you can put it back in Settings → Appearance → Person and animal records (“🐾 Animals”).
1x6xcrq: How do I add a species, change their order or hide some?

Lists → Pets → “⚙️ Settings” (or Settings → Animals): tick the species to show, arrange them with ↑ ↓, add your own (its name, and its icon: click it and choose one, animals first) or delete it with 🗑.
0ifb9ml: How do I set up the “New animal” form (order of the parts, fields shown)?

Settings → Animals → “Form”: for all animals, or for one species (“own setting” box): the order of the parts and the order of the fields in each part (↑ ↓ or by dragging ⠿), the parts and all the fields shown (the name and the species always stay). By default, the UELN number only appears for horses.
0kymimk: How do I add my own categories and fields to an animal’s record?

Settings → Animals → Form: “＋ Category” (e.g. 🧬 Genetics, Training) creates a new part of the form; “＋ Field” under a part (the app’s or yours) adds a field: short text, long text, date, number, yes / no box or list of choices (separated by ;). They are arranged and hidden like the others. On the record, an added field is shown in its part; your categories form the “🗂️ My categories” block of the full record. A deleted field keeps what was written in it (it is no longer shown).
02pwqem: How do I keep several ways of setting up animals, or move them to another computer?

Settings → Animals → “💾 Saved settings”: “💾 Save under a name…” gives them a name (e.g. Horse breeding); choose one and “Apply” to go back to it. “⤓ Export” makes a .json file (the settings and all the sets); “⤒ Import” takes it into another database.
0w95ui5: Where do the photos and notes of an animal with a full record go?

In its record, as for a person: its photos and documents (paper pedigree, health book…) in the “Media” block, its notes and sources in the “Notes” block. Those from the old animal record were moved there: nothing is lost.
1xabhte: How do I make the pedigree (the tree) of a pedigree animal?

In the animal’s record, choose its sire and dam if they have a record (otherwise write their name and registration). “🌳 Pedigree” shows 2 to 8 generations (sire’s side at the top, dam’s side at the bottom); an ancestor who appears several times has its own colour. The inbreeding coefficient (Wright’s coefficient, from the known ancestors) and the common ancestors are shown; the pedigree can be printed or downloaded as a spreadsheet. The record also shows the offspring by litter and the siblings (same parents or half). “＋ A young one” creates the record of a young animal with this parent already filled in.
19cwemv: Where do I set the colours, shapes, arrowheads, fonts and menus of boards?

Settings → “Boards”. Colours: the swatches offered for each use (fill, border, text, drawing, notes, board background), in the order you want, with several possible palettes. Arrowheads: those offered and their order, and the default arrowhead at the start and end. Shapes: the order of categories and shapes, those to hide, quick access. Fonts: font lists of your own (with the computer’s fonts). Sizes: from which to which thickness (0.5 to 500 px) and text size (up to 500 px), the default rounding. Spreadsheet: how it looks when placed. Brushes: your own, with their hardness. Menus and options: the order (or hiding) of the tools, the top buttons, the settings on the right and the “Add” menu. At the top of the page, “💾 Save under a name…” keeps all these settings together (like an Appearance design); “My saved settings” → “Apply” to go back to them, 🗑 to delete them.
1hsde7q: How do I set the caption of a line or an arrow?

Choose the line: on the right, write the “Caption”, then “Caption settings”: size, font, bold, italic, text colour, frame (fill, border, border thickness, padding, rounding; “transparent” fill for no frame), position along the line (0 % at the start, 100 % at the end), side (on the line, above, below), distance from the line, and “follow the angle of the line” to tilt it like the line.
1rgf25x: How do I choose and arrange the quick-access shapes?

Settings → Boards → Shapes: ⚡ on a shape adds it to quick access (the shapes offered directly in the bar of the Shapes tool); in “Quick access”, drag a shape or use ‹ › to change the order, × to remove it. Don’t forget “Save”.
07qpvi7: Where do I find the letters, numbers, coats of arms, frames and other shapes for boards?

In a board: Shapes tool (⬠) → “All shapes”. The library has nearly 5,000 shapes: the whole alphabet (A to Z, a to z, accented letters É È À Ç…, digits and numbers, punctuation), each alone, in a circle, in a circle (outline), in a square or in a square (outline); genealogy signs (° birth, † death, ⚭ marriage, ∞, parent → children links, braces); shields and divisions of coats of arms (per pale, per fess, quarterly, chevron, cross…); frames and friezes; labels and ribbons; simplified flags to colour; occupations, tools, animals, buildings, transport, weather, music, sport, emotions… Type a word in the box (without worrying about accents: “eglise”, “flags”, “É”); the filters at the top give the number found per kind (Tab moves from one to the next); ↑ ↓ ← → then Enter to take it. The extra shapes load the first time it is opened (a short moment), not at start-up. A shape placed stays in the board as it is.
0ze0q3g: The “All fonts” window doesn’t show all my fonts: what should I do?

In the app installed on the computer, the full list of fonts is shown directly. In a browser (Chrome, Edge), click “🔓 See all the computer’s fonts”: the browser asks for permission once. If you refused, open the site settings (the padlock to the left of the address) → “Fonts” → Allow, then reopen the window. Safari and Firefox do not give the list: the app shows the common fonts it finds, and you can type the exact name of another font. The fonts appear little by little as you scroll down, each written in its own font.
0um91kr: How do I choose the colour of what I place in a board?

As soon as a tool has colours, the top bar shows the swatches of your palette and, at the end, an “other colour” square to choose one freely: Text (text colour), Note (note fill), Shapes (fill), Line and Arrow (line colour), Drawing. For an arrow, “Arrowheads” gives the arrowheads a separate colour (“=”: like the line). Once the item is placed, everything can be changed on the right, including “Arrowhead colour”.
0ga4b2u: How do I change the order of the Settings pages?

At the bottom of the Settings column, next to “Archive room”: “Reorder”. Drag a line, or use its arrows ↑ ↓, then Save; “↺ Reset to default” puts back the original order. (The order can also be set in Appearance.)
1cg9oci: Where are the glossary and the FAQ?

In Settings, two pages: “Glossary” (genealogy vocabulary, old occupations, help reading records, your personal dictionary) and “FAQ / guide” (quick pointers and these frequently asked questions, with the “Ask your question” search). A button at the top of each page leads to the other.
1lqjdee: How do I underline, strike through, or make a bulleted or numbered list in a board?

Choose the text, note or shape: on the right, B (bold), I (italic), U (underline), S (strikethrough), then align left, centre, right, justify. “Bullets and numbers”: bullet, 1. 2. 3., I. II. III., a. b. c., A. B. C., dash, checkboxes — one line = one item. “Font” offers your font lists; 🖥 adds the computer’s fonts; you can also type a name.
0aihrtr: How do I get more shapes, or create my own?

Shapes tool (S) → “All shapes ▾”: nearly 800 shapes arranged in 23 categories (basic, geometry, arrows, bubbles, stars, symbols, genealogy, people, beliefs and memory, writings and documents, places, house and objects, clothes, occupations and tools, transport, animals, nature, weather, cooking, music games and sport, health…), with a search. “＋ Create a shape”: with the pen (as in Photoshop: click = corner point, click and drag = smooth point with its handles, click on the first point = closed shape, ⌥ / Alt for independent handles, a path inside the shape = a hole), from a drawing in the board or from an image. “🧩 From a shape”: take a shape, flip it (mirror, upside down), rotate it, stretch it, add other shapes to it or cut holes in it, and give it a name (also with ✏️ on the right on a placed shape, or on each shape in Settings → Boards → Shapes). Your shapes go into “My shapes” and into quick access.
0xjx0x8: How do I export, print, import a board?

At the top of the board: “⤓ Export” → PNG or JPG image, PDF, Print…, the selection as PNG, or “Board file” (.lcnda-tableau.json).
